title: Inside The BJP-Akali Dal Reunion: How 6 Years Of Bitter Split Ended
description: Sources from both parties said that as early as April/May, the BJP leadership began consulting with the BJP Punjab unit on whether to re-form an alliance with the Akalis with Punjab polls approaching.
author: Aishvarya Jain, Gurpreet Singh Chhina
content:
Extensive research through surveys, back-channel negotiations and efforts to bring leaders from both parties on the same page were among the factors that shaped the BJP-Akali Dal alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Ultimately, the Akali Dal's organisational network and the BJP's assessment of its electoral winnability proved decisive in sealing the alliance.
Sources from both parties said that as early as April/May, the BJP leadership began consulting with the BJP Punjab unit on whether to re-form an alliance with the Akalis with Punjab polls approaching.
While some Punjab BJP leaders were firmly against re-forming the alliance, others felt that the BJP would benefit electorally from a renewed partnership with the Akalis.
However, the BJP chose not to pre-emptively decide on this and so commissioned research on the current political landscape.
Three Types Of Surveys But One Central Question - Is The BJP Able To Compete In Punjab?
Information was compiled by the BJP through three distinct research methods: a party survey, an independent survey and also a party research function.
One area of concern to the BJP was the lack of its network and winnability in rural Punjab.
Although it has successfully built up its network in urban and semi-urban areas, the BJP - despite employing Sikh leaders and even having Kewal Singh Dhillon as state BJP chief - has struggled to replicate this success in rural regions.
While the Akali Dal has suffered electorally, it has still maintained its strong network and Panthic connection.
Sources noted that, according to the research, the BJP would find it challenging to enhance its rural winnability without a more robust alliance partner. Likewise, the Akalis recognised that the BJP had succeeded in winning over urban and semi-urban electorates and that this could effectively supplement the Akalis' traditional electorate.
Electoral Winnability Proves To Be Important Factor
As the BJP analysed how to re-connect with the Akalis, it was also looking at whether a new alliance would enhance the parties' electorally.
Previously, the BJP contested 23 assembly seats and the Akali Dal 94. But much has changed politically since they split in 2020.
There has been a growing feeling within the BJP that it should endeavour to play a broader role in Punjab, and not just stick to its traditional electorates, the research had also shown that there were constraints to the BJP's ability to contest elections alone.
For the Akali Dal, merging with the BJP would enable them to re-energise themselves. By uniting the BJP's urban network and national leadership with the Akalis' traditional rural and Panthic network, the Akalis can make use of the BJP's political muscle.
Sources from the Akali Dal told NDTV that the party's network, Panthic connection and institutional power continue to be key components of its political powerbase. Of particular importance to the Akalis is the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) which continues to be a key player in the party's traditional Panthic network.
Although newer political parties have tried to encroach on the SAD's traditional domain, so far none has been able to match the SAD's network, sources said.
From July - Developing Network And Secret Negotiations
Following Satish Poonia becoming the BJP's Punjab in-charge, the party also began to intensify its network in the state from July.
Alongside this, secret talks regarding a potential alliance continued to progress.
It was reported that one of the initial stages in the alliance negotiations involved Kewal Singh Dhillon meeting with Akali leader Parvinder Chota. This was one of the first times that the two parties had openly discussed the potential for an alliance.
Intensive cross-party talks then began.
Key BJP figures involved in the alliance talks and analysis were Kewal Singh Dhillon, Ashwani Sharma, Sunil Jakhar and former Punjab Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh.
Approximately four sets of meetings were held at state and central level.
August 7 - Meeting Between SAD Chief Sukhbir Badal And PM Modi
On August 7, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal met PM Modi in parliament. This was a key moment in the alliance process.
While it provided additional impetus to the alliance talks, decisions regarding the alliance were still under review at various levels.
The BJP leadership continued to analyse the political pros and cons of the alliance, a final understanding was subsequently reached, sources said.
The research and talks had increasingly shown that the BJP required enhanced rural and Panthic network connection. Likewise, the Akali Dal recognised that it needed to both bolster and diversify electorally.
After extensive analysis, sources said that a shared understanding was reached and a joint political plan was then drawn up.
Why The Akalis Felt An Alliance Would Benefit Them
The Akalis, sources said, were keen to return to the NDA, they also wished to re-establish themselves politically in a state where they have incurred severe electoral losses.
The Akalis possess a strong network, Panthic connection and rural presence. They recognised that the BJP had also successfully broadened its political acceptance in urban and semi-urban areas.
Accordingly, sources from the SAD said that the alliance would allow the parties to harness their respective strengths and avoid overlapping politically.
The Akalis believe that, thanks to its strong network, the alliance can better establish itself in rural areas where the BJP has been trying to grow its network.
How Differences Will Be Managed - Looking Forward
The alliance has been formally announced, this does not necessarily mean that all political and policy differences have been overcome.
As mentioned, the farm laws were the catalyst for the 24-year-old alliance's collapse in September 2020. The Akalis left the NDA and Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet.
On Tuesday, both parties made it clear at a joint press conference that they are united, with Amit Shah declaring "ab NDA complete ho gaya hai".
Shah underscored that the Akali Dal would continue to be the senior partner, or bada bhai, in the alliance. When asked who would be the chief minister if the alliance comes to power, Amit Shah said, "Jo bada bhai hota hai, wohi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother is the one who becomes the Chief Minister)."
Seat allocation was to be discussed later.
BJP chief Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal will also engage in in-depth talks in the next three months on farmer issues, Punjab's economy and the creation of jobs for the youth. A unified political plan will then be formulated based on these talks, Shah added.
In addition to devising a common political plan, the BJP and Akali Dal are expected to co-operate in drawing up a manifesto, and in campaigning and networking. Plans include a joint yatra, a unified campaign to oppose the AAP government and a chargesheet exposing what the state government is alleged to have done wrong.
Issues such as drug abuse, corruption, farming, jobs, law and order and the state of Punjab's economy are likely to be key themes of the campaign.
A New Political Setup But A Changing Punjab
Both parties now have differing aspirations.
While the BJP is aiming to greatly increase its electoral presence - compared to its previous tally of 23 seats - the Akali Dal wishes to continue as the leading local political partner and to utilise its network to restore its electoral power.
Having officially announced their alliance, both parties now seem to agree that their political strengths are mutually beneficial. Potentially, they run a greater risk by choosing to stand for election in Punjab independently, as opposed to forming an alliance.

title: Murder Accused's Hand Chopped Off With Machete, Then Shot Outside Pune Court
description: The man was released from prison four days ago.
author: Yashpal Sonkamble
content:
A murder accused was attacked with a machete and then allegedly shot at while he was appearing for legal proceedings at a Pune court this afternoon.
A video of the incident showed two men repeatedly hitting the man, identified as Mandar Maruti Kiwale, with a machete outside the Shivajinagar court premises.
The accused then fled on two scooters, while the blood-soaked man was seen trying to get up and walk.
Multiple videos later showed him lying on a footpath with one of his hands chopped off while bystanders stood around watching.
Murder Accused's Hand Chopped Off With Machete, Then Shot Outside Pune Court https://t.co/1iO1McUfsy @ritvick_ab reports https://t.co/DmfrRMUVTI
— NDTV (@ndtv) November 25, 2026
Kiwale, who is reportedly aged 35, has been taken to a hospital, and his condition remains critical.
The police have recovered two pistols and a magazine from the spot.
Mandar Maruti Kiwale Was Involved In 2025 Murder
According to the police, Kiwale was in jail in the murder case of a 26-year-old restaurant owner, Shubham Subhash Chavan, in April 2025, in Pune's Santoshnagar Katraj, over a land and financial dispute.
Chavan was beaten to death with stumps and bamboo sticks by Kiwale and his aides.
Kiwale was later arrested along with the prime accused, Amar Sakore, and his associates, Girish Subhash Babare and Yogesh Babaurao Dore.
Kiwale was released from prison four days ago and was attacked outside the court when he arrived for legal proceedings.
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar has spoken to the Pune Police Commissioner and sought details about the incident.
She has directed the police to track down the accused and take stringent action against them.

title: "I Cracked CAT In Just 15 Mocks": IIM Indore Student Shares Smart Strategies For Exam
description: CAT 2026: MBA aspirants must note that the two-hour CAT exam will be conducted in three sessions.
author: Aakanksha Singh
content:
CAT 2026: With the Common Admission Test (CAT) 2026 scheduled for November 29 and only a few days remaining for the exam, several previous years' top scorers have shared their last-minute strategies online. Tanya Pathak, as the user identifies herself on the social media platform Instagram, claimed that she passed the CAT exam after giving just 15 mocks. Pathak is currently enrolled in the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Indore's Post Graduate Programme (PGP).
Sharing her exam strategy online, the user stated: "I cracked the CAT in just 15 mocks," adding further that "the biggest mistake that CAT aspirants make is that they blindly focus on giving more and more mocks" without also focusing on other methods of study.
Pathak has listed alternate study methods and tricks to help candidates prepare for the CAT 2026 exam.
1. Watching live or online videos of past year questions solving
The student stated that she could see the exact approach of tutors solving the question live and then could adapt that approach in her own CAT preparation. 
2. Solving multiple sectional and topic based mock tests
The IIM Indore student noted that the full mock prepares a candidate mentally for the stamina that they need for the exam, however, the sectional and topic based mock tests make an aspirant understand where they are specifically going wrong so that they can rectify that in their approach at a very early stage. 
3. Maintaining a detailed book of all mistakes and approaches that they should have followed instead 
The Instagram user asserted that the questions are not repeated in the exam, however, the adaptations of those questions are asked in the final test. So if a candidate keeps revisiting this book they can track the strategies that can be taken up across new questions, she said. 
ALSO READ | FMS Delhi Alumna Shares CAT 2026 Section-Wise Strategy, Last-Minute Tips
MBA aspirants must note that the two-hour CAT exam will be conducted in three sessions. While the first session will be held between 8:30 am and 10:30 am, the second will be from 12:30 pm to 2:30 pm, and the third session will be between 4:30 pm and 6:30 pm.

title: Iranian delegation meets MEA officials to discuss multilateral ties
description: NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation
author: Mahima Sharma
content:
During a significant meeting, Alireza Tootonchian led an Iranian delegation in discussions with officials from India's Ministry of External Affairs. (Pic Credit: ANI)
NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation under the framework of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).According to news agency ANI, the Iranian delegation was led by Alireza Tootonchian, director general for multilateral and International economic cooperation. He met Thelma John David, MEA joint secretary (Indo-Pacific), in the national capital. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping.In a post on X, the Iranian embassy in India said that Tootonchian and deputy director general Abolfazl Azizi Panah held discussions with David on multilateral cooperation under the IORA framework.The meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday. Foreign ministers from member countries are expected to attend the gathering to discuss regional cooperation and strategic priorities in the Indian Ocean Region.India is also hosting the 29th IORA Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) meeting ahead of the ministerial gathering. The two-day meeting began on Wednesday.
The council of ministers is IORA's highest decision-making body and comprises foreign ministers of member states. It provides strategic and policy direction to the association, reviews progress in regional cooperation and identifies new areas of collaboration.The committee of senior officials is the organisation's second-highest decision-making body. It comprises senior government representatives who oversee the implementation of ministerial decisions, review recommendations and coordinate IORA's work programmes.Meanwhile, the European union (EU) and IORA held their first high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi on Tuesday. Representatives from several Indian Ocean countries participated in discussions on improving maritime surveillance, tackling piracy and trafficking, and protecting important shipping routes.The European union organised the event with support from its project 'Enhancing the EU's security cooperation in and with Asia and the Indo-Pacific' (ESIWA+) and in coordination with its Delegation to India.Addressing the gathering, EU ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet reaffirmed the bloc's commitment to expanding security and defence cooperation with regional partners. He also stressed the importance of sharing information to tackle maritime threats.Paquet said maritime security was a shared priority for the EU and IORA, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime crime and other challenges at sea.He also highlighted the Indian ocean's importance to global trade, warning that maritime insecurity could disrupt international supply chains and affect economic growth across the region.Representatives from IORA member states and dialogue partners, including India, Australia, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and Saudi Arabia, attended the roundtable.
Participants discussed improving maritime domain awareness, strengthening policy dialogue and expanding cooperation through EU-supported initiatives such as EUCRIMARIO, EnMAR+ and ESIWA+.The discussions also covered the European Union naval force's operation ATALANTA, which works to improve maritime security in the western Indian ocean and red sea. The operation focuses on deterring piracy, protecting vulnerable vessels and monitoring illegal maritime activities.India assumed the IORA chairmanship from Sri Lanka in November 2025 for the 2025-2027 term. Its chairmanship theme is "innovation, openness, resilience and adaptability in the Indian ocean region".

title: Bisleri row: FSSAI launches pan-India water quality checks; results within 1-2 months
description: NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged
author: Karan Manral
content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water, with the results expected to take at least one to two months, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said.The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts to examine various food categories and ensure compliance with prescribed standards."That process has started, and we're doing it across the country. The results will take at least a month or two," Punhani told reporters.He clarified that packaged drinking water was not selected for any specific reason but was part of the regulator's broader surveillance programme."Last year, we took up dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, sugary drinks and other products. So, water is also part of the process," he added.Separately, Punhani stressed the need for food businesses to follow ethical advertising practices, particularly when making claims about their products and promoting them.He emphasised that the regulator was not looking at the issue solely from a legal perspective and urged industry players to consider the ethical dimensions of advertising.
"The idea is not that it's only the legal part of it. It is also the ethical part of it," he said, calling on the industry to focus on responsible advertising practices.
The Bisleri row
Punhani's remarks and the nationwide surveillance exercise come amid regulatory action against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International over a sample collected from its Goa facility.On November 23, the FSSAI granted sanction to prosecute the company after a regulatory sample was initially found non-compliant with the prescribed limits for bromate and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.Following an appeal by the company, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further examination, which also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).However, the FSSAI clarified on Monday that the action was limited to a single sample from one batch, numbered GO 270, collected from the company's plant at Verna Electronic City in South Goa.
Also Read | ‘Only one batch affected’: Bisleri says no stock of Goa-made water under FSSAI scanner in marketThe authority also issued an order prohibiting the sale of the concerned batch under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.Bisleri International subsequently welcomed the clarification, maintaining that the sales prohibition applied only to the specific batch manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.The company stated that it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that no stocks of the particular batch were currently available in the market. It also maintained that retesting found bromate levels below the permissible limit.(With ANI inputs)
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect people’s everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

title: 'Interfering with religious faith': BJP criticises Mehbooba Mufti for opposing road construction near Sheshnag lake
description: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday asked People's Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti not to exploit people's religious sentiments for political
author: Karan Manral
content:
On Monday, Mehbooba Mufti protested against deployment of heavy machinery along Amarnath Yatra route
NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday asked People's Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti not to exploit people's religious sentiments for political gain after she criticised road construction near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath pilgrimage route in Jammu and Kashmir's Anantnag.Jammu and Kashmir BJP chief Sat Sharma said decisions should be based on technical reports and expert assessments rather than political statements.Also Read: Video of bulldozer near sacred Sheshnag lake triggers row in Kashmir - here's what happened"Development based on technical reports should not be politicised, and interference in anyone's religious faith will not be tolerated," Sharma told reporters in Jammu."If a technical report says a building is unsafe or a particular road cannot be constructed, its recommendations must be followed. If work is being carried out in accordance with technical reports, others should not interfere in the process," he added.Referring to the PDP's declining electoral fortunes, Sharma said the party's tally in the Jammu and Kashmir assembly had fallen from 28 seats to three and therefore, its leadership should avoid making statements that could further alienate it from the people.Sharma's remarks came after Mufti described the construction work as an "assault" on the region's ecology.
"In the name of development, it is an assault on our fragile ecology, putting both the Sheshnag ecosystem and the Amarnath Yatra at risk," she said.She also alleged that chief minister Omar Abdullah's government had extended a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) for constructing a road to the ecologically sensitive area.The BRO, however, clarified that all work was being carried out in accordance with applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) Jammu and Kashmir president Manish Sahni led a protest against the use of heavy machinery near Sheshnag Lake, located at an altitude of 11,730 feet.Holding placards, Sahni raised concerns over the potential threat to the fragile Himalayan ecology, religious sentiments and the safety of pilgrims.
He questioned the BRO's claim that the road-widening work had received the necessary approvals and demanded that all project-related documents, including approvals, Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), maps and environmental clearances, be made public.Sahni warned that construction in an ecologically sensitive zone without a proper environmental impact assessment and disaster risk study could have serious consequences.He also sought clarification from lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha on the administration's position and demanded that a delegation of Shiv Sainiks and Hindu leaders be allowed to visit Sheshnag to assess the situation on the ground.Drawing a parallel with the Mata Vaishno Devi shrine atop the Trikuta Hills in Reasi, Sahni said the original character of the pilgrimage had earlier been altered in the name of development. He alleged that ongoing cable car projects were now bypassing sacred sites such as Charan Paduka, Banganga and Ardhkuwari, reducing them to "picnic spots."(With PTI inputs)
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect people’s everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

title: Thirupparankundram row LIVE: Madurai District Collector says Devasthanam did not authorise lamp-lighting team
description: The Supreme Court has permitted a one-time lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the 'Deepathoon' on Thiruparankundram Hill on November 24, coinciding with Karthigai Deepam.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
- November 25, 2026 16:21VHP says anti-Hindu politics nearing extinction, seeks action against T.N. govt The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) accused the TVK government in Tamil Nadu of defying the Supreme Court’s order on the traditional lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at ‘Deepathoon’ on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai, saying its actions amount to an insult to the judiciary, the Constitution and Hindu religious sentiments. The RSS affiliate also warned that “anti-Hindu” politics and such a mindset are nearing extinction from the country’s political landscape and will soon disappear from Tamil Nadu as well. In a statement, VHP international president Alok Kumar said preventing a centuries-old religious tradition hurts the faith and sentiments of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan and reflects the state government’s “anti-Hindu obstinacy”. “Preventing a centuries-old religious tradition despite the Supreme Court’s order is a grave insult to the Indian Constitution and the judiciary. It is also a serious affront to the faith and beliefs of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan,” Mr. Kumar said. - PTI
- November 25, 2026 16:20‘Countdown has begun for TVK govt’, claims T.N. BJP chief on 'Deepathoon' row Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran said the “countdown has begun” for the TVK-led government and warned Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of “legal consequences”, after the Karthigai Maha Deepam was not lit at the hilltop pillar in Thirupparankundram despite a Supreme Court order. Speaking to reporters, Mr. Nagenthran said the incident was not merely “anti-Hindu but also violated the Constitution”. Targeting Mr. Vijay directly, he questioned the CM’s maturity and impartiality. “My assessment is that the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister lacks the maturity, magnanimity or mindset required of a CM to view everyone equally. I think he is ruining himself by getting caught in the conspiracies of certain political parties,” he alleged. - PTI
- November 25, 2026 15:20What does John Doe order passed by Madras High Court mean? The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, on November 24, 2026, passed a ‘John Doe’ order in the Deepathoon case with regard to the lighting of the lamp at Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai for Karthigai Deepam. The High Court bench restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement” only. A ‘John Doe’ order is an ex parte injuction ordered against unknown persons. Ex parte injunctions are injunctions that are granted even without hearing the other party. Issued against anonymous offenders, these are also called ‘Ashok Kumar’ orders in India and are equivalents of the placeholder ‘John Doe’ used in the U.S. Read the full story below
- November 25, 2026 15:12Hindu parties seek Supreme Court order on relocating deepam lamp to ‘deepathoon’ The Hindu parties orally mention an application filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to the State and temple authorities that the deepam lit at the Deepa Mandapam be shifted to the ‘Deepathoon’. “To light the lamp at the Deepathoon either by igniting it from the same Deepam that is still burning at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple, or by making the necessary arrangements in accordance with the order dated November 20, 2026,” the application said. - Krishnadas Rajagopal
- November 25, 2026 14:50BJP, RSS trying to divide T.N. over Thirupparankundram deepam row: TNCC chief TNCC chief B. Manickam Tagore on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) accused the BJP, RSS and Hindu Munnani of attempting to “politicise” the Karthigai Deepam celebrations at Thirupparankundram to divide the people of the state. Speaking to reporters in Thirupparankundram, a day after protests erupted over the ceremonial lamp not being lit at the disputed stone pillar (Deepathoon) atop the hill, Mr. Tagore defended the Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance government, and claimed that “both the administration and the district collector had respected the Supreme Court’s orders.” “It clearly states that the Devasthanam will decide who will light the lamp and where it will be lit. The Devasthanam’s board of trustees (Arangavalar Kuzhu) sat for six hours and decided to light it at the same traditional place as per custom. Both the Tamil Nadu government and the collector have respected the Supreme Court orders,” he said. - PTI
- November 25, 2026 12:59Madurai District Collector says Devasthanam did not authorise lamp-lighting team The Madurai District Collector on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) squarely blamed the ‘devasthanam’ of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple on Thirupparankundram Hill for defying a Supreme Court order to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on November 24. In a preliminary status report, Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna said he had held multiple meetings, been in constant touch with the local and police authorities and made arrangements to ensure the lamp was lit at the ‘Deepathoon’ ever since the evening of the Supreme Court order on November 20. “From the side of the District Administration, every arrangement was complete and every possible difficulty had been offered an immediate solution. The only step was the authorisation of the team [to light the lamp] by the Devasthanam,” the Collector’s report said. Read the full story below
- November 25, 2026 12:52BJP accuses Rahul, INDIA bloc of double standards on Constitution The BJP on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) targeted the INDIA alliance and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the Karthigai Deepam row, accusing the Tamil Nadu government of defying the Supreme Court’s directions and showing contempt for the Constitution. Addressing a press conference, BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said the state government did not implement the Supreme Court’s order. “I want to bring to your notice the biggest contempt for constitutional authority being committed by the INDIA alliance’s Tamil Nadu government, in utter disregard of India’s eternal culture,” he said. Targeting the INDIA bloc, Congress and Gandhi, Mr. Trivedi said, “You always try to keep the Constitution in your pocket, but now you are not ready to uphold a judgment delivered by the Supreme Court, which is the custodian of the Constitution.” - PTI
- November 25, 2026 12:30Madras High Court considers contempt action over non-compliance with Supreme Court order A mention was made before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) regarding the Supreme Court’s interim order allowing the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon/stone pillar atop Thirupparankundram Hill on the day of Karthigai Deepam not being complied with despite an assurance given to the High Court. K. K. Ramesh of Madurai made a mention before a Division Bench of Justices G. R. Swaminathan and M. D. Sumathi to initiate suo motu contempt. The court asked Mr. Ramesh to file a petition. - B. Tilak Chandar
- November 25, 2026 12:10Administration says Supreme Court-directed temple team arrangements made; Devasthanam declined The district administration, in a statement released yesterday, said that all arrangements were made as directed by the Supreme Court. The temple Devasthanam was requested and instructed in writing and reminded to authorise its team and proceed. However, the Devasthanam did not authorise a team until the last moment. Instead, its Board of Trustees passed a resolution to light the lamp at the usual place, and the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, said in the statement from temple officials. - The Hindu Bureau
- November 25, 2026 12:07Thirupparankundram temple says it stood by tradition, lit lamp only at customary spot Shortly after the Karthigaideepam was lit at the usual place atop Thirupparankundram yesterday, the Arulmighu Subramanian Swamy Temple Executive Officer G. Selvi and Board of Trustees chairman V. Shanmugasundaram jointly stated in a press release that the temple has followed the age-old culture and agama rules in lighting the lamp. The Board of Trustees, including C. Rajapandian, K. Alagappan, K. Regina Devi and K. Chitra, who were present, passed a resolution unanimously. The members resolved to follow the rituals and ensure that the festival was conducted in a peaceful environment. The press release said the temple, which is famous and the first abode of Lord Muruga (Arupadai Veedu), has been following the rituals from time immemorial. The temple, which has been conducting various festivals all through the year, adopted custom and rituals and age-old continued practices as per the agama rules. - The Hindu Bureau
- November 25, 2026 11:44Devotees barred from Tirupparankundram hill for second consecutive day Devotees and the general public were barred from ascending the Tirupparankundram hill here for the second consecutive day on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), with heavy police personnel deployed near the entrance of the Palani Andavar temple. Police have erected barricades along the pathway leading to the hill and are restricting entry strictly to local residents. Those living on Kottai Street, which leads to the Palani Andavar temple, are being permitted access only after verification of their address through Aadhaar cards. Heavy police deployment continued near the Palani Andavar temple entrance on Wednesday (November 24, 2026), as the restrictions remained in place. - PTI
- November 25, 2026 11:39T.N. government accused of defying Supreme Court on ‘Karthigai Deepam’ lighting in Madurai The petitioners have accused the Tamil Nadu government of defying the Supreme Court order on lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp in Madurai’s Thirupparankundram. Appearing before a Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan for the Collector said “unfortunately the lamp was not lit” at the ‘deepathoon’. A status report has been filed. Senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the Hindu parties, countered during the oral mentioning that the State was resorting to “anticipatory mentioning against a blatant breach of the law”. He accused the State of employing “strategies and devices” to circumvent the Supreme Court order to light the Karthigai Deepam on the deepathoon on November 24, 2026, as a “one-time, limited arrangement”. - The Hindu Bureau Read the full story below
- November 25, 2026 10:21BJP accuses Tamil Nadu government of defying SC order BJP leader CR Kesavan has accused the TVK-Congress government of betraying devotees by preventing the lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. He alleged that the government had hurt Hindu sentiments and accused it of pursuing appeasement politics.
- November 25, 2026 09:28Mannargudi Jeeyar accuses Tamil Nadu CM of betraying Murugan devotees over Deepam row Mannargudi Sendalangara Jeeyar has criticised the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister after the Karthigai Deepam was not lit at the disputed Deepathoon pillar despite the Supreme Court’s interim order. He accused the CM of misleading devotees and alleged that political considerations had driven the handling of the issue.

title: Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years
description: Karnataka attracts ₹800 crore Kawasaki expansion over 10 years creating 600 jobs, holds talks with Panasonic Automotive and pushes for stronger Japan-Karnataka economic ties.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Japanese industrial major Kawasaki Heavy Industries has committed to invest up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery Pvt. Ltd. at Harohalli Industrial Area in Karnataka. The expansion is expected to generate around 600 manufacturing jobs.
A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed in Tokyo in the presence of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister for Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development M.B. Patil.
The agreement was exchanged by Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, S. Selvakumar, Kawasaki Heavy Industries representative Kenji Matsushita and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery CEO Minoru Hatsuda.
Hydraulic pumps and related components
The proposed facility will manufacture hydraulic pumps, swing motors and related components for the construction equipment industry. The investment will be taken up in two phases.
Established in Bengaluru in 2012, Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery has become a major player in India’s excavator hydraulic pump market. The expansion is expected to strengthen Karnataka’s construction equipment and capital goods ecosystem.
The State government has assured the company of assistance with land allotment, approvals, clearances and applicable incentives. The Chief MInister and Mr. Patil also invited Kawasaki’s leadership to participate in the Global Investors Meet — Invest Karnataka 2027, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru from April 20 to 22.
Karnataka has attracted 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016, with more than 525 Japanese establishments currently operating in the State, according to an official release.
Talks with Panasonic Automotive
The Chief Minister and Mr. Patil also met the leadership of Panasonic Automotive in Japan, led by its president and CEO, Mike Nagayasu. The discussions focused on Karnataka’s strengths in advanced manufacturing and Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and the possibility of the company expanding its operations in the State.
The delegation invited the company to participate in the Global Investors Meet 2027.
Meets Japan Minister
Mr. Shivakumar also met Japan’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Yasutaka Nakasone, in Tokyo and discussed strengthening economic cooperation and bilateral ties. He invited a high-level Japanese delegation to the Global Investors Meet 2027, with a dedicated Japan country pavilion.
The Chief Minister thanked Japan for its continued support to infrastructure projects, including Bengaluru Metro and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board, and sought further cooperation in Karnataka’s development priorities.
During the visit, Mr. Shivakumar also met members of the Japan Kannada Association and Tokyo Kannada Balaga. He enquired about their well-being and discussed their lives in Japan, community activities and links with Karnataka.

title: FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO
description: FSSAI widens crackdown on packaged drinking water as Bisleri fails lab tests; nationwide sampling, 1-2 month results, and new packaging material inspections.
author: PTI
content:
FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said the food regulator is collecting samples of packaged drinking water from across the country and lab testing will be complete in around two months.
He also announced that FSSAI would soon start inspection of 'packaging materials' used for food items, saying those should be 'food grade'.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test.
The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International.
When asked about its enforcement drive against packaged drinking water, Mr. Punhani said, "We are in the process. The process has started. We are doing all over the country."
On the timeline for results, he said, "It's a very big country. So I think it will take at least a month or two."
The CEO said the drive on packaged drinking water is not for any particular reason but part of the FSSAI efforts to safeguard consumers' interest by ensuring safe food.
"There is no particular reason. If you notice, in the last year, we have taken up, one by one, a lot of things. We have done dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, and sugary drinks. Water is also part of that process," he told reporters on the sidelines of a CII event.
Mr. Punhani highlighted that FSSAI has taken action against misleading advertisements as well as claims on the labelling of food products.
Asked about when the regulator will start the legal process against Bisleri International, Mr. Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing and it will happen".
Earlier, sources had said that FSSAI officials have carried out inspections of the premises of all major food business operators (FBOs) engaged in packaged water business and took samples for lab testing.
FSSAI would take legal action against companies if their samples fail the lab test and they are found to be violating the rules and regulations, sources had said.
Prosecution against Bisleri
On Sunday, through a social media post, FSSAI informed that it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".
A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.
"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator had said.
Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.
The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law.
On Monday, Bisleri International asserted that its packaged drinking water is "safe" for consumption, and it will cooperate with the food regulator to address the issue.

title: UP woman flaunts jewellery in Instagram posts, neighbour and her lover steal from home
description: A woman in UP039s Etawah used her friendship with a neighbour to steal her jewellery after monitoring her Instagram posts flaunting ornaments She and her accomplices including her lover made off with gold and silver jewellery and Rs 232 lakh in cash Police arrested all four accused
author: India Today News Desk
content:
UP woman flaunts jewellery in Instagram posts, neighbour and her lover steal from home
A woman in UP's Etawah used her friendship with a neighbour to steal her jewellery after monitoring her Instagram posts flaunting ornaments. She and her accomplices, including her lover, made off with gold and silver jewellery and Rs 2.32 lakh in cash. Police arrested all four accused.
A woman's Instagram posts flaunting her jewellery gave her neighbour the idea to rob her in Uttar Pradesh's Etawah. The accused, Pooja Yadav, allegedly befriended Seema Devi and monitored her social media updates. She then roped in her lover and two aides to break into Seema's house and steal gold and silver ornaments, along with Rs 2.32 lakh in cash, police said on Wednesday.
The theft occurred on March 6, when the family was away attending a function. Pooja, 32, who masterminded the robbery, allegedly broke the latch of the back door to gain entry and stole the jewellery kept in a cupboard, police said. Pooja and her three accomplices – Gautam Yadav, 35, Asif Mansoori, 31, Ram Verma, 27, were arrested on Wednesday.
Police said that Pooja lived in Seema's neighbourhood. According to Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Brijesh Kumar Srivastava, Seema regularly wore jewellery and shared pictures of it on social media. Pooja noticed these posts and gradually befriended her, using the association to learn more about the household.
During questioning, Pooja told police that she met Seema's cousin Gautam Yadav at a wedding around four years ago. The two wanted to elope and marry but faced financial difficulties. Pooja later shared details of Seema's jewellery with Gautam, and the two allegedly hatched a plan to steal it, SSP Srivastava said.
Pooja then brought in her partner, Asif, and two other accomplices, Gautam and Ram. On the night of the theft, the group struck when the house was empty. They later sold the stolen ornaments at different locations to avoid attracting suspicion by disposing of them together, according to the SSP.
Police arrested all four accused and recovered around 36 grams of gold jewellery, 541 grams of silver ornaments and Rs 2.32 lakh in cash.
During questioning, Gautam said he had used part of the stolen money to purchase a Swift car on finance for Rs 27 lakh, besides spending some of the proceeds. The four accused have been sent to jail, and cases have been registered against them under various sections.

title: Assam to get new greenfield airport in Silchar, Cabinet approves Rs 2,014 crore
description: The Union Cabinet has approved a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar for Rs 2014 crore The project will improve passenger and cargo connectivity across the Barak Valley and neighbouring northeastern states
author: Amit Bhardwaj
content:
Assam to get new greenfield airport in Silchar, Cabinet approves Rs 2,014 crore
The Union Cabinet has approved a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar for Rs 2,014 crore. The project will improve passenger and cargo connectivity across the Barak Valley and neighbouring northeastern states.
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the construction of a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar, Assam, at an estimated cost of Rs 2,014 crore. The project is expected to improve air connectivity to the Barak Valley and neighbouring northeastern states, including Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland and Manipur, while giving a boost to tourism and cargo movement.
The proposal was approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the decision while briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting at the National Media Centre (NMC).
The proposed airport will be developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and will be fully funded through its internal resources.
EXISTING AIRPORT OPERATES FROM AIR FORCE FACILITY
The existing Silchar airport is owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India. It operates a civil enclave spread across 70 acres.
The proposed greenfield airport at Doloo will provide a dedicated new airport facility for the region, improving its capacity to handle passenger traffic and strengthening connectivity with other northeastern states.
AIRPORT TO HANDLE 1.01 MILLION PASSENGERS ANNUALLY
According to the project details, the new airport will have a terminal building spanning 12,351 square metres and a runway measuring 2,705 metres in length and 45 metres in width.
It will be designed to handle 800 passengers during peak hours, with capacity for 400 arriving and 400 departing passengers. Its annual passenger-handling capacity is estimated at 1.01 million.
Vaishnaw said the airport would improve connectivity to the Barak Valley and the adjoining northeastern region, helping promote tourism.
BOOST TO CARGO MOVEMENT AND REGIONAL ECONOMY
Besides passenger connectivity, the project is expected to facilitate cargo movement, particularly the transportation of perishable goods and horticultural produce from the northeastern region.
Improved air connectivity could help local producers access wider markets while reducing logistical challenges involved in transporting agricultural and horticultural products.
The proposed airport is expected to strengthen Silchar's role as a regional connectivity hub and improve access to several parts of the Northeast.

title: Nazir Ahmad Wani: The Kashmir militant who became Army hero
description: Once involved in militancy in Kashmir Nazir Ahmad Wani joined the Indian Army and became a hero He was killed fighting terrorists in Shopian in 2018 Eight years later his remarkable journey from terrorist to soldier and Ashok Chakra awardee remains a story worth telling
author: Anand Singh
content:
Nazir Ahmad Wani: The Kashmir militant who became Army hero
Once involved in militancy in Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Wani joined the Indian Army and became a hero. He was killed fighting terrorists in Shopian in 2018. Eight years later, his remarkable journey from terrorist to soldier and Ashok Chakra awardee remains a story worth telling.
Nazir Ahmad Wani was once a terrorist in Kashmir, on the other side of the Indian Army's guns in the Valley. But he later wore the Olive Greens, and died fighting terrorists for India. It was on this day, eight years ago, that Lance Naik Nazir Ahmad Wani, made the supreme sacrifice.
Wani's journey from being a militant to a soldier and national hero is one of the rarest stories of transformation.
On November 26, 2018, the body of Lance Naik Wani arrived at his village of Chak Ashmuji in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, wrapped in the Indian Tricolour. Some 500 to 600 villagers gathered to bid him farewell. As his body was lowered into the grave, a 21-gun salute by the Indian Army rang out.
It was a poignant end to the life of a former militant.
The man who had once walked the path of militancy had gone on to earn two Sena Medals for gallantry before making the supreme sacrifice in an operation in Shopian on November 25, 2018. He was 38.
Posthumously, he was awarded the Ashok Chakra, India's highest peacetime gallantry award, becoming the first person from Jammu and Kashmir to receive the honour.
Eight years after his death, Wani's remarkable journey was recalled by Lieutenant General Satish Dua (Retd), the former Army Corps Commander in Srinagar, who has chronicled the soldier's life in his 2024 book, A General Reminisces: A Life Under Fire in Kashmir.
In a post on X, Dua wrote, "An incredible story of a terrorist who became a National Hero."
NAZIR AHMAD WANI'S LIFE WAS SHAPED BY KASHMIR CONFLICT
Nazir Ahmad Wani was born into the family of Sonuallah, a farmer who also ran a small dhaba. In the excerpt from his book, Dua describes how the family's limited income made it difficult to support their four sons.
Wani's childhood, however, was not defined by militancy alone.
Dua recalls three incidents from Wani's early years that left an impression on the young boy. One involved his Kashmiri Pandit schoolteacher, Pandit Shubhan Ji, who explained to his Muslim pupils how different religions had different customs and how communities had coexisted in Kashmir.
Another involved a retired soldier from his village who would narrate stories of his military service to local children. The soldier once told him, with pride in his voice, "Maine teen jung mein ladai ladi hai [I've fought in three wars]." Nazir was impressed. The young Wani, according to the book, concluded that it must be a heroic thing to be at war.
After listening to him speak about fighting wars, the young Nazir declared, "I will also fight wars when I grow up." The retired soldier laughed. Lt Gen Satish Dua (Retd) wrote in his book, "Little did he [the retired soldier] know that this young boy would one day become the recipient of the highest medal for bravery."
But the Kashmir in which Wani grew up was in the grip of militancy. As a teenager, he drifted towards militancy groups, initially running errands for them and eventually becoming involved in militancy.
But Wani was fortunate to find a way out of militancy through the Ikhwan, a counter-insurgency group made up of former militants who had switched sides and began working with the security forces in Kashmir.
WHAT WAS KASHMIR'S IKHWAN FORCE?
The Ikhwan emerged in Kashmir in the mid-1990s as a counter-insurgency initiative to bring former militants over to the government's side.
Lt Gen Satish Dua describes it as a bold experiment that paved the way for an even bigger one — "raising a Territorial Army battalion comprising surrendered militants".
The Ikhwan's members worked alongside security forces, using their local knowledge to identify militants, gather intelligence and support counter-insurgency operations. For young men like Nazir Ahmad Wani, it also offered a way out of militancy.
The programme was significant because the men involved often had an understanding of the local terrain and networks that could be useful to the security forces.
Wani subsequently joined the Army's 162 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army), also known as the Home and Hearth battalion of the Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry (JAK LI), in 2004.
His transition was not merely from one organisation to another. He went on to participate in counter-insurgency operations against the very kind of militancy with which he had once been associated.
NAZIR AHMAD WANI WON TWO SENA MEDALS FOR GALLANTRY
Wani was a decorated soldier. His military career was marked by repeated acts of gallantry. He received the Sena Medal for gallantry twice, first in 2007 and again in 2018.
His first Sena Medal came after an anti-militancy operation in his home district in January 2007, during which he eliminated four militants, according to a contemporaneous report in The Tribune.
The second came on the eve of Independence Day in 2018. He was recognised for eliminating a terrorist in close combat during an operation at Kund in Kulgam in November 2017. He had also helped apprehend two other militants alive.
He also served with Rashtriya Rifles (RR) units in Kashmir. The RR is a specialised counter-insurgency force of the Indian Army, raised in 1990 to tackle militancy in Jammu and Kashmir. It operates primarily in areas affected by insurgency.
His final operation would become the defining chapter of his military career.
OPERATION BATAGUND: WANI'S FINAL BATTLE IN SHOPIAN
On November 25, 2018, Wani was part of an operation launched by the 34th Battalion of Rashtriya Rifles after intelligence inputs indicated the presence of six heavily armed terrorists in Batagund, Shopian district.
According to his Ashok Chakra citation, Wani "insisted on being part of the assault team". His unit was tasked with blocking the likely escape route of the terrorists.
As the security forces established the cordon, the terrorists attempted to break through, firing indiscriminately and hurling grenades.
Wani held his position and eliminated a terrorist in a close-range exchange of fire. The man was subsequently identified as a district commander of the Lashkar-e-Taiba.
He then moved closer to the target house under heavy fire and lobbed grenades into a room where another terrorist was hiding. When a foreign terrorist attempted to escape through a window, Wani engaged him in hand-to-hand combat and eliminated him despite sustaining serious injuries.
The citation records that he continued engaging the remaining terrorists, injuring another before being hit again. He eventually succumbed to his injuries.
The official Ashok Chakra citation reads, "For displaying unparalleled bravery and supreme sacrifice in the line of duty," Wani was awarded the Ashok Chakra posthumously.
NAZIR AHMAD WANI: THE MAN BEHIND THE UNIFORM
Beyond the soldier and his military decorations, Wani was a husband and father of two sons, Athar and Shaid.
In an interview with PTI in January 2019, nearly two months after his death, his wife Mahajabeen recalled their relationship. The two had met at a school in South Kashmir around 15 years earlier.
"It was love at first sight. He was a great husband, always fiercely protecting us," she said.
She was at her parents' home when she received the news of his death. Wani had called her the previous evening to enquire about the family's well-being.
Mahajabeen, a teacher, said she did not cry when she learnt that her husband was no more. "I did not cry when I was told he is no more. There was an inner resolve which did not allow me to cry," she told PTI.
She recalled how Wani always encouraged people around him to be happy and help resolve others' problems. Inspired by him, she said she wanted to dedicate herself to educating children and guiding young minds towards becoming good citizens.
"He loved me so much. For me, he was my guiding light," she said.
On January 26, 2019, President Ram Nath Kovind posthumously conferred the Ashok Chakra on Wani. His wife and mother received the award on his behalf at the Republic Day celebrations in New Delhi.
Eight years after his death, Dua's tribute brings attention once again to a life that cannot be understood through a single label or phase. In his Instagram tribute on Wednesday, Dua described Wani's journey as "one of the greatest stories of redemption in the history of the Indian Army".

title: FIR against comedian Yash Maheshwari for jokes about Chhath, sindoor and women from Bihar
description: The remarks drew criticism from the Congress, BJP, and Shiv Sena. Patna police cited alleged concerns that the content could disturb social harmony and trigger tensions between communities
author: Himanshu Harsh
content:
Himanshu Harsh is a Correspondent with The Indian Express, currently leading on-the-ground coverage ... Read More
- Tags:
- chhath puja
- comedian
- FIR
Patna Police have registered an FIR against Delhi-based stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari over alleged obscene and objectionable remarks about women from Bihar and Chhath Puja traditions in a video uploaded on his YouTube channel. Police cited alleged concerns that the content could disturb social harmony and trigger tensions between communities.
An officer on Thursday said the case was registered on November 24 at Patna Cyber police station under sections 75(1), 79, 351 and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with sections 66(C) and 66(D) of the Information Technology Act.
“Information was received through social media alleging that a YouTube channel, operated by Maheshwari, had carried abusive and derogatory comments about women in Bihar, allegedly attempting to undermine their dignity,” the officer said.
On further investigation, the officer said the content was found to have had the “potential to affect social harmony among different communities and create a law-and-order situation”.
“The FIR was lodged after the matter was taken seriously in view of the possibility that the remarks could disturb communal harmony and create animosity between different sections of society. The cyber police are examining the matter,” the officer said.
The controversy erupted after Maheshwari uploaded a stand-up performance titled Morally Questionable on November 21. The performance, filmed at Hideout Comedy Club, included jokes about Bihar, its women, and customs associated with Chhath Puja, clips of which later circulated widely on social media.
Among the remarks that drew criticism was a sexually explicit comparison involving the long streak of orange sindoor worn by married women during Chhath Puja, a religious tradition in which women observe rituals and pray for their husbands’ longevity.
The clips triggered criticism from a section of social media users and cultural groups, with some people demanding police action.
Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi called the remarks an attack on cultural dignity and women’s dignity, urging the Bihar and Delhi Police to take cognisance and initiate legal proceedings.
“Mocking Chhath Puja, making obscene remarks about married women and ridiculing their sindoor is a vile assault on our cultural dignity and the dignity of women masquerading as ‘comedy’,” Singhvi wrote on X.
He added that constitutional freedoms came with responsibility and called for the strictest action permissible under law.
BJP leader Ritu Jaiswal had also demanded that FIRs be registered against the comedian in every district of Bihar. In a post on X, she said legal action should be sufficiently strict to make him realise his mistake, adding, “We will not tolerate anyone maligning the faith and identity of this festival.”
Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam said that mocking religious beliefs and women’s dignity could not be defended in the name of freedom of expression.
Amid the backlash, Maheshwari removed the controversial performance from his YouTube channel and deactivated his Instagram account. On the night of Tuesday, he uploaded a video titled Public Apology to All the People of Bihar on YouTube.
In the video, Maheshwari acknowledged that his remarks about Bihar’s culture were inappropriate and apologised for them. “I shouldn’t have made those remarks. It was never my intention, but I am sorry that it came across like that, and people objected to it,” he said.
He said he had no intention of hurting anyone’s religious sentiments but admitted that his comments had come across the wrong way. Promising to be more careful about his content, he said he would refrain from sharing similar material in the future and learn from the experience.
Patna police said the investigation was continuing and that further action would be taken in accordance with the law.

title: In Ranchi, a protest against tree felling ends in detentions
description: The activists are protesting the proposed felling of trees and the displacement of Adivasi bastis for a 10-lane road project
author: Shubham Tigga
content:
Shubham Tigga is a Correspondent at The Indian Express, presently based in Pune, where he covers the... Read More
- Tags:
- Jharkhand Police
More than a dozen people, including several activists, were detained by police in Ranchi on Wednesday during a protest against the proposed felling of trees and the displacement of Adivasi bastis for a 10-lane road project.
The protesters gathered along the roadside, holding placards and appealing to ministers and legislators passing through the area as the special Assembly session was underway.
Protesters said they were standing at a distance from one another and were not obstructing traffic.
Shailesh Krishna, an activist who has been raising the issue of the proposed tree-felling, said the existing four-lane road was adequate and there was no need to expand it into a 10-lane road. He said the proposed expansion would result in the felling of thousands of mature trees, affecting Ranchi’s air quality, environment and public health.
“We are trying to draw attention towards alternative solutions. Nature has to be part of modern city infrastructure. You cannot simply remove it and build infrastructure in its place,” he said.
According to a petition filed on Wednesday by advocates Piyushita Tudu and Shailesh Poddar, approximately 7,000 trees would have to be felled to expand a 4–5 km stretch into a 10-lane road. The proposed expansion, they said, would destroy trees, affect people’s livelihoods and displace Adivasi families living in the area.
Activist Siraj Dutta said the proposed road expansion would also affect settlements along the route. He said some families had been living there for decades, while others had settled on the land after being displaced when HEC acquired land for its township.
Dutta also questioned the police action, claiming that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was not applicable at the spot where they were protesting. He said the protesters were standing nearly 2 km away from the Assembly and were not blocking the road.
Nayan, one of the two women social workers detained, alleged that police personnel used force against the protesters despite their asking under which law they were being prevented from standing there. She alleged that women police personnel pulled and pushed them before forcing them into a police van.
“We were told that we were being taken to a ground where we would be allowed to protest. However, we were driven around in the police van without being told where we were being taken and were eventually brought to the police station,” she said.
Lavanya, another social worker, alleged that five women police personnel pushed and dragged her. She also alleged that one officer struck her on the side of her ribs with a baton, leaving scratches on her arm. She said she had not yet checked whether she had sustained bruises.
A police official from Tupudana police station said that protests were not allowed within a 1-km radius of the Vidhan Sabha as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were in force. “We detained them as protests were not permitted in the area,” the official said.

title: CJP’s Saurav Das moves Delhi HC over being stopped from flying to London
description: The court will hear the matter on Thursday, November 26.
author: Sohini Ghosh
content:
Sohini Ghosh is a Senior Correspondent at The Indian Express. Previously based in Ahmedabad covering... Read More
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das has moved the Delhi High Court against the Centre’s decision to stop him from flying to the United Kingdom, where he was set to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.
Das’ counsel, advocate Krishnesh Bapat, mentioned the matter for urgent hearing on Wednesday before a division bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma. The court, however, said it would hear the matter on Thursday, November 26.
Das’ lawyer said, “I was stopped at immigration, no order was shown…I can still make it to the United Kingdom on 27 (November, if heard on November 25)…”
ACJ Sambre, however, said, “Let it be (listed) tomorrow.”
CJP co-convenor Das said on Tuesday that he had planned to speak about Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and B R Ambedkar at the lecture, to which the Oxford students’ union had invited him.
However, he claimed, immigration officials stopped him on Monday (November 23) night at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport from boarding his flight to London. Immigration authorities allegedly flagged discrepancies in his passport details.
The Regional Passport Office at Chennai has initiated proceedings that could result in the impounding of Das’s passport while issuing him a show-cause notice on November 23, asking him to respond within seven days. The notice also advises him not to use the passport for any travel until he submits his explanation.
Das said he wanted to talk about the “cockroach movement” in India — for which he was invited — and how it had grown so large without violence.
“The world would have seen how such a big movement happened without any violence,” he said at a press briefing, adding that people in other countries are also curious about it.
Following the halt in his travel plans, Das, in a series of social media posts on X (formerly Twitter), lashed out at the “anti-intellectual” BJP-led government and alleged that it was afraid of him speaking at “these prestigious institutions”.

description: The FIR was filed by the Patna Police after concerns that Yash Maheshwari's comments could affect social harmony and create hostility between communities. | India News
author: Avinash Kumar, Nidhi Giri
content:

FIR filed after comedian Yash Maheshwari's ‘derogatory’ remarks on Bihar women, Chhath Puja
The FIR was filed by the Patna Police after concerns that Yash Maheshwari's comments could affect social harmony and create hostility between communities.
An FIR has been registered at Patna cyber police station against stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari, popularly known as @Almostyash on YouTube, over “derogatory and objectionable” remarks about women in Bihar.
According to the Patna Police, the FIR was registered on November 24 under various sections of the BNS and the IT Act, after concerns that the comments could affect social harmony and create hostility between communities.
The action follows widespread backlash over a purported clip from Maheshwari’s stand-up performance in which he allegedly made disrespectful remarks about the sindoor tradition observed by women during Chhath Puja.
Deep Dive
The comments triggered sharp criticism from social media users and political leaders, with several demanding legal action. The comedian later issued an apology.
Congress leader Abhishek Singhvi condemned the comedian’s remarks, calling them a “vile assault” on India’s cultural and women’s dignity. He said mocking the festival and ridiculing married women’s sindoor under the guise of comedy was unacceptable.
“I strongly urge the Bihar Police, Delhi Police and all concerned law-enforcement agencies to take immediate cognisance, register appropriate cases and ensure the strictest action permissible under law against Yash Maheshwari. Constitutional freedoms always come with responsibility,” he posted on X.
BJP leader and activist Ritu Jaiswal also took to X to demand an FIR against the comedian in every district of Bihar, expressing her objection to his remarks about Chhath Puja and the devotees.
She said, “Legal action against him should be so strict that he realises his mistake and witnesses the grandiosity of our festival at the next Chhath. We will not tolerate anyone maligning the faith and identity of this festival.”
While the Patna Police didn't mention any remarks on Chhath Puja, the comedian did say in his apology that he shouldn't have spoken about Bihar's cultural practices.
“In connection with derogatory and objectionable comments about women from Bihar made on the social media platform YouTube through the channel @Almostyash (Yash Maheshwari) on 24.11.2026, an FIR has been registered at Patna Cyber Police Station under Case No. 1550/26, dated 24.11.2026, under Sections 75(1), 79, 351, 352 and 66(C), 66(D) of the IT Act," Patna Police said in a post on X on Wednesday.
“The FIR was registered after the matter was taken seriously in view of concerns that the objectionable comments about women from Bihar in the aforementioned video/content could affect social harmony and create hostility between different communities.”
The case is being investigated by the Patna cyber police station.
Yash Maheshwari apologises after Chhath Puja joke
In a video shared on his YouTube channel last night, Maheshwari said that he should not have made comments about Bihar's cultural traditions.
Introducing himself as a stand-up comedian, he said, "Recently, I uploaded a video in which I was talking about certain cultural aspects of Bihar. I think I should not have done that. I completely stand by that, and I apologise. I should not have made those comments in that manner."
He said he had no intention of hurting anyone's religious sentiments or offending those who celebrate the festival, adding that he was 100 per cent in the wrong for making that joke.
"It was never my intention to hurt anyone's religious sentiments, any festival or anyone's feelings in any way. But I am not sure how it was portrayed, and perhaps it was entirely my mistake that it came across that way. I genuinely accept my mistake," he added.
Maheshwari also said he would be more careful about the content he puts out and would try not to repeat the mistake.

title: CM Suvendu Adhikari directs cinema halls to allot prime-time slot to Bengali film on Hindu saint
description: The decision came days after a section of cinema hall owners in Bengal announced that the screening of the Bengali movie would be discontinued from November 27. | India News
author: HT Correspondent
content:
CM Suvendu Adhikari directs cinema halls to allot prime-time slot to Bengali film on Hindu saint
The decision came days after a section of cinema hall owners in Bengal announced that the screening of the Bengali movie would be discontinued from November 27.
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday directed cinema hall owners in the state to allot prime-time slots to “Sadhak Bamakhyapa”, a newly released Bengali movie on the spiritual journey of the 19th-century Tantric saint and mystic.
The decision came days after a section of cinema hall owners in the state announced that the screening of the Bengali movie would be discontinued from November 27 to make way for the Ayushmann Khurrana-starrer Yeh Prem Mol Liya. The Bollywood movie is set to release in theatres on Friday.
“We are very happy. The chief minister has directed cinema hall owners to screen the movie. No exhibitors can deny space to the movie,” Sayantan Ghosal, director of the Bengali movie, told the media.
In an earlier statement, the makers of “Sadhak Bamakhyapa” had called the discontinuation of the movie's theatrical run “disheartening”.
“The decision to discontinue the theatrical run of Sadhak Bamakhyapa from this Friday is an extremely disheartening one for us, especially when the film has been receiving such overwhelming love and appreciation from audiences,” said an earlier statement by the film’s makers.
It also said that since the film’s release on November 20, it has received an encouraging response, with audiences turning out in significant numbers and several shows recording houseful occupancy, even on weekdays.
“However, with the upcoming release of Yeh Prem Mol Liya, produced by Rajshri Productions and distributed by YRF, we have been informed by exhibitors about the challenges of accommodating adequate shows for Sadhak Bamakhyapa from this Friday,” it had said.
CM's intervention
On Tuesday, Adhikari met the film exhibitors and film distributors in the state. The issue came up during the meeting.
“It is not just a question of screening the movie Sadhak Bamakhyapa. He directed cinema hall owners to screen at least one Bengali movie during the prime time. He also warned that the license of the cinema halls would be cancelled if Bengali movies are not allotted space,” Rudranil Ghosh, actor and BJP MLA, told the media after the meeting.
“Bengali cinema got a new life after today’s meeting because of chief minister Suvendu Adhikari,” an SVF spokesperson said.

title: CJI Surya Kant calls for greater representation of women in legal profession
description: CJI Surya Kant calls for greater representation of women in legal profession | India News
author: PTI
content:
CJI Surya Kant calls for greater representation of women in legal profession
New Delhi, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant has called for greater representation of women in the legal profession, asking senior advocates to ensure that at least one-third of junior lawyers in their chambers are women.
Addressing the inaugural Smt Shashi Prabha Singh Memorial Awards ceremony at the Siri Fort Sports Complex here, the CJI on Wednesday also stressed the need to appoint more women as panel lawyers to strengthen their participation and representation at the Bar.
The awards, instituted in memory of the late mother of senior advocate and former Supreme Court Bar Association president Vikas Singh, were presented to four young women advocates in recognition of their potential and contributions to litigation.
The initiative also aims to provide financial assistance to help them advance their legal careers.
The CJI underscored the imperative to create equitable opportunities for women in the legal profession.
He urged that every senior advocate engaging juniors should ensure that at least one out of every three juniors in their chambers is a woman advocate.
Lawyer Monika Dhiman received the Nyaya Prabha Ratna award, while Huma Anjum and Priyanshi Kumari were jointly honoured with the Nyaya Prabha Gaurav award.
Lawyer Kavana Rao received the Nyaya Prabha Samman.
The awards were presented as part of the memorial cricket tournament, which brought together members of the Supreme Court and Delhi High Court judiciary, advocates and journalists.
Legendary cricketer and India's 1983 World Cup-winning captain Kapil Dev attended the event as the guest of honour and inaugurated the tournament.
He also felicitated the award recipients along with the CJI.
The cricket match, titled 'An Afternoon of Sportsmanship', was played between the CJI XI and the Supreme Court Media XI.
The CJI XI included several sitting Supreme Court judges, including Justices Vikram Nath, MM Sundresh, Dipankar Datta, Augustine George Masih, Sandeep Mehta, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh.
Judges of the Delhi High Court also participated. Justice Saurabh Banerjee was adjudged player of the match and also received the best batsman award.
Sumit and Shashwat of the Supreme Court Media XI were recognised as best bowler and best fielder, respectively.
The valedictory ceremony was attended by former CJI BR Gavai, CJI Justice Surya Kant and Justice Vikram Nath, among other dignitaries.
Speaking about the initiative, Vikas Singh said he had been working towards bringing the memorial project to fruition for more than three years.
He recalled the values of honesty, compassion, selflessness and service to humanity that his mother, Shashi Prabha Singh, embodied throughout her life.
He said his mother's values continued to guide him and that he sought to carry them forward by supporting and mentoring younger members of the legal profession.
