title: Saharanpur showdown: Why Akhilesh's 1st candidate list in UP has rattled Congress MP Imran Masood
description: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh
author: Pallavi
content:
Imran Masood has made back-to-back statements against SP as Akhilesh Yadav's party released the first candidate list.
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list includes two constituencies that the Congress leader considers his political turf. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress in alliance negotiations, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.Released on Tuesday night, hours after another round of seat-sharing talks between the two parties in Delhi, the five-name list features four Muslim candidates from western Uttar Pradesh and an OBC nominee from Bundelkhand. The four Muslim candidates are sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha. Jyoti Lodhi has been named from Lalitpur.The move has particularly rattled Masood, who represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and is the Congress's Uttar Pradesh working president. Having won the Saharanpur parliamentary seat in 2024, Masood sees the two qssembly constituencies as important to Congress's claim to political space in the region. His sharp response has raised a pointed question: does the SP want to take on the BJP or its INDIA bloc ally?
The Saharanpur war
The SP renominated four sitting legislators: Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha.
The fifth candidate, Jyoti Lodhi, has been named from Lalitpur.All four Muslim candidates are from western UP, where the SP is keen to retain its traditional support base and expand its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) coalition.But Behat and Saharanpur make the list particularly sensitive for Masood.The Congress MP won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in 2024 with 5,47,967 votes, defeating the BJP's Raghav Lakhanpal by 64,542 votes. He secured 44.57% of the vote, against the BJP candidate's 39.32%.His performance was particularly strong in the two assembly segments now at the centre of the dispute. Masood led by 44,626 votes in Saharanpur and 38,229 in Behat in the parliamentary election. Both, however, had elected SP MLAs in 2022.Umar Ali Khan won Behat with 1,34,513 votes, defeating the BJP's Naresh Saini by 37,880 votes. Ashu Malik secured Saharanpur with 1,07,007 votes, defeating the BJP's Jagpal Singh by 30,745 votes.The contrast is the main disagreement point between the allies. Congress is banking on the 2024 Lok Sabha mandate, while the SP is relying on its assembly-level victories and sitting legislators.For Akhilesh, the two seats are established SP territory. However, for Masood, they are part of the space where Congress can consolidate after his parliamentary victory.Masood and Malik were involved in a public exchange during a district development coordination and monitoring committee meeting earlier this year. After the SP announcement, Malik said he was under "no fear or pressure" and would contest the election strongly.Masood's nephew Hamza Masood was more combative. He asserted that Congress would contest all seven assembly seats in Saharanpur district, adding that his uncle's support was crucial in the region."BJP ko Saharanpur se Imran Masood hi hara sakte hain," he said.
The Akhilesh-Masood equation
The latest confrontation is another turn in a political relationship that has changed parties, positions and equations more than once.Imran Masood left Congress and joined the SP in January 2022, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. But the association lasted barely nine months. After the SP did not give him or his associates a ticket, Masood quit the party in October 2022 and joined the BSP.Mayawati appointed him coordinator of the BSP's western Uttar Pradesh unit, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. That stint, too, ended abruptly. In August 2023, the BSP expelled him, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. Masood returned to Congress in October that year.The return proved electorally significant. In 2024, Congress fielded him from Saharanpur as part of the INDIA bloc arrangement, with SP support. He defeated the BJP, giving Congress a prominent Muslim face in western UP.But the parliamentary victory did not necessarily settle the question of who would control the political space in the region.The unease has been building for months. Congress's decision to appoint Masood as Uttar Pradesh working president in October was viewed by some SP leaders as an attempt to strengthen its bargaining position in seat-sharing negotiations. The Indian Express reported that sections of the SP were uncomfortable with Masood's public criticism of Akhilesh and his demands for an early alliance decision.In August, another development added to the strain. Imran Masood's son-in-law, Shayan Masood, joined the SP, citing ideological differences with his father-in-law. Shayan subsequently criticised Masood for targeting Akhilesh instead of the BJP.The candidate announcement has now brought the personal and political tensions into the open."When you make such an announcement against me, I don't understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress, or the BJP," Masood said, questioning the SP's seriousness about the alliance.He also rejected the idea that Congress was seeking charity from the SP. "We are not beggars," he said, objecting to the party's unilateral announcement of candidates while negotiations were still underway.
Elder brothers or stepbrothers?
The public sparring quickly drew reactions from both camps, with some leaders attempting damage control and others adding fuel to the fire.SP leader ST Hasan urged restraint, describing the two parties as elder and younger brothers."We are like elder and younger brothers. We should not talk like two stepbrothers fighting over division of property," he said.SP MP SP Singh Patel, however, was less conciliatory. He dismissed Congress's electoral strength in Uttar Pradesh and said the party would only be able to win by relying on the SP."The Congress should simply accept whatever number of seats they are allocated in the alliance," he said.Masood hit back, invoking Rahul Gandhi's role in Patel's political rise. He argued that Patel was an MP because of the political impact Rahul Gandhi had created after 2019.The exchange has exposed a fundamental disagreement over the alliance's power structure. Congress wants its improved Lok Sabha performance recognised; the SP believes its much larger Assembly-level organisation should determine the terms.
The voter math
Strip away the personal exchanges and the five-candidate announcement points to a larger contest over political representation in western Uttar Pradesh.The region has considerable electoral significance for both parties. Saharanpur district, according to Census 2011 data, had a Muslim population of 41.9% and a Scheduled Caste population of 22.1%. These are district-wide population figures, not constituency-level voter shares, but they underline the social context in which the two parties are positioning themselves.For the SP, the PDA formula is an attempt to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broader electoral coalition. Renominating four Muslim sitting MLAs in its first list reinforces the party's commitment to that strategy.Congress, meanwhile, sees its 2024 performance as an opportunity to rebuild its own Muslim-Dalit political base, particularly in western UP. Masood's Saharanpur victory gave the party a prominent regional leader around whom it can attempt to build that presence.
The competition is not limited to the two INDIA bloc partners either. The Samajik Parivartan Morcha, a new alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), is another political formation seeking space among Muslim and Dalit voters.The BSP, too, remains part of the wider political equation, even as its organisational position has changed since the 2022 election.The SP has released a list of five, but the questions they have raised go well beyond Behat and Saharanpur. Who speaks for western UP's Muslim voters? How much space will Congress get within Akhilesh Yadav's PDA framework? And can two allies compete for the same electoral ground without undermining the alliance they are trying to build?For now, the SP has made its choices clear. Whether Congress accepts them, and whether the two parties can turn this confrontation into a workable seat-sharing arrangement, remains the bigger test.
News desk journalist, digital, at The Times of India, with a focus on Indian politics. Over a decade of chasing stories, taming headlines and arguing with commas like they're part of the opposition. Tracks elections, policy pivots, party drama and the fine print of power, where every word can tilt the narrative. Believes good journalism is clarity under pressure, ideally filed before the next breaking alert crashes in. Powered by deadlines, context, sharp edits and a steady supply of strong tea.

title: UP polls: SP, Congress seat talks turn into public tug-of-war; BJP calls it 'thugbandhan'
description: NEW DELHI: Relations between Congress and Samajwadi Party appeared to sour after the latter jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of
author: Rohitashwa Ranjan
content:
NEW DELHI: Relations between Congress and Samajwadi Party appeared to sour after the latter jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties.To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.Congress fumed over its poll partner's decision and said the high command must decide whether seat-sharing talks with SP should continue. In a sharp rejoinder the grand-old-party also reminded SP that they are not beggars and must be treated respectfully.Samajwadi Party, on the other hand, defended the announcements and maintained that announcing candidates for seats already held by the party was “a normal and expected process” in all alliance deals.The BJP, on the other hand, seized on the developments to highlight divisions within the opposition camp months ahead of a high-stakes electoral contest.What triggered the riftThe latest round of tensions began on Tuesday night when SP chief Akhilesh Yadav issued a lengthy public message to Congress, urging the party to prioritise "winnability" over the number of seats it wanted to contest.
In a social media post on X, Akhilesh also asked Congress to hold "serious discussions" on the seat-sharing deal."We propose that, by carefully considering public expectations and ground realities, we engage in serious deliberations to ensure the victory of our 'alliance' across the majority of the constituencies. Among the seats contested by us, the number of seats won should exceed the number of seats lost," he said.Moments later, Samajwadi Party declared its first list of candidates, retaining its sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha, while naming Jyoti Lodhi as its candidate from Lalitpur.Tej Narain Pandey alias Pawan Pandey was declared the party's candidate from Ayodhya in August.Behat and Saharanpur were reportedly on Congress' wishlist.The Saharanpur region is particularly significant for Congress, as the party's Uttar Pradesh working president, Imran Masood, won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 general elections.Congress has been seeking a larger share of assembly seats falling within parliamentary constituencies it won in the Lok Sabha polls. It has cited its improved performance in the 2024 general elections to strengthen its claim for a greater share of seats in the alliance.Congress cries foulThe list has started a fresh exchange of sharp remarks. Imran Masood objected to the SP's reported offer of just 26 "winnable" seats to Congress.Imran Masood expressed strong objections to the SP's decision to offer Congress just 26 "winnable" seats."Where is the alliance? If you are acting like this, then where is the alliance? Our leadership will decide what we need to do; I just don't understand it. Here you say one thing, and there something else happens," Masood told news agency IANS.Making it clear that the final call would rest with the Congress leadership, the MP said he would abide by whatever decision the party takes."This decision has to be taken by our party. What Akhilesh Ji is doing or not doing is not a big issue for me; I am bound by my party, and whatever my party says, I have to do that," Masood said."When you are holding talks on one hand and making announcements on the other, it shows that you are not serious," he added.Questioning the intention of their ally, Masood said, "I do not understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress or the BJP. It needs to be decided whether we want to fight the BJP or fight among ourselves."AICC in-charge of UP Rajendra Pal Gautam also expressed displeasure over the Samajwadi Party's decision and said this should have been avoided while seat-sharing talks were ongoing."They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over). Nevertheless, this had also happened in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, and some candidates were withdrawn as well," Gautam said."I hope everything will go in the right direction," Gautam added.Congress leader Hamza Masood, nephew of Congress MP Imran Masood, also questioned SP's approach towards its alliance partner, asking whether the SP wanted to fight Congress or BJP.Hamza alleged that SP leaders, supporters, former ministers and MPs were continuously targeting Congress leaders on social media, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, despite Congress maintaining silence and adhering to the principles of the alliance."First, they should decide whether they want to fight against us or against the BJP. If you check Twitter, their supporters, leaders, former ministers and MPs continuously target our leaders and make remarks against Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi," Hamza told IANS."We remain silent and follow the alliance principles, and will continue to do so on Rahul Gandhi's instruction, but Saharanpur is our strong district, in 2012 our candidates fought on these two seats strongly, in 2017 our MLAs won," he added.SP advises Congress to 'exercise patience'Samajwadi Party, however, said that the it was already agreed between both the parties that there would be no compromise on seats held by each other."It was clear from the outset and known to all. Don't really know what the objection is all about," Samajwadi Party MP Rajiv Rai said.Another SP MP Ramjilal Suman said that the party said that announcing candidates for seats already held by the party was “a normal and expected process” in all alliance deals."Don't know what the brouhaha is about? The SP has merely announced candidates on seats held by the party. What's wrong with that and why so much hullabaloo?"SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel weighed in on the controversy and refuted Congress's claim that SP's seat tally improved due to leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi."My advice to him (Imran Masood) is to exercise patience and refrain from making such direct, provocative statements. I did not become an MP because of the Congress party; I belong to the Samajwadi Party. We contested the election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav, not Rahul Gandhi. Therefore, such claims should not be made. We were part of an alliance, from which the Congress party also benefited," Patel said."Let’s be direct: how many of your candidates won? Out of 17 candidates, 6 of yours won--that’s 30%--whereas 37 of our candidates won out of 63, which is about 70%. You can do the math yourself; so, please don’t claim that we won because of them," he added.Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad, however, refuted speculation over the seat-sharing talks, saying that nothing of the sort was discussed in Tuesday's meeting and dismissing reports of discord between the alliance partners."Nothing of the sort was discussed in yesterday’s meeting. These are just baseless rumours, mere talk in the air. It would be best not to pay any heed to such talk. These are just rumours, and rumours simply vanish into thin air,” Prasad told ANI.Reiterating that the coalition remains united around the core objective of ousting the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he added, “There has been no such statement. Instead of focusing on such baseless rumours, consider what is actually significant: the decision to remove the BJP from power has been finalised. It is a settled matter that, under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav, a good government will be formed in Uttar Pradesh.”Outlining the progress of the seat-by-seat review, Prasad noted that further rounds of discussions would follow as the entire discussion could not be concluded. He added that the matters raised were discussed constructively.“The matters raised during the meeting were discussed constructively and in a cordial atmosphere. The core objective is to defeat the BJP at any cost and, in its place, make Akhilesh ji the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. To this end, seat-by-seat discussions took place, though the entire discussion could not be concluded," Prasad said.BJP's sharp jibeMeanwhile, BJP took a jibe at the opposition and sought to highlight that all was not well in the opposition camp."They should perhaps focus on their own seat-sharing numbers—whether the Samajwadi Party is offering them 5 seats or 26," BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said at a press conference."Akhilesh Yadav began his campaign from Raebareli. Then, the SP announced they would provide 26 seats, but following this they released a list of five names without any consultation—three of which could prove quite problematic for the Congress party. In doing so, they have clearly signalled their priorities," he added.Reacting to the seat-sharing talks between SP and Congress, the deputy chief minister said whether the deal cooks up or not makes no difference to BJP."SP has shown Congress its standing; now let Congress show SP its standing. Whether their deal cooks up or not, it makes no difference to us.""Such theatrics keep happening between the two parties (SP and Congress), but it will have no impact on the BJP's health," he added.The deputy chief minister said the people of Uttar Pradesh were politically aware and would stand “firmly behind the BJP”."That is not an alliance but a 'thugbandhan (alliance of deceivers)’ of goons, criminals, corrupt people and rioters. Its condition is neither good today nor is it going to improve in the future," Maurya said."Voting for the Samajwadi Party is like inviting trouble, while voting for the Congress would once again push the country towards decline. People are standing strongly with the BJP, and the party will form the government in Uttar Pradesh for the third time with a massive majority," he said.
Inside the seat-sharing deadlockReportedly, the first round of talks, which ended on Tuesday at Congress veteran Pramod Tiwari's Delhi residence, remained inconclusive.Congress is demanding 120 constituencies, including the Gandhi family's traditional strongholds of Amethi and Raebareli, and is unwilling to settle for fewer seats, news agency ANI reported, citing party sources.Congress conveyed its demand during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi, where it submitted a list of 120 constituencies it wants to contest, sources told ANI.Meanwhile, Akhilesh has called for mutual understanding between the alliance partners and said candidates should be selected based on their electoral prospects. He also emphasised the need for consensus candidates representing the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework on every seat to take on BJP.SP has also sought details about Congress's prospective candidates and their electoral prospects in other constituencies claimed by the party.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

title: 'Need to halt' vs 'politically motivated session': Jharkhand govt, oppn spar as assembly passes resolution against SIR
description: NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution demanding an immediate halt to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of
author: Karan Manral
content:
NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution demanding an immediate halt to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The resolution was passed by voice vote following a heated debate.As a special two-day session of the Jharkhand assembly began on Wednesday, finance minister Radha Krishna Kishore moved the resolution opposing the SIR.Leader of opposition and former chief minister Babulal Marandi described the session as "politically motivated" and accused the JMM-led state government of attempting to "mislead" people on the issue.Moving the resolution, Kishore claimed that voters were facing difficulties due to procedural complexities and technical shortcomings in the revision process."Of Jharkhand's 2.21 crore voters, 27% were deemed suspicious and sent notices," PTI quoted him as saying.He called the Election Commission a "puppet" of the BJP-led Centre and asserted that removing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was "necessary to protect the Constitution.""There is an urgent need to halt the SIR exercise immediately and to issue a fresh standard operating procedure to ensure transparency in the process," Kishore added.
BJP hits back
Hitting back at the Jharkhand government, senior BJP leader Babulal Marandi said that the SIR was aimed at purifying electoral rolls, but the state government was creating "confusion" over the exercise."While presenting details, the government concealed the break-up of deleted names. Of the 43 lakh deleted names, 7.63 lakh belonged to deceased voters, 15.53 lakh had shifted, 4.38 lakh were duplicates, and 14.50 lakh were untraceable," he claimed.He maintained that his party opposed any form of administrative negligence but warned that it would not accept attempts to "undermine" the statutory powers of constitutional institutions through "political manoeuvring.""I urge the state government to cooperate with the Election Commission in this (SIR) process, focusing on the inclusion of those who have been left out of the voter's list. I also urge the Election Commission to ensure that the SIR is conducted by taking into account the socio-economic and geographical conditions of Jharkhand," Marandi said.
He further argued that halting the electoral roll "purification drive" was not the solution, stressing the need to make the process more transparent, inclusive and accountable.The resolution will now be forwarded to the Centre and other competent authorities, seeking a fresh standard operating procedure (SOP) in consultation with various political parties for transparency.(With PTI inputs)
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect people’s everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

title: Srisailam temple organises Karthika Vanabhojanalu
description: Karthika Masam festivities at Srisailam feature Vanabhojanalu and free Sparsha Darshan for 420 Chenchu devotees.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The management of the Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple at Srisailam organised Karthika Vanabhojanalu at Rudra Vanam in the northeastern part of the temple complex on Wednesday as part of the month-long Karthika Masam festivities.
Srisailam MLA Budda Rajashekhara Reddy, temple trust board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu, Executive Officer M. Srinivasa Rao, members of the Board of Trustees, temple officials and staff, along with their families, participated in the event. Officials and staff of various local government departments also attended. The programme began with rituals performed to the Usiri (Indian gooseberry) tree at Rudra Vanam.
Mr. Ramesh Naidu said Vana Samaradhana was organised to preserve Vedic culture and traditions and familiarise participants with the temple’s customs. According to the Puranas, performing Vanabhojanalu in accordance with tradition conferred significant spiritual merit.
Mr. Srinivasa Rao said Vanabhojanalu performed at the sacred Srisailam carried greater spiritual significance. The Puranas described Srisailam not merely as a kshetra but also as a tirtha, home to several sacred water bodies. It was revered as an Anadi Kshetra, an ancient and timeless pilgrimage centre, and was also known as the nabhisthana, or the navel of the Earth. This was reflected in the reference to Srisailam as the central point in the solemn vows recited during Vedic rituals and worship, he said.
Spiritual scholar Nori Narayana Murthy of Tenali delivered a discourse on the significance of Karthika Masam and the tradition of Vanabhojanalu. Students of Likshitasri Dance Academy, Nandikotkur, presented a traditional dance performance.
Meanwhile, the temple management arranged free Sparsha Darshanam for members of the Chenchu tribal community on Wednesday. As many as 420 devotees from various Chenchu settlements were provided the facility to have Sparsha Darshanam of the presiding deity and darshan of the Goddess.

title: J&K clerics apologise, offer ‘repentance prayers’ for standing during Vande Mataram at Waqf Board function
description: Clerics apologize for standing to Vande Mataram at Waqf Day, pledge repentance, while MMU considers legal action over the controversy in J&K.
author: Peerzada Ashiq
content:
A group of prominent Muslim clerics who attended the Waqf Day function in Srinagar on Monday (November 23, 2026) apologised on Wednesday and “offered repentance prayers” over standing during the Vande Mataram song, as the incident triggered a wave of protests from religious groups in J&K, including the Muttahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU).
The controversy was sparked by the November 23 event of the J&K Waqf Board that was attended by Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Srinagar. At the first-ever Waqf Day function organised by BJP leader and J&K Waqf Board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi, the full Vande Mataram song was played with several top Muslim clerics on the dais as well as in the audience. National Conference (NC) MP Mian Altaf Larvi and Shia cleric and J&K Peoples Conference leader Imran Reza Ansari also attended the function.
Vande Mataram and the right to dissent
Facing criticism, Maulana Farooq, accompanied by other clerics, said in an online video, “Some things unacceptable from the Sharia point of view took place on the occasion. We repent for the same. We went outside the venue, immediately recited ‘kalima’ in a congregation and offered our repentance. Ulemas from other sects also attended it. We did not recite anything from our hearts. Allah will accept our repentance.”
Those who attended the function included Mufti Syed Basharat, Mufti Farooq, Mufti Inayatullah Qasmi, Maulana Farooq, Maulana Basharat Sakafi, Pir Syed Ejaz, Maulana Zakir, Abdul Rashid Dawoodi and imams of the Dastigeer Sahib shrine and the Hazratbal shrine.
A nation’s song: On Vande Mataram’s rendition
Maulana Rahmatullah, who heads Kashmir’s biggest seminary, Darul Uloom Raheemiyyah, welcomed the “act of repentance by the Muslim priests for their mistake”. “I congratulate these religious leaders for their immediate repentance prayers and reciting the ‘kalima’ again for the mistake. Allah must be pleased with them.”
Mr. Rahmatullah said anything that interferes with the faith of Muslims “is not acceptable”. “Mr. Dawoodi should have mentioned the Supreme Court ruling and clarified that the Vande Mataram cannot be forced. It was not a political stage but a Waqf function. I had advised Ms. Andrabi beforehand that you belong to a family who have spread Islam. I fail to understand why she committed this wrong. She should have conveyed to sing Jana Gana Mana but not play with religious sentiments and sing Vande Mataram. I ask Mr. Dawoodi to educate Ms. Andrabi on this, but then granting ‘imaan’ is in the hands of Allah,” said Mr. Rahmatullah.
Meanwhile, the MMU, an amalgam of religious organisations headed by Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, said, “It has categorically made clear on several occasions in the past, the fundamental and non-negotiable principle of Tawheed in Islam — the absolute Oneness of Allah. Islam strictly prohibits associating any partner with Allah or attributing divinity to any person, object, land or creation.”
The MMU said it was highly “regrettable and unacceptable” that Vande Mataram was played at the function of the Waqf Board, an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments and their sanctity. “There was no legal obligation to play Vande Mataram simply because it was an official function, and playing it was optional,” said the MMU.
It said the Waqf Board went ahead “with utter disregard for the fundamental religious beliefs and sensitivities of Kashmiri Muslims, which has caused deep hurt and anguish among people.”
“The MMU expresses grave concern over the increasingly routine inclusion of Vande Mataram at official government functions across Muslim-majority Jammu and Kashmir, despite the well-known religious reservations of Muslims. Such imposition disregards their religious convictions and constitutional rights and deepens distrust and alienation,” said the MMU spokesman.
The MMU said it was considering seeking legal opinion in this matter and will also submit a formal representation to the authorities concerned, “seeking an immediate end to the forcible imposition of Vande Mataram at government functions, educational institutions and other public events in Jammu and Kashmir”.
The MMU also asked Muslims, particularly those entrusted with religious responsibilities, “to uphold the fundamental principles of Islam, irrespective of any pressure, position or consideration”.

title: Deloitte India opens Mangaluru office, plans to recruit over 1,000 professionals in next two years
description: Deloitte India opens its first office in Mangaluru, aiming to hire 1,000+ professionals across AI, tech, data, and analytics in two years.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Deloitte India which opened its Mangaluru office on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) will initially house approximately 250 professionals, with plans to gradually scale the workforce to more than 1,000 professionals in the next two years, said Romal Shetty, Chief Executive Officer, Deolitte South Asia.
Speaking to press persons he said that Mangaluru office will host professionals working across areas including technology, artificial intelligence (AI), data and analytics, cybersecurity, consulting, tax, risk advisory, and other emerging capabilities, supporting Deloitte India’s growing client needs across sectors.
“The new office at wrkwrk Triangle, Kottara Chowki, marks another significant milestone in the organisation’s growth journey and underscores its commitment to taking high-quality professional opportunities closer to where talent resides,” Mr. Shetty said.
Recruitment of coastal talent
He said the Mangaluru office is Deloitte India’s 27th office in the country and the first office in Karnataka outside Bengaluru. “It will operate as an integrated capability and delivery center, connecting local talent with opportunities across Deloitte India’s national and global client network,” he said.
The CEO said that the company will also shift its innovation team from Bengaluru to Mangaluru office.
He said the company plans to recruit talent from Mangaluru and nearby regions, while also creating opportunities for Deloitte professionals currently working in larger cities to relocate closer to their families. It expects the new office to attract a combination of experienced professionals, fresh graduates, and specialised talent across multiple disciplines. “Developing the next generation of talent in Coastal Karnataka will be supported through campus engagement, industry-relevant skilling programmers, and career development opportunities,” the CEO said.
Attractive destination for global businesses
“Mangaluru has long been known for its strong educational institutions, entrepreneurial spirit, and talented professionals, many of whom have traditionally moved to larger cities in search of opportunities. By establishing a significant presence in Mangaluru, we are bringing world-class careers closer to home and enabling talented individuals to work on impactful engagements for clients in India and around the world, while remaining connected to their families and communities,” the CEO, who has his family roots in Kundapur in Udupi district, said.
Mr. Shetty said recent investments and the emergence of Mangaluru as a technology and innovation hub, often referred to as the ‘Silicon Beach of India’, are further strengthening its position as an attractive destination for global businesses and high-value knowledge services.
The CEO said Mangaluru’s high quality of life, lower commute times, strong communities, and coastal lifestyle make it a compelling destination for professionals seeking to build long-term careers outside traditional metropolitan centers.
Earlier, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Information Technology, Bio-technology and Home, inaugurated the company’s office in Mangaluru.

title: Birth certificate denied for newborn after father's name deleted from voter list
description: A newborn in West Bengal039s Cooch Behar has been denied a birth certificate for over two months with her family alleging that her father039s name being deleted from the voter list during the SIR exercise has stalled the registration process
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Birth certificate denied for newborn after father's name deleted from voter list
A newborn in West Bengal's Cooch Behar has been denied a birth certificate for over two months, with her family alleging that her father's name being deleted from the voter list during the SIR exercise has stalled the registration process.
A newborn girl in West Bengal's Cooch Behar district has been waiting for her birth certificate for over two months. Her family alleged that the registration process has been stalled because her father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
The father, Abdul Habib, said officials have refused to issue him a residency certificate, a document required for his daughter's birth registration. His wife, Amina Khatun, gave birth to the baby at a state-run hospital in Dinhata on September 8, but the family is yet to obtain her official birth record.
Habib said the problem began when he approached the local panchayat for a residency certificate. He alleged that officials cited the ongoing SIR exercise and his exclusion from the voter list as reasons for withholding the document. The panchayat is also currently without a pradhan, further complicating the process.
Officials reportedly advised him to approach the local MLA, but repeated visits to government offices have failed to resolve the issue.
Habib questioned why his electoral status should affect his daughter's birth registration, pointing out that his wife remains a registered voter and that the family possesses documents, including both parents' birth certificates and the 2002 electoral roll carrying his father's name.
When contacted by India Today TV, the Block Development Officer (BDO), Lhamu Y Wangdi, said the administration would look into the matter.
   
    
  
The incident has triggered political reactions, with leaders from the BJP, Congress and Trinamool Congress weighing in.
President of the ruling BJP in Cooch Behar, Abhijit Barman, said Habib should approach the tribunal to challenge the deletion of his name from the electoral roll. He maintained that the birth certificate would be issued as per the rules and said the matter should be examined through the appropriate legal process.
"If he is a genuine voter, his name will definitely appear. He should approach the tribunal and appeal. If he is a genuine resident, there is nothing to worry about," Barman said, adding that the birth certificate would be issued in accordance with the applicable rules.
Cooch Behar Congress district president Biswajit Sarkar, meanwhile, alleged that the SIR exercise had resulted in the deletion of names of genuine voters, leaving families facing difficulties in accessing essential documents.
He claimed Habib belongs to the local Muslim Rajbanshi community and is an indigenous resident of the region, alleging that genuine citizens were being wrongly portrayed as migrants or infiltrators.
"The names of genuine voters have been deleted during the SIR exercise, causing severe hardship. Children born to such people are now facing problems getting birth certificates. This is a major issue in Cooch Behar, and we will continue our agitation until the names of genuine citizens are restored," Sarkar said.
He alleged that the deletions were part of a broader attempt to disenfranchise genuine voters and said the Congress was pursuing the issue through protests and legal channels.
Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh also criticised the situation, saying the issue should be addressed by both the state and central governments.
"What happened in Cooch Behar is a serious problem. This is a newborn baby, and there is a problem. Similar complaints are emerging from several places. The state government or the central government should take this seriously because citizens are being harassed, and this should not happen," Ghosh said.
He added that discrepancies in the father's documents, if any, should be examined with utmost seriousness, rather than allowing them to affect the child's registration.

title: Global powers want dominance, don't want India to progress, says Mohan Bhagwat
description: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said powerful nations do not want India to progress as they seek to maintain their global dominance He said India unlike such powers believes in helping all countries including hostile neighbours such as Pakistan during crises
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Global powers want dominance, don't want India to progress, says Mohan Bhagwat
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said powerful nations do not want India to progress as they seek to maintain their global dominance. He said India, unlike such powers, believes in helping all countries, including hostile neighbours such as Pakistan, during crises.
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Wednesday said global powers do not want India to progress as they seek to retain their dominance, while India believes in helping even countries that are hostile towards it, PTI reported.
Bhagwat was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan (Retd) was the chief guest at the event.
The three-day festival has been organised by the Gyanyajnah Foundation and brings together Padma awardees from different fields to interact with people.
Bhagwat said the world was in a strange situation. "No power in the world wants India to progress because these powers seek to retain their dominance and believe in the principle of 'survival of the fittest'," he said.
"They keep everyone under pressure. This is how they are considered powerful and able to boss people around. If India grows, these powerful people's 'shops' will shut because India wants to help everyone," he added.
Listing countries that India had assisted, Bhagwat said it helped its neighbours in times of need even if they were hostile towards it.
"When the Maldives was in trouble, India transported water. India provided financial assistance to economically distressed Sri Lanka. India helps Nepal when it faces environmental problems and also assists Bangladesh. We have also helped Pakistan during floods and earthquakes," he said, according to PTI.
Bhagwat said India believed that power should be used to protect the weak and bring peace. "This is India," he said.
The RSS chief also said the younger generation was free from the influences of slavery. "If someone speaks genuinely, the youth are prepared to stand behind him. They hate lies and want to make their country great. The youngsters are thinking this way in every aspect," he said.
Bhagwat said good work should be emulated to achieve one's goals. "We should have faith in people who are doing good and not question their motives. Their work is worth emulating. If someone has done something out of self-interest, we should set aside that motive and follow their work. The next generation should take up their work, which will give them satisfaction," he said.
He said the Padma awardees had worked with great determination and brought changes to the lives of lakhs of people. "No matter how much they have earned, the satisfaction they have gained is incomparable. This event has given people here an opportunity to interact with such individuals," Bhagwat said.
The inauguration was held at Manthan Hall on the MIT Campus along Beed Bypass Road. Interactive sessions with Padma Shri awardees will also be held at the venue, the organisers said.
In his address, General Chauhan said young people would be the biggest contributors to and beneficiaries of Viksit Bharat.
"If we want to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the youth will make the biggest contribution and will also be its biggest beneficiaries. Fulfilling this dream is the responsibility of everyone. We have to learn from our past successes and bring our intellectual energy to the fore," he said, according to PTI.
General Chauhan also said developed countries could create obstacles in a country's path to development. The event highlighted India's approach to helping other countries, the role of young people in achieving the goal of a developed India by 2047, and the work of Padma awardees.

title: We're following Indian laws: Meta to Congress amid row over alleged curbs on posts
description: The Congress delegation presented material it said showed that posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi were being restricted Meta039s policy team told the delegation that the company follows transparent policies the sources said
author: Anmol Nath Bali
content:
We're following Indian laws: Meta to Congress amid row over alleged curbs on posts
The Congress delegation presented material it said showed that posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi were being restricted. Meta's policy team told the delegation that the company follows transparent policies, the sources said.
Meta’s policy team told Congress social media leaders that the company follows Indian law and applies transparent policies, sources said.
It was the first meeting between the two sides since the Congress accused Meta of restricting posts and accounts linked to the party and its youth wing, the Indian Youth Congress (IYC).
The meeting followed IYC protests outside Meta’s offices in Hyderabad, Gurugram and Mumbai. During the talks, the Congress delegation presented material it said showed that Meta was restricting posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi.
At Friday’s protest at Meta’s Hyderabad office, Telangana Youth Congress president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy alleged that Meta had suspended or restricted the Instagram accounts of IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma.
The Telangana Youth Congress said its workers entered the office in Gachibowli and demanded that Meta restore the affected accounts. Police detained Reddy and several other workers and took them to a police station.
WHAT THE YOUTH CONGRESS IS DEMANDING
On the same day, the IYC gave Meta seven days to publicly explain the alleged restrictions. It said it would continue protesting and raise the issue in court if the company failed to respond.
The youth wing asked Meta to disclose how many Indian accounts it had restricted in response to government orders over the previous six months and how many were still blocked. It also asked the company to explain what it described as the automated blocking of posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi or criticising the Narendra Modi government.
The IYC also demanded that Meta lift restrictions it described as illegal on the accounts and posts of opposition leaders, journalists and content creators.
Meanwhile, the IYC put up hoardings across Bengaluru, accusing Meta of favouring the BJP and failing to curb fake news and hate speech. One hoarding near Sadahalli Gate on the airport road depicts Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg in RSS attire under the slogan “Meta, BJP Ka Beta” (Meta, BJP’s son).

title: Tamil Nadu TVK MLA summoned over sexual harassment complaint by district collector: Police
description: Kallakurichi police served the summons at the TVK MLA’s residence after the Madras High Court directed Tamil Nadu to form a team to probe the complaint. | India News
author: S Vijay Karthik
content:
Tamil Nadu TVK MLA summoned over sexual harassment complaint by district collector: Police
Kallakurichi police served the summons at the TVK MLA’s residence after the Madras High Court directed Tamil Nadu to form a team to probe the complaint.
Tamil Nadu’s Kallakurichi police on Wednesday summoned Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh for questioning in connection with a sexual harassment complaint filed against him by a district collector, as a special team was constituted to investigate the allegations following a Madras High Court direction.
A team comprising a senior officer from the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station and a constable visited Vignesh’s residence in T Ramaswamy Nagar on Wednesday morning to serve the summons.
After informing his family members, the police handed him the summons and directed him to appear for questioning as part of the investigation, sources in the police department said.
The Kallakurichi All Women Police Station had registered a first information report (FIR) under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) after the district collector lodged a formal complaint alleging that the legislator had sent her obscene messages.
On November 24, while hearing the case, Madras High Court judge V Lakshminarayanan directed the state government to constitute a team to investigate the allegations.
Tiruppur superintendent of police Srishti Singh has been assigned to lead the investigation, under the supervision of inspector general of police (Administration) Kamini.
The judge also directed the Tamil Nadu government to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) with independent members.
Vignesh has dismissed the allegations as “fake news” and termed them baseless.
State minister for energy resources and law C T R Nirmal Kumar has described the issue as a “narrative” allegedly being pushed by the opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and its MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi.
Several political parties, including the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), have demanded the legislator’s arrest.

title: Pak show Dar-e-Nijaat’s screenings cancelled in Bengaluru after backlash
description: The screenings of Pakistan TV serial Dar-e-Nijaat were to be held on November 28 and December 5 at two separate venues in Bengaluru. | India News
author: Arun Dev, hindustantimes.com, Nidhi Giri
content:
Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.
Pak show Dar-e-Nijaat’s screenings cancelled in Bengaluru after backlash
The screenings of Pakistan TV serial Dar-e-Nijaat were to be held on November 28 and December 5 at two separate venues in Bengaluru.
Two private screenings of a Pakistani television serial named ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ were cancelled in Bengaluru as organisers withdrew their plans after online backlash over the move.
The screenings of ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ were to be held on November 28 and December 5 at two separate venues. Both invitations specified Pakistani clothing as the dress code, a detail that became central to the objections raised on social media.
Organisers cancel screenings
A representative of Sheesh Kebab confirmed that the November 28 programme had been called off but did not explain the decision. The host of the December 5 screening said the event had been intended for family members and a small group of acquaintances.
"We have cancelled the event. Although it was meant for family and a close circle, since this has become an issue, we have decided to cancel the screening," a representative told reporters.
The police became involved after a post on X questioned the events and called for intervention. The post objected to the proposed dress code and the promotion of Pakistani television content through the gatherings.
Talking to the media, police commissioner R Hitendra said the department was seeking information from the organisers before deciding on any action. “We are getting in touch with the organisers to know more details about it. If anything needs to be done on the ground, it will be done," he said.
ALSO READ: 'Serial practitioner of terrorism misrepresented facts': Jaishankar hits out at Pakistan PM Sharif at UNGA
Organisers had not obtained prior permission: Police
Police later said neither organiser had obtained prior permission and warned against holding the events. Pulakeshinagar Police, responding to the complaint on X, said the screenings had been cancelled. "It has come to our notice that the shows stand cancelled. Any information regarding the same is appreciated," the police said.
The first gathering was planned by The Bloom Society Sisters' Club at Sheesh Kebab in Frazer Town in east Bengaluru. The organisers had advertised a screening of two episodes, 34 and 35, followed by a Persian and Arabic dinner. The tickets were priced at ₹1,999.
The second event, hosted by The Star Club at Mowie Private Theatre in Jayamahal Extension, was also billed as a private screening.

title: ‘Sincerely apologise’: Tamil Nadu govt to Supreme Court on temple lamp row
description: On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted the lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day | India News
author: Ayesha Arvind
content:
Ayesha Arvind is a Senior Assistant Editor specialising in legal and judicial reportage. She covers High Courts and tribunals across southern India, and believes that important legal developments do not only come from New Delhi. Her work focuses on bringing significant decisions and developments from the region to a wider audience and explaining what they mean beyond the courtroom. She tries to make legal material accessible by translating legal jargon into clear, readable prose and putting pleas, lawsuits, judgments and legal developments in context. She also looks at their political realities and practical consequences for people. Ayesha is committed to the standards of integrity journalism requires. She places a premium on accuracy and fairness, and believes that journalism's powerful voice must be tempered by humility and a sense of proportion. Over almost two decades in journalism, she has covered law and order, civil law, crime and other areas of legal affairs. Her work includes breaking news, legal affairs stories, online analysis and commentary. Ayesha is deeply interested in the law, court judgments and the Constitution because they shape everyday life. She believes every citizen should have a basic understanding of them. What she enjoys most about covering courts is that every story brings something new to learn.
‘Sincerely apologise’: Tamil Nadu govt to Supreme Court on temple lamp row
On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted the lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day
Madurai collector Nishant Krishna apologised to the Supreme Court on Wednesday for failing to carry out its order allowing a ceremonial lamp to be lit at a disputed stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill, but blamed the temple board for not complying with the top court order.
“I sincerely apologise for the lamp not been lit at the Deepathoon,” the Madurai collector said in his status report to the top court. Krishna said he had taken “all the steps” between November 21 and 24 to secure the Devasthanam’s authorisation for a team to light the lamp at the stone pillar, known as the Deepathoon, in line with the court’s November 20 order.
“However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated 24.11.2026, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place. I submit that I will submit an additional status report with all supporting documents along with the same,” the Tamil Nadu government official said.
Deep Dive
“From the side of the District Administration, every arrangement was complete and every possible difficulty had been offered an immediate solution. The only step was the authorisation of the team [to light the lamp] by the Devasthanam,” the collector said in his report. Krishna was also present in the top court during Wednesday’s hearing.
On November 20, a bench of justices Aravind Kumar and VM Pancholi permitted the lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar at Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day as a restricted, one-time measure only. On Wednesday, the bench declined to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings over the issue but said it will take up applications, including contempt petitions, in a day or two.
In the report, Krishna outlined the sequence of events on November 24, and acknowledged that he was caught off guard by the decision of the board of trustees to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam, adding that “at no point did the Devasthanam communicate to the District Collector any authorisation of persons to light the lamp at the Deepathoon”.
Kumar said he had even emailed a reminder to the Devasthanam’s executive officer at 3.47 pm, asking him to authorise the team’s names without further delay. The collector said he was informed of the decision to light the lamp “at the place where it is customarily lit” after the lamp had been lit at 8.30 pm.
The temple board also issued a statement, declaring that it unanimously resolved to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam, located directly above the main deity, and protect the temple’s age-old customs. “Such long-standing continuous practices, religious traditions and rituals and the Agama rules are considered the unique religious identity of the temple,” a statement signed by the temple board’s chairperson V Shanmugasundaram said.
The Karthigai Deepam controversy centres on a dispute over where and by whom the lamp should be lit on the Thiruparankundram hill.
For decades, the deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes. Hindu groups had sought permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone lamp pillar located higher up the hill, approximately 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.

title: 'Following Indian Laws': What Meta Told Congress Leaders Amid Protests Over Restrictions On Party Posts
description: Meta executives Aman Jain and Natasha Jog met Congress social media leaders in New Delhi following IYC protests over alleged restrictions on party accounts and posts.
author: Shuddhanta Patra
content:
'Following Indian Laws': What Meta Told Congress Leaders Amid Protests Over Restrictions On Party Posts
Meta executives Aman Jain and Natasha Jog met Congress social media leaders in New Delhi following IYC protests over alleged restrictions on party accounts and posts.
Meta executives Aman Jain and Natasha Jog met Congress social media leaders in New Delhi following protests by the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) outside the company’s offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram over alleged restrictions on accounts and posts. During the meeting, Meta representatives also raised concerns over vandalism, while the Congress flagged alleged restrictions on its content. Meta, on Tuesday, assured the party that this was not the case.
The meeting was the first between Meta and Congress social media leaders since the party accused the company of restricting posts and accounts linked to the Congress and the IYC.

The Congress delegation presented material that it said showed posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi were being restricted. Meta’s policy team told the delegation that the company follows transparent policies and Indian laws, as per reports.
Youth Congress protests outside Meta offices
The meeting came amid protests outside Meta’s offices in Gurugram, Hyderabad and Mumbai. On November 21, the IYC gave the company seven days to publicly explain the alleged restrictions on accounts and posts critical of the BJP-led Centre.
The Youth Congress said it would continue to raise the issue through protests and in court if Meta failed to respond.
What the Youth Congress is demanding
The IYC has sought details from Meta on the number of Indian accounts restricted under government orders in the past six months and how many of them remain blocked. It has also demanded an explanation for what it described as the automated blocking of posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi or criticising the Narendra Modi government and the BJP.
The Congress has accused Meta of targeting content and accounts associated with the party and the Indian Youth Congress, while the company has maintained that it is neutral, follows Indian laws and has transparent policies.
Quick Answers
The Indian Youth Congress protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Gurugram over alleged restrictions on accounts and posts critical of the BJP-led Centre. They demanded a public explanation for automated blocking of posts mentioning Rahul Gandhi and wanted details on accounts restricted under government orders.

title: Maharashtra cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh BPL farmers for three months
description: The cabinet also sanctioned Rs 5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project (NTRLP) in Nandurbar district.
author: PTI
content:
Maharashtra cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh BPL farmers for three months
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:12 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:12 IST
The cabinet also sanctioned Rs 5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project (NTRLP) in Nandurbar district.
Amid drought, the Maharashtra cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh Below Poverty Line (BPL) farmers in 33 districts who are not covered under the direct benefit transfer scheme for the next three months.
The cabinet also sanctioned Rs 5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi River-linking Project (NTRLP) in Nandurbar district.
Under the food security scheme, farmers below the poverty line not covered under the direct benefit transfer (DBT) scheme will receive five kg of free foodgrains per person every month, comprising three kg of rice and two kg of wheat, according to a statement issued after the weekly cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.
The NTRLP envisages constructing six diversion barrages and is expected to provide irrigation benefits to around 26,526 hectares in the region. It will also generate 11.50 MW of electricity.
The cabinet also approved amendments to the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act to expedite attachment of properties of institutions involved in financial frauds.
A separate MPID tribunal will be established, with a provision to dispose of cases within 90 days.
In another decision, the cabinet approved amendments to the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966, to introduce a Revenue Court Case Management System for quasi-judicial proceedings in the revenue department, according to the release.
The amendments will also provide for a "one district, one appeal" mechanism to expedite disposal of cases.
The cabinet also approved an increase in allowances under the Dr Panjanrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme for EBC students, socially and educationally backward classes (SEBC) and economically weaker sections (EWS) pursuing undergraduate courses in health sciences.
The revised rates will cover food, accommodation and maintenance allowances.
The government also decided to provide financial empowerment facilities to teachers and non-teaching staff covered under the Shalarth system through NBFCs registered with the Reserve Bank.
The cabinet approved amendments to Sections 32(B) and 53(1A) of the Maharashtra Stamp Act to bring uniformity in the rates of fees charged for adjudication and appeals. A bill to this effect will be introduced in the forthcoming winter session of the state legislature.
It also approved amendments to the Acts governing Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University, Ramtek, and Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University, Nashik, to bring uniformity in provisions relating to registrar appointments, statutes, finance and accounts committees, building construction committees, annual reports and accounts.
The cabinet cleared the draft Maharashtra Private Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, paving the way for a comprehensive law governing private aided schools. The bill will be introduced in the legislature.
Amendments to the Maharashtra Mathadi, Hamal and Other Manual Workers (Regulation of Employment and Welfare) Act, 1969, and the Maharashtra Private Security Guards (Regulation of Employment and Welfare) Act, 1981, were also approved.
The cabinet further cleared a draft bill to amend the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021, to exclude acupuncture as a system of treatment from its purview, the release said.
In another decision, librarians working in private-aided Ayurveda and Unani colleges will be granted revised pay scales in accordance with the recommendations of the Seventh Pay Commission, on par with full-time librarians in government medical, dental and Ayurveda colleges.
The cabinet approved amendments to the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, and decided to place the amendment bill before the legislature.
It also sanctioned the allotment of government land to Mouda Nagar Panchayat in Nagpur district for construction of its administrative building.

title: Cardamom ad sparks clash between Bollywood star, India's food regulator
description: An advertisement for cardamom is at the centre of a legal spat between a Bollywood actor and India's most prominent food commissioner, with a court ruling set to shape how far companies can go in indirectly advertising brands whose promotion is restricted.
author: Reuters
content:
Ajay Devgn takes on Maharashtra food authority over Vimal cardamom ad as surrogate advertising row reaches court
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:08 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:08 IST
Bollywood stars and food regulators are locking horns over surrogate endorsements as authorities crack down on indirect promotions for restricted goods. The impending court ruling threatens lucrative celebrity revenue st
An advertisement for cardamom is at the centre of a legal spat between a Bollywood actor and India’s most prominent food commissioner, with a court ruling set to shape how far companies can go in indirectly advertising brands whose promotion is restricted.
India restricts advertising for liquor and tobacco but officials have for years also frowned upon the use of indirect means, called surrogate advertising, by companies in such sectors promoting their brands in the guise of sodas, water or glassware.
While companies say these are genuine businesses in their own right whose advertising cannot be curbed, health officials say the advertisements are aimed at generating recall of the parent brand whose publicity is restricted. Since 2024, India has been trying to finalise stringent guidelines to prohibit such advertisements outright.
In the case involving Bollywood stars, actor Ajay Devgn has sued the food authority of Maharashtra state, arguing he has been wrongly told to stop appearing in advertisements for Vimal cardamom packs, according to a non-public court filing dated October 15 reviewed by Reuters.
The state, whose food safety commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has become a national sensation for his aggressive stance on public health, asked Bollywood stars Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August to stop appearing in advertisements promoting Vimal cardamom, arguing the brand is mostly known for its betel nut mix, or pan masala, which is banned in the state.
The spat in the High Court in Mumbai could set a precedent, New Delhi-based lawyer Anuj Tiwari said. ”The case will test both the fairness of the department’s process before it imposes restrictions … and the parameters for deciding what counts as indirect advertising,” he said.
COURT SPAT ON CARDAMOM AD
In the advertisement available on Vimal Cardamom’s YouTube page and posted two years ago, the Bollywood stars are seen celebrating, throwing saffron at each other after Devgn consumes the product. The Hindi-language advertisement has 107 million views, while clips dubbed in other Indian languages have garnered millions more.
Devgn in his filing argues cardamom has not been prohibited in the state and ”there is no bar in endorsing a product which is not prohibited”.
Devgn did not respond to Reuters queries. Mundhe told Reuters the state believes the advertisements are against public health interests, and the state is separately reviewing responses submitted by Khan and Shroff, although Reuters could not ascertain details of their submissions.
Dushyant Mahant, a lawyer for PB Agro, which holds the licence to make Vimal cardamom and pan masala, told Reuters the allegations were futile as the company does not promote Vimal in Maharashtra and only advertises the product via nationally televised broadcasts that cannot be restricted geographically.
Industry estimates show India’s pan masala market was worth around $5 billion last year. Health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.
While Maharashtra bans it, Vimal’s tobacco-free pan masala sachets in other states cost around 5 rupees (5.4 US cents). But they are often consumed with chewing tobacco, sold at kiosks as ”twin packs” — a pan masala sachet alongside a tiny pouch of unbranded tobacco.
An adverse ruling in Devgn’s case could affect Bollywood stars as endorsements can amount to up to 30% of an actor’s earnings, and promoting tobacco-linked products is more lucrative than other advertisements, said Suresh Mathew, a Mumbai-based screenwriter.
”Most actors know if a product is a surrogate for another product,” he added. ”There are cases where certain actors have refused to lend their name to a product that they feel is harmful.”
($1 = 92.4950 Indian rupees)

title: Karnataka delegation studies Tokyo's integrated urban development model during Japan visit
description: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumarled delegation visited Tokyo Midtown Roppongi, a landmark mixeduse urban complex, developed in collaboration with Japan's leading architecture, engineering and urban planning firm Nikken Sekkei.
author: PTI
content:
Karnataka delegation studies Tokyo's integrated urban development model during Japan visit
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:04 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 17:04 IST
Karnataka's leadership is evaluating Tokyo's mixed-use urban models to reshape Bengaluru's infrastructure, focusing on fast-track execution and green spaces. Find out which specific city corridors officials plan to redev
Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar-led delegation visited Tokyo Midtown Roppongi, a landmark mixed-use urban complex, developed in collaboration with Japan’s leading architecture, engineering and urban planning firm Nikken Sekkei.
During the visit, the delegation, which included Minister for Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development M B Patil, interacted with Wataru Tanaka, Senior Executive Officer and Head of the Global Business Department at Nikken Sekkei, who was closely associated with the project’s master planning, the Chief Minister’s Office said in a release on Wednesday.
The delegation studied how the approximately 25-acre development transformed a former defence land parcel into an integrated urban district featuring office spaces, residential facilities, retail outlets, hospitality and cultural amenities, while retaining nearly 50 per cent of the area as open and green spaces, the release added.
Discussions focused on integrated master planning, vertical development, optimal land utilisation, pedestrian-friendly public spaces, seamless public transport connectivity and quality urban infrastructure.
Completed in approximately 2.5 to three years, the project offers valuable insights into developing sustainable, well-connected and livable urban spaces.
The delegation also explored the possibility of adapting Japan’s urban development model to Bengaluru’s strategic redevelopment initiatives and future infrastructure projects, with a focus on leveraging global best practices in integrated and mixed-use urban development, the release added.

title: विदेशों में बजेगा पंजाब के उद्योगों का डंका! शारजाह के 3,000 इंडस्ट्रियल नेटवर्क से जुड़ेगा 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब'
description: पंजाब के उद्योगों को वैश्विक बाजार देने के लिए 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' शारजाह के 3,000 इंडस्ट्रियल नेटवर्क से जुड़ने जा रहा है. जानें इस साझेदारी से राज्य के निर्यात और व्यापार को कैसे मिलेगी नई रफ्तार.
author: रवींद्र प्रताप सिंह
content:
पंजाब के उद्योग एवं वाणिज्य मंत्री अमन अरोड़ा ने पंजाब और संयुक्त अरब अमीरात (UAE) के बीच औद्योगिक, व्यापारिक और निवेश साझेदारी को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए एक अहम कदम उठाया है. उन्होंने शारजाह चैंबर ऑफ कॉमर्स एंड इंडस्ट्री और इंडियन बिजनेस एंड प्रोफेशनल काउंसिल (IBPC) के अधिकारियों के साथ उच्च स्तरीय रणनीतिक बातचीत की.
इस बैठक का मुख्य उद्देश्य दोनों क्षेत्रों के उद्यमियों को आपस में जोड़ना, बिजनेस-टू-बिजनेस (B2B) संबंधों को मजबूत करना और साझा निवेश के लिए एक ठोस ढांचा तैयार करना है. इससे पंजाब और शारजाह के व्यापारियों को नए बाजार तलाशने, संयुक्त उपक्रम (ज्वाइंट वेंचर) स्थापित करने और निर्यात बढ़ाने में मदद मिलेगी.
बातचीत के दौरान 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' और IBPC उद्योग-से-उद्योग स्तर पर तालमेल बढ़ाने के लिए सहमत हुए. अमन अरोड़ा ने बताया कि 'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' शारजाह के निर्माताओं, निर्यातकों और सेवा प्रदाताओं को पंजाब के उद्योगपतियों से सीधे जोड़ने में मदद करेगा. साथ ही, UAE के बाजार में विस्तार की चाह रखने वाली पंजाब की कंपनियों को भी पूरा सहयोग दिया जाएगा.
उद्योग मंत्री ने पंजाब के मजबूत औद्योगिक आधार और रणनीतिक स्थिति को वैश्विक निवेशकों के सामने रखा. उन्होंने कहा कि मुख्यमंत्री भगवंत मान के नेतृत्व में राज्य सरकार ने नियमों को बेहद आसान बनाया है. 'ईज ऑफ डूइंग बिजनेस' को बढ़ावा देकर और सिंगल-विंडो सिस्टम लागू करके पंजाब को देश का एक प्रमुख निवेश केंद्र बनाया गया है.
अमन अरोड़ा ने स्पष्ट किया कि पंजाब केवल पारंपरिक निवेश तक सीमित नहीं रहना चाहता, बल्कि विनिर्माण, प्रौद्योगिकी, निर्यात और सेवाओं जैसे क्षेत्रों में दीर्घकालिक द्विपक्षीय साझेदारी बनाना चाहता है. उन्होंने शारजाह के व्यापारिक समुदाय को पंजाब आकर निवेश की संभावनाएं तलाशने का न्योता भी दिया.
बैठक में भारत-UAE व्यापक आर्थिक भागीदारी समझौते (CEPA) का विशेष जिक्र किया गया. अमन अरोड़ा के अनुसार, पंजाब और UAE के बीच मजबूत संबंध न केवल आपसी व्यापार को बढ़ाएंगे, बल्कि पंजाब के निर्यातकों के लिए मध्य पूर्व और अन्य अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाजारों का दरवाजा भी खोलेंगे. शारजाह का औद्योगिक नेटवर्क भी पंजाब के लिए काफी उपयोगी साबित हो सकता है, जहां 3,000 से अधिक विनिर्माण इकाइयां, 7 फ्री जोन और 18 औद्योगिक जोन मौजूद हैं.
'इन्वेस्ट पंजाब' के सीईओ अमित ढाका ने एक प्रस्तुति के जरिए राज्य की नई औद्योगिक नीतियों और प्रशासनिक सुधारों की जानकारी दी. उन्होंने बताया कि 'फास्ट-ट्रैक पंजाब' पोर्टल के जरिए निवेशकों को सभी जरूरी मंजूरियां, सुविधाएं और आफ्टर-केयर सेवा एक ही जगह से उपलब्ध कराई जाती हैं. इस पूरी पहल से पंजाब और UAE के व्यापारिक संबंध मजबूत होंगे और स्थानीय उद्यमियों को वैश्विक सप्लाई चेन से जुड़ने का सीधा मौका मिलेगा.

title: LoC पर हलचलः कठुआ में मिला 'टॉय एयरप्लेन', संदिग्ध गुब्बारे से भेजा गया सीक्रेट संदेश! सुरक्षा एजेंसियां चौकन्ना
description: कठुआ सेक्टर में एक संदिग्ध गुब्बारा पाया गया है. एयरप्लेन के आकार वाले इस खिलौने में PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप मच गया. सूचना मिलने के बाद पुलिस के जवान मौके पर पहुंचे और संदिग्ध गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में ले लिया. पुलिस अब इसकी जांच कर रही है.
author: राज मिश्रा
content:
लश्कर आतंकी लतीफ अहमद भट्ट के मारे जाने के बाद केंद्रीय गृहमंत्री अमित शाह ने घाटी से आतंकवाद का नामो-निशान मिट जाने का दावा किया था. हालांकि, सुरक्षा बलों और विभिन्न रिपोर्टों के अनुसार आतंकी नेटवर्क की चुनौती अभी पूरी तरह समाप्त नहीं हुई है. सुरक्षाबलों के मुताबिक, पाकिस्तान के कब्जे वाले कश्मीर में फिर से आतंकी कैंप सक्रिय हैं और वहां से सीमा पार से करीब 500 आतंकी घाटी में घुसने की फिराक में हैं. इस इनपुट के बीच अब कठुआ सेक्टर में एक संदिग्ध गुब्बारा पाया गया है. एयरप्लेन के आकार वाले इस खिलौने में PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप मच गया. सुरक्षाबलों ने तुरंत गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में लेकर इस सीक्रेट मैसेज को डिकोड करना शुरू कर दिया है.
गुब्बारे पर PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप!
जानकारी के मुताबिक, जम्मू-कश्मीर के कठुआ जिले के मढ़ीन तहसील के हांडे चक गांव में सफेद और पीले रंग का हवाई जहाज के आकार का एक गुब्बारा मिला है. गुब्बारे पर PIA लिखा है. यह पाकिस्तान की सरकारी विमानन कंपनी है, जिसका मुख्यालय कराची में स्थित है. जानकारी के अनुसार, गांव के एक बच्चे ने इस गुब्बारे को देखा, जिसके बाद इसकी सूचना पुलिस पोस्ट मढ़ीन को जानकारी दी गई. सूचना मिलने के बाद पुलिस के जवान मौके पर पहुंचे और संदिग्ध गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में ले लिया. पुलिस अब इसकी जांच कर रही है.
कठुआ में घुसपैठ का खतरा ज्यादा
बता दें कि कठुआ सेक्टर LoC के काफी पास है. घने जंगल और उंची पहाड़ियों के चलते इस इलाके से आतंकियों के घुसपैठ का खतरा सबसे ज्यादा रहता है. पिछले महीने 29 अक्टूबर को कठुआ जिले के बाना चक गांव में खेत से आंशिक रूप से जली हुई सैन्य वर्दी, जूते और पिट्ठू बैग बरामद हुए थे. हालांकि, पुलिस की ओर से आतंकी घुसपैठ की संभावनाओं से साफ इनकार किया गया था. इस घटना से पहले 11 सितंबर के हिरानगर सेक्टर के बोबिया इलाके में सीमा बाड़ के पास से एक संदिग्ध आतंकी पकड़ा गया था.
