title: राहुल गांधी को 'सुप्रीम' राहत, ED-CBI नहीं करेगी आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच; हाईकोर्ट में फिर होगी सुनवाई
description: राहुल गांधी को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से बड़ी राहत मिली है. SC ने CBI और ED को कांग्रेस नेता के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करने के हाईकोर्ट के आदेश को खारिज कर दिया है.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट से कांग्रेस सांसद राहुल गांधी को बड़ी राहत मिली है. शीर्ष न्यायालय ने इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट के उस आदेश को खारिज कर दिया है, जिसमें CBI और ED को कांग्रेस नेता के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करने का निर्देश दिया गया था. मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने राहुल गांधी के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों वाली याचिका को नए सिरे से विचार करने के लिए इलाहाबाद हाई कोर्ट के पास वापस भेज दिया है.
दरअसल, सीजेआई जस्टिस सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी मोहना की पीठे ने इस मामले में सुनवाई की और फिर से इस आदेश पर नए सिरे से विचार करने के लिए याचिका को हाईकोर्ट भेज दिया.
इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट ने केंद्रीय जांच एजेंसियों को आदेश दिया था कि वे कांग्रेस नेता राहुल गांधी पर लगे आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करें. इस संबंध में हाईकोर्ट ने आदेश भी जारी किया था. इसी आदेश को कांग्रेस नेता ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट में चुनौती दी थी. अब मामले की सुनवाई के बाद सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने इसपर नए सिरे से विचार करने को कहा है.
बता दें कि इस मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान शीर्ष न्यायालय ने याचिका की सुनवाई करते हुए कार्यवाही का ऑडियो बंद कर दिया था. मामले के शिकायतकर्ता विग्नेश शिशिर भी आदालत के सामने पेश हुए थे. उनके व्यक्तिगत रूप से कोर्ट के सामने पेश होने के वजह से सुनवाई की ऑडियो-वीडियो बंद कर दी गई थी.
गौरतलब है कि इससे पहले सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने हाईकोर्ट से कहा था कि वह आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों से जुड़े मामले में आगे की कार्रवाई को रोक दे. इसके अलावा कोर्ट ने सीबीआई और ED को भी निर्देश दिया था कि वे राहुल गांधी के खिलाफ इस मामले में हाई कोर्ट के आदेशों के तहत कोई रिपोर्ट दाखिल न करें.
हालिया सुनवाई के दौरान हाईकोर्ट ने कहा था कि सीबीआई की ओर से दाखिल हलफनामा उसके पिछले आदेश के अनुरूप नहीं है. इसमें याचिकाकर्ता की ओर से राहुल गांधी की संपत्ति को लेकर की गई शिकायत पर अब तक हुई प्रगति के बारे में कोई स्पष्ट जानकारी नहीं दी गई थी. वहीं, बाद में इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट ने नई दिल्ली स्थित CBI के अधिकारी से कहा था कि वे खुद न्यायालय के सामने पेश हों और मामले में हुई जांच की प्रगति के बारे में जानकारी दें.

title: 65 Pakistani Terrorists On Security Radar In J&K As Hunt Intensifies After Killing Of Last Active Local Militant
description: Security agencies have launched a massive hunt for around 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir, including 35 linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba and 25 to Jaish-e-Mohammed, following the killing of the last known active local militant Lateef Bhat.
author: Asian News International
content:
65 Pakistani Terrorists On Security Radar In J&K As Hunt Intensifies After Killing Of Last Active Local Militant
Security agencies have launched a massive hunt for around 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir, including 35 linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba and 25 to Jaish-e-Mohammed, following the killing of the last known active local militant Lateef Bhat.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Days after the killing of lone active local terrorist Lateef Bhat from Jammu and Kashmir soil, a massive hunt is on for 65 estimated Pakistani terrorists operating in the erstwhile state, having allegiance to banned terror outfits Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) and others, sources in the security establishment said.
Officials in the security establishment told ANI that these 65 Pakistani terrorists have been on the radar since their presence was confirmed by different intelligence wings within the system and it is learnt that the majority of them belong to the LeT and the JeM.
Of the 65 foreign terrorists, 35 are linked to the LeT and 25 to the JeM, while the rest are from different outlawed terror outfits. Pakistan-based groups, primarily JeM and LeT, have been responsible for major attacks, including the 2001 Indian Parliament attack, the 2016 Uri attack, and the 2019 Pulwama bombing. These groups operate with logistical support from across the border, using infiltration routes along the Line of Control (LoC).
With the fresh inputs received, Jammu and Kashmir has no listed active local militants after the killing of LeT's last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir Valley, Lateef Bhat, who was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district on November 18, after an eight-day search operation.
Advertisement
As per officials, the estimated number of terrorists operating in the Union Territory has fallen from 91 terrorists (including foreign terrorists and local terrorists) registered in 2024 to around 65-- which includes only Pakistani terrorists-- till date.
Officials said the disappearance of local militants has altered the security landscape in Kashmir, but Pakistan-origin terrorists remain active in certain areas of Jammu, particularly in remote districts marked by dense forests and rugged mountainous terrain.
Advertisement
Security agencies estimate that the number of 65 foreign terrorists are operating across Jammu and Kashmir, with their presence being monitored in districts such as Poonch, Rajouri, Kishtwar and Doda areas in Jammu and Kashmir--which has been a hotspot for militancy and terrorism since the late 1980s, with insurgency fueled by Pakistan-based terror groups, cross-border infiltration, and
radicalisation efforts.
Officials made it clear that the figure is based on assessment reports of multiple agencies working in Jammu and Kashmir, and it varies as terrorists frequently keep on changing their locations.
Addressing the passing-out parade of probationary deputy superintendents of police, sub-inspectors and assistant directors of the Forest Protection Force at the Sher-i-Kashmir Police Academy in Udhampur on November 18, J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed confidence that the region would soon become terror-free, and asserted that only a handful of foreign terrorists remained in the Union Territory.
Officials indicated multi-agency operations based on inputs to carry out the elimination of the estimated foreign terrorists, as in the neutralisation of all seven members of the JeM group led by Saifullah in Kishtwar earlier this year. The operation against the Saifullah group was a major success for the security forces as the group, which had infiltrated in April 2024, was neutralised in a series of operations culminating on February 22 in the Chatroo area during Operation Trashi-I.
Despite the reduction in the number of active terrorists, security agencies continue to focus on preventing infiltration, identifying support networks and tracking foreign terrorists operating in remote areas.
As per a data, a total of 135 terrorists were active in 2022. Of them, 85 were foreign terrorists, and 50 were local terrorists. Compared with the figure of active terrorists in 2022, there was a nearly 48. 35-person decline in the number of active terrorists in 2023.
The continuous decline in the number of active terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir is the result of intensifying counter- terrorism operations in the region, focusing on tracking and neutralising active militants.
The government has reiterated its commitment to eliminating terrorism and ensuring peace in Jammu and Kashmir. Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely as intelligence agencies work to identify and dismantle terrorist networks operating in the region.

title: 'BJP's Face Is Lotus, MLAs Will Decide CM': Keshav Maurya Backs Yogi Adityanath, Rules Out Self As Contender For UP's Top Post
description: Uttar Pradesh Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya backed Yogi Adityanath as Chief Minister but said elected MLAs would decide the party's CM after the 2027 Assembly polls. He also dismissed the SP-Congress seat-sharing tussle and predicted a third consecutive BJP government in UP.
author: Asian News International
content:
'BJP's Face Is Lotus, MLAs Will Decide CM': Keshav Maurya Backs Yogi Adityanath, Rules Out Self As Contender For UP's Top Post
Uttar Pradesh Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya backed Yogi Adityanath as Chief Minister but said elected MLAs would decide the party's CM after the 2027 Assembly polls. He also dismissed the SP-Congress seat-sharing tussle and predicted a third consecutive BJP government in UP.
- India News
- 5 min read
Jaunpur: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya on Wednesday said the BJP contests elections on the "lotus flower" and that the party's Chief Minister will be decided by elected MLAs after the polls, while confirming that he supports incumbent CM Yogi Adityanath.
Asked about the BJP's face for the 2027 Assembly elections, Maurya said, "BJP's face at the time of elections is the lotus flower, and elections are contested based on the lotus flower. After the elections, when MLAs are elected, their meeting is held, and central observers arrive. Based on that meeting, whoever is decided unanimously then leads. At present, our Chief Minister is Yogi Adityanath ji. Whether Yogi ji or someone else will be Chief Minister in the future, I cannot decide. The MLAs elected at that time will decide it."
Asked directly whether he supports Yogi Adityanath, Maurya replied, "Yes, I do."
When asked if he could himself be a contender, he said, "No individual decides this. SP, BSP, and Congress are private limited companies. We have a system here. Whenever the leader of the legislative party is chosen, central observers come after the election. Whatever happens, you will find out in 2027."
Advertisement
On Congress MP Imran Masood's remark that his party was not "begging" for seats, Maurya said it made no difference to the BJP.
"Whether Imran Masood ji is upset, Rahul Gandhi is upset, or Aradhana ji is upset, what does it have to do with us? Whether they fight and clash among themselves or stay united, it makes no difference to BJP's health," he said.
Advertisement
"Out of 100, 60 per cent of the votes are ours. The remaining 40 per cent is divided, and even in that divided share we have a portion, because the BJP's double-engine government is working with 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas'," he added.
Commenting on the SP-Congress seat-sharing talks, he said, "SP has shown Congress its standing; now let Congress show SP its standing. Whether their deal cooks up or not, it makes no difference to us."
Maurya claimed the Opposition's defeat was certain. "Whether the INDI alliance contests together or without an alliance, their complete defeat in Uttar Pradesh is certain, and the formation of a BJP government for the third time is certain," he said.
"In Jaunpur alone, the BJP will win double the number of seats compared to last time. Their political future in Uttar Pradesh is in darkness until 2047. BJP is in the present, and BJP will remain in the future," he added.
Maurya's remarks came amid a public exchange between Congress leader Imran Masood and SP leaders over the ongoing seat-sharing discussions. Masood had objected to the SP announcing five candidates while alliance talks were underway, asserting that Congress had neither asked for 26 seats nor sought specific constituencies.
"We were in the midst of discussions within the alliance. Alliance meetings took place in Delhi, and following those meetings, if a declaration is made in this manner--it is claimed that we asked for 26 seats. We never even asked you for 26 seats. We are not beggars," Masood had said.
In response, SP Lok Sabha MP Rajeev Rai urged Masood to exercise restraint and said alliance partners should maintain decorum in their public statements.
"Why is he saying this? The selection of words should be appropriate. One should speak in the spirit of an alliance," Rai had said.
Rai denied that the SP had taken any unilateral decision, maintaining that the party had clarified from the beginning that seats held by sitting legislators would not be part of the discussions. He also said the party leadership was capable of resolving differences through talks.
The seat-sharing discussions are taking place ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The SP has offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of negotiations, while the Congress has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, as per party sources. The next meeting is likely to take place on November 27, sources said.
Earlier, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had asked Congress to identify additional potential constituencies beyond the 26 seats on its priority list and called for consensus candidates under the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework.
The SP has announced five candidates in its first list: Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mehboob Ali from Amroha and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur.
In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, which the SP and Congress contested independently, the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested, while Congress secured two of the 399 seats it contested.
The two parties subsequently contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections together under the INDIA bloc. The SP won 37 of the 62 seats it contested, while Congress won six of the 17 seats it contested in the state.

title: Winter Chill Grips Delhi, Air Quality Remains ‘Poor’ with Overall AQI at 228
description: The Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider restricting vehicles operating in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to those complying with Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission norms as part of measures to combat worsening air pollution in the region.
author: Namya Kapur
content:
Winter Chill Grips Delhi, Air Quality Remains ‘Poor’ with Overall AQI at 228
The Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider restricting vehicles operating in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to those complying with Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission norms as part of measures to combat worsening air pollution in the region.
- India News
- 5 min read
New Delhi: Air quality in the national capital remained in the 'poor' category on Wednesday morning, with Delhi recording an overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of 228 at 7 am, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Several areas of the national capital continued to experience poor air quality, with Anand Vihar recording an AQI of 336 and the area around Akshardham temple registering 327, both falling in the 'very poor' category.
Chandni Chowk recorded an AQI of 275, while IIT Delhi registered 254 and Vivek Vihar recorded 251, placing these areas in the 'poor' category. Meanwhile, the air quality around India Gate and Kartavya Path was comparatively better, with an AQI of 161, falling in the 'moderate' category.
Other areas, including Badarpur (181), Dwarka Sector 8 (173), IGI Airport Terminal 3 (191), RK Puram (188) and Uttam Nagar (173), also recorded AQI levels in the 'moderate' category. According to CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor' and 401-500 'severe'.
Despite the deteriorating air quality in several parts of the city, visibility around India Gate and Kartavya Path remained clear, with visitors saying that the winter chill was gradually intensifying. Arvind Kumar, who had come from Greater Noida to visit India Gate, said that he visited the monument after a long time to experience the winter weather in the national capital.
Advertisement
"We live in Greater Noida. But after a long time, we felt like visiting India Gate, the pride of Delhi, and experiencing the winter weather here for ourselves. We also wanted to guide others on how to visit. You can see India Gate clearly right now," he told ANI. Highlighting the visibility conditions, he said that visitors could get a clear view of India Gate and Kartavya Path, while advising people to carry warm clothes as temperatures were gradually falling.
"There are no visibility issues; both are clearly visible," he added. Another commuter, Ashish, who was travelling from Gurugram towards Noida, also spoke about the cold conditions and advised people to wear warm clothes. "It is very cold; keep your jacket and whatever else you have on. Keep your muffler and things like that on," he told ANI.
Advertisement
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi is expected to record a maximum temperature of 27 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature of 11 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, with mainly clear skies. The weather department has forecast "shallow fog" between November 25 and November 27, with the minimum temperature expected to reach 9 degrees Celsius.
Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider restricting vehicles operating in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to those complying with Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission norms as part of measures to combat worsening air pollution in the region.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed while hearing a matter concerning air pollution in the national capital."We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR," the Bench remarked. The Bench also suggested an alternative arrangement for the supply of essential commodities, proposing the establishment of warehouses at Delhi's borders where goods could be unloaded and subsequently transported into the city using smaller battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles.
Separately, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has introduced district-level action plans, setting a mandatory minimum target of 15 per cent reduction, with the potential to reach 20 per cent, in annual average air pollution levels across Delhi-NCR for 2027.
The Commission has written to the governments of Delhi and other NCR states, calling for comprehensive Annual Action Plans for 2027 at the State, District and Municipal Corporation levels. The plans aim to shift the focus from listing pollution-control activities to achieving measurable outcomes through defined targets, timelines, monitoring parameters and ground-level accountability.
Earlier, CAQM began assessing and ranking Delhi and neighbouring states on their performance in implementing pollution-control measures. Its 2026 report card, covering progress up to October, highlighted gaps in several areas, including industrial inspections, waste management, public transport and pollution-monitoring infrastructure.
According to the report card, none of the four states and Delhi had established the targeted number of green crematoriums. Against a combined target of 421 across Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, the achievement stood at zero as of October 31.
Industrial inspections also recorded significant shortfalls. Against a combined annual target of 11,607 inspections across the four states, only 2,584 had been completed by October 31.
While Delhi exceeded its target by conducting 1,609 inspections against 979, Haryana completed 177 of its 3,865 targeted inspections. Rajasthan recorded 68 inspections against 2,974, while Uttar Pradesh completed 730 against 3,789. The CAQM has classified performance of 100 per cent as satisfactory, achievement between 75 per cent and less than 100 per cent as needing improvement, and progress below 75 per cent as unsatisfactory.
The final report card for 2026 is scheduled to be released in January 2027, allowing states and the Delhi government to accelerate the implementation of pollution-control measures during the remaining period of the year.

title: Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
description: Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
author: Tanishq.Priya
content:
Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days.
This information was provided in response to an RTI query to AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute.
Under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, data regarding lung cancer cases and associated deaths between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, were requested from the hospitals. Safdarjung Hospital only provided the number of lung cancer deaths but did not disclose the total number of cases.
A request was also made for data on patients who had never smoked. However, none of the institutes provided any data on it.
According to information provided in response to separate RTI applications filed by PTI Bhasha, 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded across three of the four hospitals (excluding Safdarjung), averaging 83 cases per month. Across all four hospitals, 913 deaths were reported, which translates to one patient dying every three days.
The national capital is currently grappling with a severe air pollution crisis, an annual affair now in November, which is observed as the Lung Cancer Awareness Month.
Although health experts state that long-term exposure to air pollution increases the risk of lung cancer, it is not the sole cause. Smoking and genetic mutations are two of the other contributing factors.
The highest number of cases was recorded at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). This central government hospital provided data for the period from January 2020 to March 2026, during which 4,860 cases of lung cancer were registered and 158 deaths occurred. This averages to approximately 65 cases per month, with two patient deaths occurring monthly.
According to data from the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), 1,613 cases of lung cancer were reported between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, resulting in 354 deaths. This translates to an average of 20 cases per month, with four patient deaths occurring monthly during this period.
The institute noted that in 2021, the disease was also diagnosed in two children, and over a span of about six and a half years, 351 women were found to be suffering from lung cancer. However, it did not provide a gender-segregated breakdown of the deaths.
Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital reported 108 cases of lung cancer during this period, including 47 women, with eight deaths recorded. Safdarjung Hospital reported 393 deaths among patients suffering from lung cancer during the same timeframe.
A senior doctor at the DSCI, speaking to PTI on the condition of anonymity, mentioned that the institute receives patients not only from Delhi but also from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, and even Nepal.
Regarding the role of air pollution in Delhi on lung cancer cases, the doctor said the primary cause is smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke, though genetic mutations also play a role.
According to doctors, lung cancer has also been detected in non-smoking women; this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution.
Doctors also said that the disease is often diagnosed only in its final stages, making treatment extremely challenging.
Dr Geeta Kadayaprath, a senior specialist at the Apollo Athenaa Women’s Cancer Centre, said that long-term exposure to polluted air—common in cities like Delhi—can increase the risk of lung cancer.
She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), under the World Health Organization, has classified outdoor air pollution and the particulate matter it contains as carcinogenic to humans.
She explained that PM 2.5 particles are so minute that they can penetrate deep into the lungs and, over time, cause damage to cells.
When asked about symptoms, Dr Vikas Maurya, a senior specialist at Fortis Hospital in Shalimar Bagh, explained that there are often no clear symptoms in the early stages.
However, potential warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, changes in one’s voice, unexplained weight loss, and recurring chest infections.
He further noted that the condition cannot be detected through a standard X-ray; instead, a CT scan is required for diagnosis.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by Firstpost staff.)

title: How safe is bottled water? How chemicals in Bisleri put the $4 billion industry in the spotlight
description: Bisleri is in hot water after a sample was found to contain carcinogenic chemicals, bromate and PAHs, above the prescribed limit, prompting India’s food safety regulator to sanction prosecution. The findings have also put the entire packaged water industry under scrutiny, with the FSSAI warning of more tests of all brands
author: FP Explainers
content:
How safe is bottled water? How chemicals in Bisleri put the $4 billion industry in the spotlight
Bisleri is in hot water after a sample was found to contain carcinogenic chemicals, bromate and PAHs, above the prescribed limit, prompting India’s food safety regulator to sanction prosecution. The findings have also put the entire packaged water industry under scrutiny, with the FSSAI warning of more tests of all brands
When one thinks Bisleri, one thinks of pure water.
However, that notion is facing a huge cloud of suspicion after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against the packaged drinking water brand over an ‘unsafe’ sample.
This finding isn’t just a problem for Bisleri International but also for the country’s $4 billion packaged drinking water industry. We explain why.
Why is Bisleri facing prosecution?
On Sunday (November 22), India’s food safety regulator sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after a sample collected from its premises was found unsafe.
According to the FSSAI, the sample of water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. After the company appealed, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory. FSSAI said the laboratory also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
For those who don’t know, bromate and PAHs are both carcinogens, meaning they can cause or increase the risk of cancer.
How did Bisleri respond to FSSAI’s findings?
As Bisleri found itself in hot water, the brand issued a statement on Monday (November 23), maintaining that its water is “safe for consumption”.
It explained that the matter pertained to a sample taken from a batch in September 2025 from its Goa plant, one among its 143. The company added that FSSAI drew six samples there on 30 September 2025. Five passed all checks, while the sixth showed bromate at 12 microgrammes per litre, above the permitted 10.
Bisleri said it appealed in November 2025, and FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory. That lab found bromate within the limit but flagged polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). The mismatch, Bisleri said, “raised questions that Bisleri believed warranted clarification.”
The company adds in its statement that it then had the same sample tested at an FSSAI-approved lab, which also found bromate within the limit. Bisleri sent those results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office in February this year.
Bisleri adds that its submissions were met with silence and that they “received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed”.
“Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process and will continue to cooperate with FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process. A trusted brand for years, Bisleri remains safe for consumption,” the company said.
Will the latest findings shake public’s trust in Bisleri?
The FSSAI’s finding of bromate and PAHs in the Bisleri sample has led many to question if Bisleri’s water is safe to drink.
One Pune resident was quoted by the Times of India as saying, “For years, during train journeys and other travel, I would check whether I’d been sold the real ‘Bisleri’ or a fake ‘Bislery’ or ‘Besleri.’ Now it seems the problem is with the original.”
Another user wrote on X, “Do bisleri bachi hui hain, khatam karu ya nahi #FSSAI.”
As questions began to grow about the safety of Bisleri, shopkeepers also noted a change in buying patterns. “Once people lose confidence, they will think twice before purchasing. We are already seeing people asking for other drinking water brands,” said Ramesh Gupta, a local grocery store owner in Pune, to Times of India.
Even brand experts noted that such FSSAI’s action could hurt the trust that Bisleri has built over the years. Ganapathy Viswanathan, an independent communication consultant and author, was quoted as saying, “A brand like Bisleri does not build its reputation overnight. It has taken years of advertising, distribution and consumer confidence to reach where it is today.”
He noted that even though people don’t understand PAHs and bromate, the fact that Bisleri’s safety is being questioned may force people to move to other brands.
Harish Bijoor, brand and business strategist, was also quoted telling Open, “A brand is a trust statement. And to that extent, when that trust is questioned or shaken, consumers tend to reassess their ability to want that exact brand. I do believe this is going to suffer the downside of this FSSAI issue, and rightly so.”
Why does the action against Bisleri matter to the industry?
The action against Bisleri is significant for the country’s packaged drinking water market.
That’s because Bisleri International is the most dominant brand in this space. It controls 36 per cent of the industry whereas competitors like Aquafina trail at 20 per cent, and Kinley at 15 per cent. The remaining 29 per cent of the industry is held by smaller names or unbranded packaged drinking water.
Following Sunday’s findings, the FSSAI announced that it plans to test more Bisleri samples from across the nation. The FSSAI also said it would initiate legal proceedings against Bisleri.
In fact, Goa’s Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) has already stepped up against packaged drinking water in the state. FDA Director Shweta S Dessai said she has instructed officials to collect samples of different packaged water brands manufactured and sold in Goa for testing.
In Gujarat, Minister of State for Health Praful Pansheriya also told IANS that his department would step up inspections of all those who produce packaged drinking water. “Three to four days ago, my department issued instructions that starting tomorrow, wherever there are plants in Gujarat and wherever local bottled water is produced, both cleanliness and norms need to be checked, and this campaign of ours will be carried out across Gujarat.”
And the scrutiny isn’t going to be limited to just Bisleri. The FSSAI plans to conduct inspections of other packaged drinking water companies. As a government source said, “The whole industry is under the scanner now.”
This, according to Ankur Bisen, a partner at consulting firm The Knowledge Company, will result in all companies ensuring that their products comply with FSSAI norms.
Only time will tell if packaged drinking water is indeed safe in India.
With inputs from agencies

title: Who is the man in the photograph PM Modi gifted to Nepal PM Balen Shah?
description: PM Modi's gift collection for Balen Shah included a framed photograph, Gangajal from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade stole in a traditional Gujarati Sadeli box and a Kalamkari painting of the Ramayana. One of these gifts came with a story of its own
author: FP News Desk
content:
Who is the man in the photograph PM Modi gifted to Nepal PM Balen Shah?
PM Modi's gift collection for Balen Shah included a framed photograph, Gangajal from Varanasi, a Banarasi brocade stole in a traditional Gujarati Sadeli box and a Kalamkari painting of the Ramayana. One of these gifts came with a story of its own
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's gifts to Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah ranged from Gangajal (sacred ganges water) and a Banarasi brocade stole to a Kalamkari artwork depicting the Sampoorna Ramayana (the complete story of the Ramayana). One present, however, stood apart from the rest.
It was a framed photograph from Gujarat that took Balen Shah back to his late father's postgraduate years. The photograph was of Dr Ram Narayan Shah at Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar.
Dr Ram Narayan Shah was an Ayurvedic physician who spent much of his professional life in Nepal's public healthcare system. From his early years in Mahottari to his postgraduate education in India and his decades of service in Kathmandu, his journey was rooted in the practice and promotion of traditional medicine.
From Mahottari to Jamnagar: The making of an Ayurvedic physician
Born in 1948 in Ekdara, in Nepal's Mahottari district, Ram Narayan Shah was the son of Muni Lal Shah, a local landowner and influential figure in the community. He grew up in Nepal's Terai region, where his family had agricultural and social ties, as per a profile published on him by Al Jazeera.
Shah chose to pursue a career in Ayurveda, the traditional system of medicine practised across the Indian subcontinent. His search for advanced training took him to India, where he enrolled for postgraduate studies at Gujarat Ayurveda University in Jamnagar.
The institution, now known as the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, is a prominent centre for Ayurvedic education and research. Shah's years in Jamnagar in the late 1970s became a significant chapter in his life.
A career in Nepal's public healthcare system
After completing his studies in India, Shah returned to Nepal in the early 1980s and moved to Kathmandu with his family. He joined the government as an Ayurvedic physician and was assigned to Singha Durbar Vaidhyakhana, one of Nepal's oldest state-run institutions dedicated to the preparation and distribution of Ayurvedic medicines.
The institution has a long history in Nepal's traditional medicine system. It was established to prepare medicines for the royal household and the wider public, and has continued to play a role in the country's public healthcare network.
Shah spent several decades working in the government healthcare system. His career eventually took him to the top of the institution. Between 2001 and 2005, he served as the managing director of Singha Durbar Vaidhyakhana, overseeing an organisation responsible for producing traditional medicines and making them available to the public.
His work placed him within Nepal's efforts to preserve and develop its Ayurvedic healthcare system, even as modern medicine became increasingly widespread.
His ties to his hometown
Despite spending much of his professional life in Kathmandu, Shah retained close links with his ancestral home in Ekdara, Mahottari. He continued visiting the area and remained involved in community initiatives.
Reports in The Rising Nepal have noted his contributions to his hometown, including donating land for a weekly community market, locally known as a hatiya, and supporting the upkeep of a local temple.
These contributions reflected a connection to the community where he had grown up. Beyond his career in public service, Shah was remembered for supporting local infrastructure and religious institutions in his native village.
A legacy carried forward by his family
Dr Ram Narayan Shah died on December 1, 2025, at the age of 77 at Civil Hospital in Kathmandu. He was survived by his wife, Dhurba Devi Shah, and their children, including his youngest son, Balen Shah.
His death came months before his son became Nepal's prime minister. Balen, who first rose to prominence as a rapper and later became the mayor of Kathmandu, went on to take the country's top political office.
What are the big takeaways from the Modi-Balen Shah talks?
The high-level talks between PM Modi and Balen Shah delivered a series of major announcements covering development assistance, connectivity, energy and bilateral cooperation.
India announced a development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepal's reconstruction and development, including in the aftermath of severe floods. The two sides also signed eight memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering satellite communications, civil servant training, healthcare, Ayurveda, forensic sciences and livestock development.
Connectivity featured prominently in the discussions. The leaders launched the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in India with Janakpur Dham in Nepal. They also inaugurated the Dharchula-Darchula motorable bridge and dedicated Phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline, aimed at strengthening cross-border transport and energy links.
The two countries also stepped up cooperation in the energy sector. The foundation stones were laid for the 669 MW Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project and an oil storage terminal in Jhapa.

title: Meta delegation meets Congress as protests intensify over content curbs
description: Meta's Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday
author: Reuters
content:
Meta delegation meets Congress as protests intensify over content curbs
Meta's Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday
Listen to This Article
\Meta's top executives in India held closed-door talks with the country's opposition Congress party as the two sides try to defuse escalating tensions over the US firm's content moderation practices, four people familiar with the matter said.
The talks show how Mark Zuckerberg's company is caught between Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, which has stepped up demands to remove online content ‌it deems illegal, and an opposition accusing it of bias, the latest challenge for Meta in India, its biggest market by users.
Meta's Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday, one person said.
They raised concerns about protests targeting Meta's offices and the depiction of CEO Zuckerberg in posters. Congress raised concerns about a rise in restrictions on its leaders' accounts and posts, and about allegations that Meta favours Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), three other people said. Meta has denied any favouritism.
The meeting marked Meta's first direct engagement with the party since protests by its youth wing began on Friday.
Also Read
The Youth Congress has demanded that Meta restore accounts taken down on government orders and explain how its algorithms restrict posts, and its members have clashed with ‌police near Meta's offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram.
Congress did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Meta said it moderates content in India in accordance with the law. Meta executives Jain and Jog did not respond.
POSTERS TARGETING ZUCKERBERG
During the meeting, which lasted more than 40 minutes, Meta said some of the removals were the result of its policy on AI-generated content, one of the people said.
Congress countered by citing examples of BJP posts that were also generated using AI but had not been taken down, and told the executives that Meta's takedown policy appeared arbitrary, the person said.
Meta made no commitments to the party during the meeting and explained that it was bound by local laws, said a second source. The executives also emphasised ‌that Meta was neutral towards all political parties, the person added.
The dispute adds to political pushback for Meta in India, where it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts under local laws in the first half of 2026, up from about ‌70,000 in all of 2025, company disclosures show.
Meta attributes the rise to India's amended IT rules that require faster and more proactive ‌takedowns, but it has triggered a debate over free speech as the government steps up demands to remove online content.
The protests took a fresh turn in recent days as posters and banners depicting Zuckerberg in a white shirt, khaki shorts ‌and black cap, the traditional uniform of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), appeared in cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Patna, Mumbai and Bengaluru. The RSS is a Hindu nationalist volunteer organisation that is the ideological parent of the BJP.
"This is Congress Model: Vandalise ‌offices of private companies," BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wrote on X on Saturday.

title: Deepam row: TN apologises to SC over failure to light lamp at Deepathoon
description: The state told the Supreme Court that the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to light the ceremonial lamp on November 24, despite arrangements by the district admin
author: Press Trust of India
content:
Deepam row: TN apologises to SC over failure to light lamp at Deepathoon
The state told the Supreme Court that the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to light the ceremonial lamp on November 24, despite arrangements by the district admin
Listen to This Article
The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised to the Supreme Court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hill on November 24, claiming the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise a team proposed for carrying out the exercise.
In a status report filed by Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna before a bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, the state government said the district administration had completed all arrangements for implementing the apex court's November 20 order permitting the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon through a restricted team authorised by the temple administration.
However, the order of the apex court could not be complied with because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed for carrying out the exercise and instead resolved to follow the customary practice of lighting the Karthigai Mahadeepam at its traditional location, the state government claimed in the report.
"I submit that I took all the steps to comply with the order in good faith. There has been no wilful deliberate disobedience on my part of any directions of this Hon'ble Court. I hold the orders of the Hon'ble Court in the highest respect and remain committed to comply with every direction this Hon'ble Court may issue.
"I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon. However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated November 24, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place. I submit that I will submit an additional status report with all supporting documents along with the same," the status report said.
Also Read
The District Collector said the administration made every effort to secure authorisation of Devasthanam for lighting of lamp at Deepathoon.
The top court fixed the main plea against the Madras High Court order permitting lighting of ceremonial lamp for final hearing in January next year.
The bench may take up the contempt plea, if any, filed in the matter.

title: SC seeks Delhi Police response on bail pleas of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
description: The Supreme Court sought Delhi Police's response to the activists' bail pleas in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots conspiracy case, saying it would consider interim relief after hearing the police
author: Press Trust of India
content:
SC seeks Delhi Police response on bail pleas of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
The Supreme Court sought Delhi Police's response to the activists' bail pleas in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots conspiracy case, saying it would consider interim relief after hearing the police
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused, as of now, interim bail to activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, who had challenged a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in a UAPA case related to the alleged "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response.
During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail in the meantime.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Imam, also sought similar relief on grounds of long incarceration.
However, the bench said, "Not today".
Also Read
It said it will hear the police before considering the prayer for interim bail.
The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration.
In their pleas before the top court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.
Violence erupted in northeast Delhi during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).
Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.

title: Mahadev betting app scam: Why ED arrested Delhi lawyer over alleged  ₹15 crore payment from kingpin Saurabh Chandrakar
description: The ED has arrested Delhi lawyer Himanshu Shekhar over an alleged  ₹15 crore payment from Mahadev betting app kingpin Saurabh Chandrakar to influence judges and officials. A Raipur court has remanded him to ED custody till November 28.
author: Bhanu Pratap
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested a Delhi-based lawyer for allegedly receiving more than ₹15 crore from Saurabh Chandrakar, the alleged mastermind of the Mahadev online betting app scam, on the promise of influencing judges, advocates and government officials connected with the case, according to a PTI report. The accused, Himanshu Shekhar, was reportedly remanded to the ED's custody until November 28 by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Raipur late Monday night. The remand came hours after the Bombay High Court set aside a Mumbai court order that had rejected the agency's request for his transit remand. ED counsel Sourabh Kumar Pande told PTI that Chandrakar had named Shekhar during his custodial interrogation and alleged that the lawyer had promised to manage people in the government and judicial system, including judges and advocates. According to the agency cited by PTI, Chandrakar told investigators that he had paid Shekhar ₹15 crore, followed by additional amounts in smaller instalments. The ED subsequently issued a lookout circular (LOC) against the lawyer to prevent him from leaving the country. Shekhar was reportedly detained by immigration officials at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport around 3 pm on November 20, when he was scheduled to board a flight to Dubai. He was subsequently handed over to the Customs Department, which informed the ED about the lookout circular, Pande said. An ED team from Raipur reached Mumbai and took Shekhar into custody at around 1.10 am on November 21. After questioning him, the agency produced him before a special court in Mumbai at approximately 2.45 pm the same day and sought transit remand to take him to Raipur for further investigation. However, the Mumbai court rejected the application, citing procedural grounds. According to the ED's counsel, the court observed that Shekhar should have been produced during the first session of working hours rather than towards the end of the 24-hour period. The dispute also involved the calculation of the period of detention. The ED maintained that the clock began ticking at 1.10 am on November 21, when its officials formally took Shekhar into custody. The Mumbai court, however, considered his detention to have started at 3.03 pm on November 20, when immigration officials first detained him under the LOC. The court subsequently directed Shekhar to appear before the ED's Raipur office on November 23. The ED challenged the Mumbai special court's decision before the Bombay High Court, which quashed the order on Monday, clearing the way for the agency to proceed with the arrest in Raipur. Shekhar's lawyer, Faizal Rizvi, disputed the ED's account of the subsequent events. Rizvi claimed that the agency had told the Bombay High Court that his client failed to appear before its Raipur office, whereas Shekhar had actually reached the office at 4.25 pm on Monday. He further said that Shekhar was arrested after reaching the office. The defence has also approached the special court in Raipur seeking directions to preserve CCTV footage and entry registers of the ED office. According to Rizvi, these records could be produced before the Supreme Court in any future legal proceedings. The alleged payment to Shekhar is linked to the wider investigation into the Mahadev online betting app network. Chandrakar, who was extradited from Oman earlier this month following an operation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), is currently lodged in Raipur Central Jail in judicial custody. The ED has alleged that illegal betting operations through the Mahadev app and associated money-laundering activities continued, with the total proceeds of crime estimated to have exceeded ₹92,000 crore. Investigative agencies have alleged that Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal, both natives of Bhilai in Chhattisgarh's Durg district, promoted the Mahadev Book App and ran an online betting network through a system of panel and branch operators. The alleged network involved payments described as protection money to police personnel, administrative officials and influential political figures to facilitate its operations. According to investigative agencies, Chandrakar and other promoters operated from Dubai, which they allegedly treated as the network's headquarters. The promoters are accused of recruiting several youths from Chhattisgarh to work as managers, supervisors and other staff members to run the betting operations. The alleged network functioned through multiple panels and branches, allowing betting activities to be conducted across locations. The ED's investigation has reportedly focused on the alleged generation and laundering of proceeds from these operations, as well as the suspected involvement of officials and influential individuals who may have helped the network function. With inputs from PTI report. Bhanu Pratap is a journalist who reports and writes on foreign affairs, India’s foreign policy, geopolitics and strategic affairs. He closely follows diplomatic developments in New Delhi and has a keen interest in defence and national security.

Bhanu also focuses on in-depth, interview-based reports and regularly speaking with experts and policymakers to bring perspectives and context to major developments around the world.

He is also interested in stories with strong humanitarian angles.

One such report examined the cases of Indian nationals who were allegedly recruited and forced into Russia’s war against Ukraine. While reporting the story, Bhanu spoke to the families of those affected and documented their experiences. The report was later taken into account by the United Nations in its findings on human rights violations linked to the war in Ukraine.

For Bhanu, the zeal to produce meaningful and impactful journalism remains at the heart of his work.

He has previously worked with Firstpost, NDTV, Newslaundry and Republic.

Bhanu studied at the Delhi School of Journalism, University of Delhi. He initially chose science with plans to pursue engineering, influenced by conventional expectations, but fate had other plans and eventually led him to journalism.

Beyond the newsroom, Bhanu enjoys exploring culture and history and often spends his days off on heritage walks. He is also passionate about travelling, biking and listening to folk music.

title: Vantara signs 10-year wildlife conservation pact with Madagascar to repatriate trafficked animals — All we know
description: Under the agreement, Vantara will assist in the safe return of Malagasy animals seized overseas and support their rescue, rehabilitation, and veterinary care.
author: Livemint
content:
Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar to help bring animals seized abroad back to their home country, support their rehabilitation, and, where possible, return them to the wild.
The Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre Society (Vantara), based in Jamnagar, Gujarat, and Madagascar’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD) signed the non-exclusive Memorandum of Understanding on wildlife conservation and animal welfare on November 24.
The deal fulfils a commitment Vantara made to India’s CITES Management Authority on August 19. Under the agreement, Vantara will assist in the safe return of Malagasy animals seized overseas and support their rescue, rehabilitation, and veterinary care.
Beyond repatriation, the partnership focuses on building Madagascar’s domestic conservation capacity. Vantara will help train local wildlife experts and may support the construction and establishment of a National Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre.
Planned as a national hub for conservation, research, and training, the centre will remain the property of the Republic of Madagascar and operate under MEDD’s authority on government-provided land.
Madagascar is home to species found nowhere else on Earth, many of which are under severe threat. According to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, 90% of lemur species in the country are threatened with extinction, and nearly a third are Critically Endangered.
The country’s radiated tortoises face a similar crisis. The Turtle Survival Alliance estimates their wild population dropped by more than 47% between the late 1990s and 2013. Madagascar also lost roughly 29% of its tree cover between 2001 and 2023.
Illegal wildlife trade compounds the problem, with Madagascar’s environment minister describing it as the second leading cause of biodiversity decline after habitat loss. Between January and April 2026 alone, rescuers in the country received more than 1,000 tortoises from six confiscation cases.
Bringing seized animals home is often a slow and complicated process. When Thai authorities intercepted 48 lemurs and more than 1,000 tortoises in 2024, 131 tortoises had already died in transit, and others did not survive the weeks that followed.
While Thailand cared for the surviving animals and backed their return, there was no dedicated funding, and complex international permit procedures delayed flights back to Madagascar twice.
Under the new pact, Vantara’s teams can assist at Madagascar’s request across different stages of an animal’s return, including health checks, disease screening, transport, quarantine, and post-arrival care.
Vantara will also share scientific expertise, such as field research and genetic profiling, to help Madagascar decide which animals can be released into the wild and where, in line with IUCN guidelines.
Every final decision will rest solely with the Government of Madagascar, advised by the country's CITES Scientific Authority.
Through training, internships, specialist exchanges, and applied research, the partnership aims to ensure local teams can sustain conservation work long after rescued animals return.
“Madagascar is a biodiversity hotspot of global importance, and our wildlife is part of who we are as a nation. These animals belong to the forests that shaped them,” said H.E. Nolave Luck Aristide Andriatsihala, Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development, Republic of Madagascar.
“Protecting them takes cooperation across borders, and we are grateful to the countries and organisations, such as Vantara, who work with us to safeguard Madagascar's natural heritage,” Andriatsihala added.
MEDD’s Director General of Environmental Governance Rakotondravoninala Valison Kiady said the partnership will focus on practical execution. “Vantara brings world-class expertise in animal rescue, veterinary care and welfare, and we look forward to working together to turn this commitment into concrete actions, from immediate deliverables to long-term, results-oriented programmes, all guided by science, regulations and international best practice,” Kiady said.
Vantara Chief Executive Officer Vivaan Karani said the initiative reflects the organisation's focus on in situ conservation, or protecting animals in their natural home range.
“Madagascar is home to some of the world’s most extraordinary and unique wildlife, and protecting these species in their natural habitats is central to our ten-year conservation strategy,” Karani said. “Our priority is to strengthen the people and institutions working to conserve wildlife in its country of origin. We thank the Government of Madagascar for this partnership and look forward to supporting its long-term conservation priorities, with every decision resting firmly with Madagascar.”

title: Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Check fuel cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
description: Global oil prices steadied as traders balanced indications of rising global supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported.
author: Livemint
content:
Petrol and diesel prices today, November 25: Petrol and diesel prices have remained largely steady across major cities despite a surge in global crude oil costs due to the US-Iran war, which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri attributed this to the Centre's strategy of cutting excise duties and managing domestic fuel supplies.
Here is a look at the petrol and diesel prices in major metropolitan cities as of November 25:
New Delhi: Petrol is retailing at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel is priced at ₹95.20 per litre. The national capital continues to have relatively lower fuel prices compared to other metros.
Mumbai: In the financial capital, petrol is priced at ₹111.21 per litre, and diesel costs ₹97.83 per litre.
Chennai: Residents in Chennai are paying ₹107.76 per litre for petrol and ₹99.55 per litre for diesel.
Kolkata: Petrol costs ₹113.51 per litre, while diesel costs ₹99.82 per litre.
Bengaluru: Petrol is priced at ₹110.44 per litre, and diesel at ₹99.56 per litre.
Hyderabad: Petrol costs ₹116.15 per litre, while diesel costs ₹104.23 per litre.
Source: GoodReturns
Oil prices steadied as traders balanced indications of rising global supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reported.
Brent crude traded around $91 a barrel after climbing 2.3% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) hovered below $82. On Tuesday, Iran claimed a fourth tanker was struck by a mine, according to the Fars news agency, extending a recent wave of vessel attacks by the Islamic Republic.
Tehran also warned it would tighten its grip over the Strait of Hormuz until its demands are met, Tasnim reported—highlighting that an end to the nearly nine-month conflict remains out of reach. Even so, crude shipments from the Persian Gulf have surged in recent months, prompting the International Energy Agency (IEA) to forecast that the market will tip into a surplus this quarter.
“The reality on the ground is more a ‘war but no war’ situation, with spasms of violence,” Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC, told Bloomberg. Under that scenario, “look for the supply surplus to become the dominant theme in coming weeks,” he added.
Brent has dropped sharply this month as Gulf exports climbed and US President Donald Trump held off on renewed strikes against Iran following the US midterm elections.
Adding to the downward pressure, a key timespread for the Middle East’s Dubai crude benchmark flipped into a bearish structure this week, signalling that supply is now outpacing demand, Bloomberg noted.

title: Execution of proclamation orders against Hafiz Saeed, five other 26/11 accused still awaited
description: The trial against Zabiuddin Ansari, the handler of the 26/11 terror attacks, is ongoing in Mumbai. Proclamation orders for six absconding terrorists, including Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, have yet to be executed. The Ministry of Home Affairs has not responded to requests for further action against these accused. Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam believes the perpetrators will ultimately be punished in India.
author: PTI
content:
Mumbai: While the trial in the 26/11 terror attacks is on against Zabiuddin Ansari alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists Hindi, steps to execute the proclamation orders against six other perpetrators, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken.
A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year. The court is currently conducting the trial against Jundal.
In August and September this year, the prosecution told the court that it had requested the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to serve the proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks case. However, the MHA has not responded to the request yet.
Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said that while there has been no development regarding the execution of the proclamation orders issued against the wanted accused, he assured that the perpetrators of the attacks would be punished in India.
"The prosecution will ensure that all those persons who facilitated the dastardly attacks would be punished on Indian soil," Nikam told PTI.
He said as per procedure, non-bailable warrants and Interpol Red Corner notices were issued through diplomatic channels against the absconding accused, who are the main perpetrators and conspirators behind the attacks.
"But I am sure that the Pakistan government will not respond as that country continues to be a haven for terrorists," Nikam said.
The prosecution had in August and September told the court that the MHA was requested to take necessary steps to serve the proclamation orders, through Interpol, against the accused believed to be residing in Pakistan.
Nikam had then told the court that amid the procedural compliance, the trial against the absconding accused would commence as Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 allows criminal trials in absentia for absconding proclaimed offenders, even where there is no immediate prospect of arrest.
The trial against Jundal, which had been on hold since 2018 pending a petition filed by government authorities over the furnishing of certain documents to the accused, commenced in November last year after clearance from the Bombay High Court.
Jundal is accused of not only having planned the attacks but also of personally training the 10 Pakistani terrorists who struck Mumbai on November 26, 2008, specifically teaching them Hindi and crucial details about Mumbai's topography to help them blend in.
Apart from Saeed and Lakhvi, the four other absconding accused are Sajid Mir, Abu Alqama, Asim alias Abu Qahafa, and Major Abdur Rehman Pasha.
The role of these men in the attack was revealed by Ajmal Kasab and accused-turned-approver David Headley.
A total of 166 people, including six Americans and other foreigners, were killed in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks in which 10 heavily armed Pakistani terrorists entered the financial capital via the Arabian Sea on the night of November 26, 2008, and laid a more than 60-hour siege at iconic and vital locations across the city.
Investigators alleged that Jundal played a key role as a handler of the terrorists. The sole terrorist caught alive, Ajmal Kasab, was convicted and sentenced to death by a special court in 2010 and was hanged in Pune's Yerwada Jail in November 2012.

title: Cardamom ad sparks clash between Bollywood star, India's food regulator
description: A legal conflict has emerged involving Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn and the Maharashtra food authority. The actor has been asked to discontinue advertisements for Vimal cardamom due to its link to a prohibited product. Maharashtra's food safety commissioner believes these advertisements promote unhealthy consumption behaviors. The case may establish important precedents regarding indirect advertising in India. A ruling against Devgn could impact endorsements for Bollywood actors significantly.
author: Reuters
content:
India restricts advertising for liquor and tobacco but officials have for years also frowned upon the use of indirect means, called surrogate advertising, by companies in such sectors promoting their brands in the guise of sodas, water or glassware.
Also Read: Over 74% organizations expect increase in wage cost under the Labour Codes: Grant Thornton Bharat’s Survey
While companies say these are genuine businesses in their own right whose advertising cannot be curbed, health officials say the advertisements are aimed at generating recall of the parent brand whose publicity is restricted. Since 2024, India has been trying to finalise stringent guidelines to prohibit such advertisements outright.
In the case involving Bollywood stars, actor Ajay Devgn has sued the food authority of Maharashtra state, arguing he has been wrongly told to stop appearing in advertisements for Vimal cardamom packs, according to a non-public court filing dated October 15 reviewed by Reuters.
Also Read: Delhi's clean air dream runs into reality as ambitious EV plan sputters
The state, whose food safety commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has become a national sensation for his aggressive stance on public health, asked Bollywood stars Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August to stop appearing in advertisements promoting Vimal cardamom, arguing the brand is mostly known for its betel nut mix, or pan masala, which is banned in the state.
The spat in the High Court in Mumbai could set a precedent, New Delhi-based lawyer Anuj Tiwari said. "The case will test both the fairness of the department's process before it imposes restrictions ... and the parameters for deciding what counts as indirect advertising," he said.
Court spat on cardamom ad
In the advertisement available on Vimal Cardamom's YouTube page and posted two years ago, the Bollywood stars are seen celebrating, throwing saffron at each other after Devgn consumes the product. The Hindi-language advertisement has 107 million views, while clips dubbed in other Indian languages have garnered millions more.
"Ajay, Shahrukh, and Tiger played saffron Holi like crazy and drenched the entire community in saffron!" says the advertisement's description, referring to the Hindu festival of colour.
Devgn in his filing argues cardamom has not been prohibited in the state and "there is no bar in endorsing a product which is not prohibited".
Devgn did not respond to Reuters queries. Mundhe told Reuters the state believes the advertisements are against public health interests, and the state is separately reviewing responses submitted by Khan and Shroff, although Reuters could not ascertain details of their submissions.
Dushyant Mahant, a lawyer for PB Agro, which holds the licence to make Vimal cardamom and pan masala, told Reuters the allegations were futile as the company does not promote Vimal in Maharashtra and only advertises the product via nationally televised broadcasts that cannot be restricted geographically.
Industry estimates show India's pan masala market was worth around $5 billion last year. Health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.
While Maharashtra bans it, Vimal's tobacco-free pan masala sachets in other states cost around 5 rupees (5.4 US cents). But they are often consumed with chewing tobacco, sold at kiosks as "twin packs" — a pan masala sachet alongside a tiny pouch of unbranded tobacco.
An adverse ruling in Devgn's case could affect Bollywood stars as endorsements can amount to up to 30% of an actor's earnings, and promoting tobacco-linked products is more lucrative than other advertisements, said Suresh Mathew, a Mumbai-based screenwriter.
"Most actors know if a product is a surrogate for another product," he added. "There are cases where certain actors have refused to lend their name to a product that they feel is harmful."
($1 = 92.4950 Indian rupees)

title: उमर खालिद और शरजील इमाम को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से झटका, अंतरिम जमानत देने से इनकार
description: उमर खालिद और शरजील इमाम को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से फिलहाल अंतरिम जमानत नहीं मिली है. कोर्ट ने दिल्ली पुलिस को नोटिस जारी किया है. कोर्ट ने कहा कि अंतरिम जमानत पर विचार करने से पहले वह दिल्ली पुलिस का पक्ष सुनेगा.
author: संजय शर्मा
content:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने उमर खालिद और शरजील इमाम को फिलहाल अंतरिम जमानत देने से इनकार कर दिया है. अदालत ने इस मामले में दिल्ली पुलिस को नोटिस जारी किया है और स्पष्ट किया है कि अंतरिम जमानत की अर्जी पर विचार करने से पहले वह दिल्ली पुलिस का पक्ष सुनेगी.
चीफ जस्टिस सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी मोहना की पीठ के समक्ष हुई सुनवाई के दौरान उमर खालिद और शरजील इमाम की ओर से पेश वरिष्ठ वकील कपिल सिब्बल और सिद्धार्थ दवे ने दोनों को अंतरिम राहत देने का अनुरोध किया था. अदालत ने फिलहाल ये अपील और दलील अस्वीकार कर दी.
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने बुधवार को 2020 के दिल्ली दंगों की बड़ी साजिश से जुड़े मामले में आरोपी पूर्व JNU स्कॉलर उमर खालिद की अंतरिम जमानत की मांग फिलहाल स्वीकार करने से इनकार कर दिया. कोर्ट ने स्पष्ट किया कि अभी अंतरिम जमानत नहीं दी जा सकती.
बता दें, दोनों आरोपी 2020 के दिल्ली दंगों से जुड़े यूएपीए (UAPA) मामले में छह साल से अधिक समय से जेल में बंद हैं. इससे पहले दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट और सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने जनवरी 2026 में भी उनकी जमानत याचिकाएं खारिज की हैं.
साल 2020 में उत्तर-पूर्वी दिल्ली में हुए दंगों में 53 लोगों की मौत हुई थी और 700 से ज्यादा लोग घायल हुए थे. यह हिंसा नागरिकता संशोधन कानून (CAA), 2019 और राष्ट्रीय नागरिक रजिस्टर (NRC) के खिलाफ हो रहे प्रदर्शनों के दौरान भड़की थी.
