title: Union Cabinet Okays Rs 2,014 Crore Doloo Greenfield Airport in Assam's Silchar
description: National | Silchar greenfield airport gets Rs 2,014 crore Cabinet approval. The Doloo project in Assam will handle 1.01 million passengers annually.
author: PratidinTime National Desk
content:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar, Assam, to be built by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs 2,014 crore, as the existing facility in the town has little room left to grow.
The proposal was cleared by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The current Silchar airport operates only as a civil enclave inside a defence-controlled airfield, which restricts its space and operations at a time when passenger numbers are rising steadily.
Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, briefing reporters after the meeting, said the project will be funded entirely from AAI's own internal resources. He added that the airport will have an annual capacity of 1.01 million passengers.
The new terminal building will cover 12,351 square metres and handle 800 passengers during peak hours. It will include modern passenger facilities and sustainable green building features, and can be expanded in modules as traffic grows. The project also includes a 2,705-metre-long, 45-metre-wide Code-4C runway suitable for A-320 aircraft, a new apron that can park six A-320 aircraft, and a separate isolation bay.
Doloo lies in Cachar district and sits at the heart of the Barak Valley, a region known for its tea gardens and agro-based industries, and with strong potential for eco and cultural tourism.
The government said the airport will serve growing air traffic in southern Assam and parts of neighbouring states, ease pressure on the existing infrastructure and give a boost to trade and tourism. It is also expected to better link Northeast India to national and international growth corridors.

title: 22-Year-Old Woman Alleges Gangrape After Late Night Party, 3 Arrested
description: National | A 22-year-old woman has alleged that she was gang-raped by two men after attending a late-night party at a cafe in Preet Vihar area, prompting police to arrest three people, including two women, in connection with the case.
author: PratidinTime News Desk
content:
A 22-year-old woman has alleged that she was gang-raped by two men after attending a late-night party at a cafe in the Preet Vihar area, prompting police to arrest three people, including two women, in connection with the case.
According to reports, six people, comprising four men and two women, have been named in the FIR. While three accused have been arrested, the remaining three are absconding, and efforts are underway to trace them.
Late-Night Party At Cafe Under Police Scanner
Preliminary investigation revealed that the survivor and the accused were employees of Cafe 8, located inside Cross River Mall in Karkardooma.
On Monday night, a group of eight people, including the woman, reportedly gathered at Saltanate Cafe in Preet Vihar for a party.
The cafe generally closes at 11.30 pm. However, one of the employees allegedly had access to its keys, allowing the group to reopen the establishment late at night and continue the gathering.
Police said the group allegedly consumed alcohol during the party before leaving the cafe at around 3.30 am.
The woman subsequently alleged that two men sexually assaulted her. She also claimed that other colleagues supported the accused during the incident.
Police Probe Underway, Three Accused Arrested
The woman did not approach the police immediately after the alleged assault. CCTV footage reportedly shows her leaving in a vehicle accompanied by a male friend and two other women.
She reached the police station at around 5.45 am on Tuesday and lodged a complaint.
Police have since registered an FIR against six people in connection with the alleged gangrape. Three accused, including two women, have been arrested, while a search is underway for the remaining three.
The survivor's statement is currently being recorded at the police station. Her statement will also be recorded before a magistrate as part of the ongoing investigation.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the alleged assault, the role of the accused and the events leading up to the complaint. The allegations are yet to be established through the investigation.

title: China's Mega Dam Near Arunachal Takes Shape, Satellite Images Reveal Scale
description: NATIONAL | It will involve tunnels stretching approximately 40 km through the region, including a passage beneath the Namcha Barwa Mountain, to utilise a river drop of more than 2,000 metres over a distance of about 50 km.
author: PratidinTime News Desk
content:
China's massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet, close to the Arunachal Pradesh border, has entered an advanced stage of construction, with fresh satellite imagery revealing extensive infrastructure development, cleared villages and river diversion work.
An assessment by EarthSense Labs, an Indian geospatial technology firm incubated at the Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer (FITT), IIT Delhi, has documented significant changes at the project site between July 2025 and August 2026.
The proposed 60,000-megawatt (60 GW) Medog hydropower project is being developed on the lower reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo, which enters India as the Siang in Arunachal Pradesh and flows into Assam as the Brahmaputra.
According to the assessment, the project is located around 40-50 km north of Arunachal Pradesh, close to the McMahon Line. Satellite images indicate that construction activities have progressed across multiple locations, including the proposed main dam site near Mainling.
The project is planned as a series of five hydropower stations, with an estimated investment of 1.2 trillion yuan, or around USD 168 billion. It will involve tunnels stretching approximately 40 km through the region, including a passage beneath the Namcha Barwa Mountain, to utilise a river drop of more than 2,000 metres over a distance of about 50 km.
The EarthSense assessment identified four major locations associated with the project: a proposed large dam near Mainling town, a lower dam possibly near Pai town, a tunnel through Namcha Barwa Mountain and a tunnel outlet near the India-China border, downstream of Medog County.
Satellite images from July 2025 showed villages and agricultural fields around the proposed Mainling dam site. By December that year, the settlements and fields had been cleared, and earthwork had started. Images from August 2026 further showed river diversion activities, new roads, temporary accommodation and office buildings, along with the relocation of entire villages.
India's proposed Siang project
The developments have drawn attention in India, particularly in view of the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh.
The proposed Indian project is planned further downstream along the Siang River, covering Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts. According to project proponents, its reservoir is expected to hold around 9.2 billion cubic metres of water and could help regulate river flows in the event of sudden changes in water discharge from upstream.
Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu has said the proposed reservoir would give India greater control over downstream water flows and help maintain water availability during lean seasons. He has also raised concerns over the absence of a binding water-sharing agreement and a transparent arrangement for sharing river data with China.
However, the proposed Siang project has faced opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community, who have expressed concerns over displacement, loss of land and the impact on traditional livelihoods.
Members of the community have approached Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the issue. Tensions also escalated during protests against the project's pre-feasibility survey, with violence reported in October.

title: Prasanth Nair Urges Ambani, Adani, Tata to Join Hands for India's Private Space Missions
description: Astronaut-designate Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair has urged Ambani, Adani, Tata and Mahindra groups to join hands to develop India's private human spaceflight capabilities, similar to Elon Musk's SpaceX.|Science/Tech | National | Top Stories|
author: DY365
content:
Prasanth Nair Urges Ambani, Adani, Tata to Join Hands for India's Private Space Missions
Astronaut-designate Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair has urged Ambani, Adani, Tata and Mahindra groups to join hands to develop India's private human spaceflight capabilities, similar to Elon Musk's SpaceX.
New Delhi: Astronaut-designate Air Commodore Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair has urged major Indian business groups to work together to develop private human spaceflight capabilities in the country.
Speaking at the India International Space Conclave on Monday, Nair suggested that industrial groups such as the Ambanis, Adanis, Tatas and Mahindras should form a consortium to take up ambitious space projects, similar to Elon Musk's SpaceX and its Crew Dragon programme.
He expressed hope that India could become the second country after the United States to achieve this through private sector participation.
Nair is one of the four astronaut-designates selected for India's Gaganyaan mission, which aims to send humans into space. The other three are Group Captains Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla.
Speaking about Gaganyaan, Nair said the first uncrewed test flight would be an important step towards sending astronauts into space. The mission will test the spacecraft's journey from launch to its return and recovery from the sea without carrying any human crew.
He added that the team is preparing safety procedures, communication systems and emergency plans for astronauts at every stage of the mission.
The first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight is expected next year, followed by more test missions before India attempts its first human spaceflight.

title: CJP’s Saurav Das Barred From Travelling To London For Oxford University Event
description: Das was scheduled to board a 1 am flight from Delhi to London to participate in a panel discussion at the prestigious University of Oxford | National | Top Stories
author: DY365
content:
CJP’s Saurav Das Barred From Travelling To London For Oxford University Event
Taking a sarcastic dig at the government, Das compared his situation with that of fugitive businessmen Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya, suggesting that he might have been allowed to travel had he been involved in financial wrongdoing
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das has alleged that he was stopped from travelling to London after immigration officials at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport informed him that his passport had been flagged by the authorities.
Das was scheduled to board a flight from Delhi to London at 1 am on Tuesday to participate in a panel discussion at the prestigious University of Oxford. He said he had been invited by the Indian Students' Union at the university to speak about the ongoing 'Cockroach Movement'. He was also expected to deliver talks at other reputed institutions, including the University of Cambridge, the London School of Economics (LSE) and the University of Edinburgh.
In a video message following the incident, Das questioned the government's decision and accused it of targeting him for his involvement in the movement.
"Why is the government actually afraid? An educated youth is going for an intellectual discussion with educated people," he said.
Taking a sharp and sarcastic dig at the government, Das compared his situation with fugitive businessmen Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya, questioning why he was being prevented from travelling abroad.
🚨This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement. Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions! @Cockroachisback
— Saurav Das (@SauravDassss) November 23, 2026
"I have spoiled my life. I wish I had been Nirav Modi or Vijay Mallya. I wonder if I could have looted a bank worth thousands of crores, the government might have allowed me to travel," he said.
He further alleged that young people like him did not believe in threatening others or engaging in hooliganism and criminal activities. Taking another swipe at the government, he said,
"We the youth don't have that mentality within us. We cannot threaten people, get involved in hooliganism, loot people, assault people or become a 'tadipar' (fugitive). That's why we are stopped and not allowed to travel outside the country or do some good work for the nation."
Das also claimed that Indian students at Oxford were interested in the Cockroach Movement and wanted to understand the developments taking place in the country. He alleged that the government was uncomfortable with the movement gaining attention beyond India's borders.
Calling the government "anti-intellectual", Das criticised its approach towards education and questioned the condition of public schools and the availability of public libraries in the country.
"This is an anti-intellectual government. They have nothing to do with education. First fix the schools in the country. Look at the condition of the schools we have. How many public libraries have been built in the country? None!" he said.
Das further alleged that the government was afraid of the movement and claimed that flagging a citizen's passport was an attempt to discourage those associated with it. However, he asserted that such actions would not weaken their resolve.
"They must know that they cannot bring down our spirit," he said.
The specific reason for Das's passport being flagged and the official response from the authorities were not available at the time of filing this report.

title: Home Ministry Warns WhatsApp Users Against Staying Logged In on Office Computers
description: The Union Home Ministry has warned WhatsApp users against leaving their accounts logged in on public or shared computers, as cybercriminals could misuse them to access private chats and carry out fraud. |National | Top Stories|
author: DY365
content:
Home Ministry Warns WhatsApp Users Against Staying Logged In on Office Computers
The Union Home Ministry has warned WhatsApp users against leaving their accounts logged in on public or shared computers, as cybercriminals could misuse them to access private chats and carry out fraud.
New Delhi: The Union Home Ministry has warned WhatsApp users not to leave their accounts logged in on computers, especially on shared or public devices. It said cybercriminals could use these open sessions to read private messages and misuse accounts to cheat others.
In its latest advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) said that an open WhatsApp Web account could allow strangers to read personal chats, see contact details and access group conversations. They could also send messages pretending to be the account owner and trick their friends and family members.
The agency has reminded users that simply closing the browser or WhatsApp Web tab does not log them out. Users must manually log out after every session to keep their accounts safe.
The advisory asks people to be careful while using WhatsApp Web on office computers, public computers or shared devices. It also advises users not to log in from cyber cafes, hotels and other public places. If using another computer is necessary, users should open WhatsApp Web in private or incognito mode.
The agency has also advised users not to share personal, financial or official information through WhatsApp Web on computers.
Users should regularly check their accounts for unusual activity, such as messages they did not send or strange replies from their contacts. These could be signs that someone else has accessed their account.
The I4C has also asked users to keep their computers, browsers and security software updated. It has warned against downloading unknown files or using cracked software.
The agency has urged everyone to follow these safety steps to protect their WhatsApp accounts and avoid online scams and financial fraud.

title: PM Narendra Modi Welcomes Shiromani Akali Dal’s Return to NDA
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday welcomed the Shiromani Akali Dal's (SAD) return to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), describing the BJP-SAD alliance as a natural partnership that would prioritise Punjab and the welfare of its people.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
‘Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’
New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday welcomed the Shiromani Akali Dal's (SAD) return to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), describing the BJP-SAD alliance as a natural partnership that would prioritise Punjab and the welfare of its people.
In a post on X, PM Modi expressed delight over the Akali Dal rejoining the NDA, particularly on the occasion of Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
"Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji," the Prime Minister said.
He described the BJP-SAD partnership as a natural alliance and said it would work towards ensuring pro-people governance and taking Punjab to new heights of progress.
"Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said. (ANI)

title: Bisleri Confirms FSSAI Re-Test Clears Disputed Goa Batch
description: Bisleri International on Tuesday welcomed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) clarification on November 23, stating that the sale prohibition applies only to one batch, GO 270, manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
New Delhi: Bisleri International on Tuesday welcomed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) clarification on November 23, stating that the sale prohibition applies only to one batch, GO 270, manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.
According to Bisleri, the explanation was sought for a single sample from a batch manufactured 14 months ago at its Goa plant. The company said it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that there are currently no stocks of the particular batch in the market.
Bisleri stated that the FSSAI had clarified on November 23 that bromates were found below the permissible limit upon re-testing of the sample from the batch in question.
According to the company's communication, "The FSSAI has categorically and conclusively clarified on 23rd November 2026 that bromates were found below the permissible limit on re-testing of the above batch sample."
Elaborating on the testing process, Bisleri said that six samples containing water from the same source were collected for testing and all six initially cleared the prescribed parameters. However, during the subsequent re-test, one out of the six samples reported PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre in Batch GO 270, while another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters. (ANI)

title: Saurav Das targets Centre after being ‘stopped’ from flying to London
description: After being barred from boarding his flight to London, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Saurav Das on Tuesday accused the Centre of stifling youth voices and resorting to administrative hurdles.
author: Sentinel Digital Desk
content:
‘Why is this govt so afraid?’
New Delhi: After being barred from boarding his flight to London, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Saurav Das on Tuesday accused the Centre of stifling youth voices and resorting to administrative hurdles.
While addressing a press conference here, he alleged that curbs were being imposed on expression across both physical and digital spaces.
"The world is watching how the voices of young people are being suppressed. Meta has deleted 6 million posts. We are being denied the freedom to express ourselves both on the streets and online. Akhilesh Yadav's Facebook account has also been deactivated," Das said.
"They are now raising questions about discrepancies in my passport. They cannot find anything against any of their so-called leaders and since they cannot use UAPA, ED or CBI against us, they are resorting to such petty tactics. If I were Nirav Modi or Mehul Choksi, a red carpet would have been rolled out for me instead. As you all know, I was supposed to travel to London, but unfortunately, that could not happen because of this cowardly government," he added.
Outlining the purpose of his scheduled trip, Das noted that he had intended to speak to students abroad about peaceful mobilisation.
"The invitation from the Oxford Union was the primary reason for my visit. Ratna was also invited. Indian students studying there wanted to understand what the CJP movement is all about. I wanted to go there and share my perspective on how such a large-scale movement evolved into a non-violent movement. There is considerable interest among Gen Z communities in several countries around the world to understand this," he said.
"I want to ask, why is this government so afraid? I would have spoken about the principles and ideals of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru.
It would have been an opportunity for the world to learn how such a massive movement can remain non-violent and draw strength from the principles of peaceful resistance," Das added.
This comes after Das alleged that he was stopped at Delhi Airport from travelling to London, where he was scheduled to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.
"I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford," Das informed earlier. (ANI)

title: 1 Feb 2026 · 1 min read New Aadhaar app dedicated to nation NEW DELHI, 31 Jan: Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada dedicated the new Aadhaar app to the nation on Wednesday, marking a significant milestone in identity verification keeping people at its core.…
description: NEW DELHI, 31 Jan: Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada dedicated the new Aadhaar app to the nation on Wednesday, marking a significant milestone in identity verification keeping people at its core.…
content:
NEW DELHI, 31 Jan: Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada dedicated the new Aadhaar app to the nation on Wednesday, marking a significant milestone in identity verification keeping people at its core.
Developed by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the Aadhaar app is a next-generation mobile application designed to provide Aadhaar number holders (ANH) with a secure, convenient and privacy-first way to carry, share, show and verify their digital identity.
After unveiling the new app, Prasada congratulated the UIDAI for the commendable work and underlined that Aadhaar remains a digital governance showpiece for the government. He said the UIDAI is making service delivery hassle-free and seamless, and the new app would accelerate the process further.
In his address, MeitY Secretary S Krishan said the new app would promote data minimisation and enhance security and promote selective sharing of information by Aadhaar number holders.
UIDAI Chairman Neelkanth Mishra said the journey from paper to paperless is great step forward and the UIDAI would keep people at the centre of its action and innovation.
UIDAI CEO Bhuvnesh Kumar said a key feature of the app is selective credential sharing. Residents can share only the specific identity fields required for a particular use case through customised QR codes generated by requesting entities.
This ensures that Aadhaar numbers are not stored by verifiers and only digitally signed verifiable credentials are shared, promoting data minimisation in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, he explained. (PIB)

title: 23 Jan 2026 · 2 min read ECINet digital platform launched at IICDEM NEW DELHI, 22 Jan: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday launched the Election Commission of India Network (ECINet) – its one-stop digital platform for all election-related information and services…
description: NEW DELHI, 22 Jan: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday launched the Election Commission of India Network (ECINet) – its one-stop digital platform for all election-related information and services…
content:
NEW DELHI, 22 Jan: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday launched the Election Commission of India Network (ECINet) – its one-stop digital platform for all election-related information and services – at the India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management (IICDEM), 2026.
The three-day conference is being held at Bharat Mandapam here.
The ECINet was envisaged by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India, Gyanesh Kumar, along with Election Commissioners (ECs) Dr Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Dr Vivek Joshi, and its development was announced in May 2025.
Speaking at the launch, the CEC said that the ECINethas been developed in strict accordance with the law and is available in 22 scheduled languages and English. He offered the EMBs of the world the opportunity to collaborate with India on the development of similar digital platforms for their countries, in accordance with their own laws, and in their respective languages.
EC Dr Sandhu said that ECINet is a great tool to enhance trust in EMB as it brings in greater transparency and helps monitor all functions and provides for quick decision-making and information dissemination.
EC Dr Joshi said that the conference would give EMBs an opportunity to learn and draw from global practices on the adoption of technology and digital innovations.
During her presentation, Information Technology Director General Dr Seema Khanna said that cybersecurity is one of the key pillars of the ECINet. She said that tech is no longer a support function but a strategic enabler. She added that the ECINet enhances transparency, efficiency, credibility, and public trust in elections.
The ECINet is the world’s largest electoral service platform, bringing all electoral services of the world’s largest democracy together in one seamless experience by integrating 40+ apps and portals of the Election Commission of India.
The platform has been developed in full compliance with the Constitution of India, the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961.
The ECINet connects citizens, candidates, political parties and election officials, and brings key services like voter registration, electoral roll search, ‘track your application’, ‘know your candidate’, connect with election officials, book-a-call with BLO, e-EPIC download, polling trends, grievance redressal, among others, onto one secure platform.
The beta version was successfully piloted during the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections and the special intensive revision (SIR), enabling the Election Commission to deliver enhanced citizen-centric electoral services and make available all election-related information at the click of a button.
Ahead of the launch, suggestions were sought from citizens before giving final shape to the platform.
Since the beta release, the ECINet has processed over 10 crore registration forms till date – an average of 2.7 lakh forms per day. More than 11 lakh booth level officers are registered on the platform. Over 150 crore documents have been digitised through this platform during SIR till date. The ECINet also provides a seamless mechanism for monitoring of ground level functionaries.

title: 7 Jan 2026 · 1 min read Journalist killed in Bangladesh, PEC demands thorough probe GENEVA, 6 Jan: Bangladesh, engulfed in political unrest while heading for its national election on 12 February, 2026, recorded the murder of journalist Rana Pratap Bairagi, who incidentally becomes the first…
description: GENEVA, 6 Jan: Bangladesh, engulfed in political unrest while heading for its national election on 12 February, 2026, recorded the murder of journalist Rana Pratap Bairagi, who incidentally becomes the first…
content:
GENEVA, 6 Jan: Bangladesh, engulfed in political unrest while heading for its national election on 12 February, 2026, recorded the murder of journalist Rana Pratap Bairagi, who incidentally becomes the first journo-victim across the world this year.
The global media safety and rights body, Press Emblem Campaign (PEC), strongly condemned the shooting down of Bairagi (45) and demanded a thorough probe to identify the culprits for punishment under the law.
Local media reports stated that Bairagi, a resident of Arua village in Jessore locality of south Bangladesh, was fatally shot in his head by three miscreants on 5 January. The editor of a Bengali newspaper titled Dainik BD Khabar, he was found dead at Kopalia Bazaar with his throat also slit.
Son of a Hindu schoolteacher in Keshabpur upazila, Bairagi also ran an ice-making factory in Kopalia market.
Blaise Lempen, president of the PEC, has urged Nobel laureate Dr Muhammad Yunus, head of the interim government in Dhaka, to take interest in delivering justice to the bereaved family.
The PEC’s south and southeast Asian representative Nava Thakuria informed that the Muslim majority nation has lately drawn international media attention for recent socio-political turmoil, where many religious minority families were attacked by radical elements across the country of over 170 million people.
Last year, the south Asian country witnessed the murder of five media professionals, namely, Assaduzzaman Tuhin (Dainik Pratidiner Kagoj), Bibhuranjan Sarkar (Ajker Patrika), Wahed-uz-Zaman Bulu (Dainik Ajker Kagoj), Khandahar Shah Alam (Dainik Matrijagat), and Imdadul Haque Milon (Bartaman Somoy).

title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, Rs 5,548 crore for Narmada-Tapi project
description: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi Valley Diversion Project and a draft bill to regulate private aided schools, among 14 decisions taken at the meeting.
content:
Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], November 25 (ANI): The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi Valley Diversion Project and a draft bill to regulate private aided schools, among 14 decisions taken at the meeting.
According to a release from the Chief Minister’s Secretariat, under the foodgrains scheme, 42,30,783 farmers from 33 districts will receive five kilograms of free foodgrains per person for the next three months, comprising three kg of rice and two kg of wheat. The scheme covers farmers who fall under the Below Poverty Line category of the National Food Security Scheme but are not included in the DBT scheme.
The Cabinet also approved ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi Valley Diversion Project in Nandurbar district. The project envisages six diversion weirs, providing irrigation to around 26,526 hectares and generating 11.50 MW of electricity. 
It further approved the draft Maharashtra Private Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, to establish a comprehensive legal framework for private aided schools. The bill will be placed before the State Legislature.
Maharashtra School Education Minister Dada Bhuse said a significant number of schools in Maharashtra are privately aided and are currently governed by the 1977 Act, which does not provide separate comprehensive legislation for them.
“The Maharashtra Cabinet has approved a bill concerning privately aided schools in the state. A significant number of schools in Maharashtra fall under the privately aided category. Currently, these schools are governed by the 1977 Act, but there is no separate comprehensive legislation specifically for them. The government is introducing certain amendments to the existing law. The proposed legislation will provide statutory status to these schools,” Bhuse told reporters here. 
Bhuse said the government is introducing amendments to the existing law and that the new legislation will provide statutory status to these schools.
“Once the Act is enacted, rules and regulations will be framed within the legal framework. The objective is to ensure quality education, adequate staff availability, transparent admissions and decisions related to employees,” he said, adding that the bill will be introduced in the upcoming legislative session. 
To expedite action against financial fraud, the Cabinet approved a separate Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (MPID) Tribunal, with a 90-day deadline for disposing of cases. It also approved amendments to the MPID Act to facilitate faster attachment of properties belonging to financial fraud companies and institutions.
The Cabinet approved a Revenue Court Case Management System for quasi-judicial proceedings in the Revenue Department, along with a “One District, One Appeal” provision through amendments to the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966.
It also approved financial facilities for teachers and non-teaching staff under the Shalarth system through Non-Banking Financial Companies registered with the Reserve Bank of India.
Students from the EBC, SEBC and EWS categories pursuing professional health science degrees will receive higher food, accommodation and maintenance allowances under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme.
Librarians in private aided Ayurveda and Unani colleges will now receive 7th Pay Commission benefits, on the lines of full-time librarians in government medical, dental and Ayurveda colleges.
The Cabinet also approved amendments to Sections 32(B) and 53(1A) of the Maharashtra Stamp Act to bring uniformity in adjudication and appeal fees.
It cleared amendments to the Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University Act, 1997, and the Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University Act, 1989, to align provisions concerning registrars, statutes and committees.
Amendments were also approved to the Maharashtra Mathadi, Hamal and Other Manual Workers Act, 1969, and the Maharashtra Private Security Guards Act, 1981.
Acupuncture will be excluded from the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021, through a draft amendment bill approved by the Cabinet.
The Cabinet also cleared amendments to the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, and approved the allotment of government land to Mouda Nagar Panchayat in Nagpur district for the construction of its administrative building.
Maharashtra is facing a severe agricultural and water crisis triggered by a steep monsoon deficit, particularly across Marathwada and Vidarbha.
Following the latest cabinet additions, 310 out of 358 talukas across the state, covering roughly 86.5% of Maharashtra, are officially declared drought-affected. The cabinet’s approvals of three months of free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh non-DBT Below Poverty Line farmers across 33 districts and ₹5,548 crore for Nandurbar’s Narmada-Tapi river-linking project aim to provide relief in the situation. (ANI)

title: YSRCP condemns attack on Swarnalatha, seeks action against perpetrators
description: Speaking to the media in Tadepalli, party spokesperson Nagamalleswari questioned the police's handling of the matter and alleged that Swarnalatha was targeted for questioning the alleged atrocities committed by a person close to the Eluru MLA.
content:
Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh) [India], November 25 (ANI): The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) on Wednesday condemned the attack on advocate and social activist Swarnalatha from Eluru and demanded strict action against those responsible, alleging that the police had registered ten cases against her instead of acting on her complaint.
Speaking to the media in Tadepalli, party spokesperson Nagamalleswari questioned the police's handling of the matter and alleged that Swarnalatha was targeted for questioning the alleged atrocities committed by a person close to the Eluru MLA.
She alleged that anyone questioning the ruling coalition was being targeted and said the attack on Swarnalatha had taken place in the presence of the police.
Nagamalleswari further alleged that the police refused to acknowledge the attack or register a case in connection with it. She said Home Minister Anitha and the Women's Commission must answer for what she described as the injustice done to Swarnalatha.
"Cases should be filed against the perpetrators, not the victim," she said, calling for an inquiry into the incident.
She also urged the Women's Commission to rise above party lines and help women secure justice.
Nagamalleswari said the YSRCP would stand by Swarnalatha until justice was served.  
Meanwhile, in a post on X, the YSRCP alleged that TDP leaders were behind the attack on Swarnalatha, a lawyer, and accused the police of failing to intervene despite the incident taking place outside the Eluru Two Town police station.
ఏలూరు షాడో ఎమ్మెల్యే కంప్యూటర్ ప్రసాద్ అక్రమాలను బయటపెట్టిన న్యాయవాది స్వర్ణలతపై పోలీస్ స్టేషన్‌ ఎదుటే దాడి చేయించిన టీడీపీ నేతలు ఏలూరు టూటౌన్ పోలీస్ స్టేషన్ ఎదుటే దాడి జరుగుతున్నా.. కనీసం పట్టించుకోని పోలీసులు మీ అక్రమాలను, అవినీతిని ప్రశ్నిస్తే ఇలా దాడులు చేయిస్తారా చంద్రబాబూ?
— YSR Congress Party (@YSRCParty) November 25, 2026
The party said, "TDP leaders had lawyer Swarnalatha attacked right outside the police station for exposing the wrongdoing of Eluru’s shadow MLA, Computer Prasad. Even as the attack was taking place right outside the Eluru Two Town police station, the police didn’t even bother to intervene."
The party also questioned Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu over the alleged attack, linking it to Swarnalatha raising questions about wrongdoing and corruption.
The post read, "Is this how you respond to questions about your wrongdoing and corruption, Chandrababu?"  (ANI)

title: Read More
How Telugu translations of Shakespeare’s plays changed culture in 19th-century Madras Presidency
description: An excerpt from ‘Travelling Texts: Translating Nineteenth-Century European Classics into Indian Languages’, edited by Shantanu Majee and K Subramanyam.
author: Nishi Pulugurtha
content:
The map of bhashas
The term “bhasha” signifies “language” in many South Asian tongues, but it also evokes the rootedness of vernacular identity – the earth-bound tongues spoken not in courtly, colonial, or cosmopolitan registers but in practices of everyday life. Across India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal, bhasha literatures are rich in history, folklore, philosophy and resistance.
Yet historically, these literatures have often been overshadowed – first by the dominance of colonial presence, and later, by the prominence of a few “major” languages like Hindi, Bengali or Tamil.
The process of translating European classics into South Asian bhashas raises complex ethical questions. To what extent can a translator adapt a source text without distorting its intent? Is fidelity owed to the original’s linguistic structure or to its philosophical substance? This act of cultural transcreation becomes even more charged in postcolonial contexts. Translation is not merely literary; it becomes political. The prestige of European classics, often valorised through colonial education systems, means their entry into bhasha literatures is often both aspirational and subversive.
By translating Dostoevsky into Bengali, then, a bhasha translator both affirms the universality of the Russian’s themes and asserts the vernacular’s capacity to absorb and reinterpret the global canon.
Travelling with words
Unlike translation between major world languages (say, French and English), translation between South Asian bhashas often involves multiple modes of mediation. Sometimes a work moves first into Hindi, then into English, then into Marathi, picking up layers and distortions like a snowball. Each translation is a fresh departure and arrival: no two voyages are the same.
Take, for instance, the epic Silappadikaram of Tamil, one of the foundational texts of ancient Indian literature. When rendered into Malayalam, Telugu or Kannada, the work doesn’t simply cross into different scripts; it reorients itself towards new mythologies of place and body. The anklet that causes devastation in Madurai may, in another language’s retelling, seem to chime slightly differently, evoking local memories of betrayal, fidelity and injustice.
Scholars like GN Devy and AK Ramanujan have emphasised that bhasha literatures are intensely tied to their regional soil – their idioms saturated with climate, cuisine, caste and cosmology. An old proverb confirms that if at every three or four kilometres the water tastes different in this country, then there’s a different tongue to be heard at every 12–15. Therefore, every translation embodies a travel itself – not merely moving the text but “replanting” it in new soil, where it must adapt, sometimes thriving, sometimes transforming beyond recognition.
Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak also refers to the “intimate act” of translation – one that recognises both the alterity of the source text and the demands of the receiving culture. In this context, translation is not a bridge between static points. It is a caravanserai, a moving camp of meanings.
The dangers of travel
Yet, travel is not innocent. Travellers bring with them baggage; translators bring their own histories, politics and unconscious biases. In South Asia, where language often intersects with religion, caste and class, translation can become a deeply political act. When the Tirukkural, a seminal Tamil ethical text, was translated into Sanskrit and later Hindi, there were accusations of “Sanskritisation” – of imposing Brahminical values onto a text celebrated for its secular and egalitarian spirit. Similarly, Dalit literature, when translated from Marathi or Kannada into English or Hindi, often undergoes a softening of its rawness, a domestication of its rage to make it palatable to upper-caste or global readers.
– an excerpt from the Preface by Shantanu Majee.
Colonial education in India resulted in several English literary texts being taught and read in 19th-century India. Among them were plays by Shakespeare. The history of Shakespeare in India can be traced back to the colonial encounter, to the study, performances, recitations, and translations of Shakespeare into several Indian languages. The National Library in Kolkata recorded several Shakespeare translations and adaptations done in the various Indian languages till the year 1964.
Of a total of 670 such records, 128 were in Bengali, 97 in Marathi, 83 in Tamil, 70 in Hindi, 66 in Kannada and 62 in Telugu. The latter half of the 19th century was witness to a literary revival in Telugu that was strongly marked by the influence of Sanskrit and English literature. There were also translations of works from these two languages during the period.
The translations and adaptations of Shakespeare’s plays into Telugu created a corpus of literary texts, both in prose and dramatic forms, that reveal that the plays of Shakespeare were no longer just texts to be studied but were becoming an important part of the cultural scenario as well.
Telugu was a language spoken in the Madras Presidency in the nineteenth century. Madras Presidency or Madras Province, was an administrative province of British India. It was officially referred to as the Presidency of Fort St George. This province included the states of present-day Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, some areas of modern-day Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha and Telangana as well.
The city of Madras (present-day Chennai) was the winter capital while the hill station of Ooty was the summer capital. The languages spoken here were Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Odia and Tulu. Telugu was the language spoken in the districts to the north of the city of Madras and to the east of Bellary (now part of Karnataka) and Anantapur (in present-day Andhra Pradesh) districts. The 1871 census noted a total of 11,610,000 people who spoke Telugu in the Madras Presidency which increased in the 1901 census to 14,276,509.
During the times of India’s independence in 1947, Tamil and Telugu speakers comprised over 78% of the total population of the Madras Presidency. Today Telugu is the language spoken in two states – Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
Theatrical performances in Telugu chiefly consisted of Kuchipudi performances, dance dramas based on the puranas and folk forms like the burrakatha (an oral form of storytelling that includes songs, prayers, dialogues and music) and the tholibomma aata (literally the art of leather puppets, a performance with shadow puppets).
In the latter part of the 19th century, a change was noticed. This was due to the Parsi theatre companies from Bombay touring various parts of the Madras Presidency. These performances led to local people forming drama companies and resulted in productions and performances in the Telugu language. The influence of Parsi theatre groups that toured various parts of the south of India in the nineteenth century had a great influence on the way Shakespeare found its way into the cultural and literary ethos of the Telugu people.
The Dharwar School from Maharashtra was another popular group that influenced Telugu theatre. These touring groups were an important form of entertainment in South India. Their success and popularity led to the formation of local language drama groups that often staged plays based on the works of Kalidasa and Shakespeare. These performances led to the development of Telugu theatre companies, chief among them being Surabhi Theatre.
Plays performed were chiefly based on stories from Indian mythology and the epics. Sanskrit plays were being translated for performance in Telugu as well. One such play was Sakuntala, a play in which actors rendered the Sanskrit shlokas followed by the Telugu translation of them. This was the translation done by Kandukuri Veerasalingam.
An important name in Telugu translations from Sanskrit is Vedam Venkataraya Sastry (1853–1929), a poet, dramatist and critic, who wrote plays in Telugu and translated Sanskrit plays by Kalidasa and Harsha. His translations of Kalidasa’s Vikramorvasiya (1901) and Harsha’s Nagananda (1891) were well-known and popular. Two of his Telugu plays are Prataparudriya natakam (1897) and Usha natakam (1901). The word natakam means a play.
In 1876, Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri (1851–1897) translated Julius Caesar. A pioneer in translating Shakespeare into Telugu, his translation retained the names of the characters of the source text while adapting them to the Telugu language. Julius Caesar becomes “Juliusudu”, Brutus becomes “Brutusudu” in the translation. Sastri uses the common suffix used in Telugu while referring to the names of people here. The translation was done in verse, in a metre that the translator believed was closest to the iambic pentametre.
In 1880, Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice was translated as Venusu Vanija Naatakamu. Gurazada Sriramamurti (1851–1899), who translated the play, used both prose and verse in the translation. He also used the names of the dramatis personae as they appeared in the source text. Gurazada Sriramamurti was a scholar in the court of King Ananda Gajapathiraju of Vizianagaram and is known as the first person who wrote the biography in Telugu – Kavijivitamu (Lives of Poets, 1893). CSR Krishnamma translated Macbeth – a Telugu prose translation that was done in 1895. Lady Macbeth and Lady Macduff become Macbeth Devi and Macduff Devi in the translation.
In 1880, Kandukuri Veeresalingam (1848–1919) began an association for Telugu drama in the Madras Presidency. He wrote a play in Telugu – Vyavahara Dharma Bodhini. He also translated William Shakespeare’s Comedy of Errors into Telugu, his mother tongue, as Chamatkara Ratnavali. The drama association that he began staged both these plays in Telugu on April 16, 1880; the performers were his students.
In the same year, he translated Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice from Tales from Shakespeare by Charles and Mary Lamb. Printed at Vivekavarthani Press in Rajahmundry in the year 1880, the translation had on its front cover this description of the author/translator as “Kandukuri Veerasalingam, Telugu Pundit, First Grade Government College, Rajahmundry.”
Kandukuri Veeresalingam, often referred to as the father of modern Telugu literature, translated Charles and Mary Lamb’s Tales from Shakespeare in a very simple style. The names of characters were changed. Situations and incidents that would fit the Telugu ethos were used in the translation. In 1880, Kandukuri notes in his autobiography that he had begun a translation of The Merchant of Venice with the title Venusu Vartakuni Charitramu.
Kandukuri Veeresalingam was not just a writer and translator. Often referred to as Veerasalingam Pantalu, he was an important social reformer of the time and was a strong advocate of women’s education, widow remarriage and the abolition of child marriage. Kandukuri Veerasalingam’s life and work reveal the amalgamation of the political, social and cultural environment of the times.
Missionary activity in the region had resulted in the building of several churches in the area, and English education was seen in Andhra as well. In 1840, Lord Hay began the first Anglo-vernacular school in the region. Soon, several other such schools were set up in the region.
Samuel Dey, an American Baptist missionary, founded the Telugu Baptist Church in 1840 in Nellore. Till 1805, it was the Roman Catholic missionaries who worked in this region (which, after 1950, was formed into the state of Andhra Pradesh). After 1805, the Protestants began to propagate Christianity in the region as well. Visakhapatnam became an important centre for religion, and the Bible and other books were translated into Telugu. Like the Scottish missionaries who set up educational institutions in Calcutta, the Noble College was set up by missionaries who came to Machilipatnam in 1841.
The Charter Act of 1813 led to the free entry of missionaries into India, though it took some years for the spread of missionary activity. Sir Arthur Cotton, a military engineer who toured the Godavari delta region in 1833, worked to create a mission station in the region. Cotton supervised the construction of the Godavari Barrage near Dhavaleswaram and the rail bridge across the Godavari River connecting Rajahmundry and Kovvur.
On his way back from England in 1836, Cotton brought with him several missionaries, two of whom set up what later came to be called the Godavari Delta Mission that had its headquarters at Narsapur. Besides its evangelical work, the Godavari Delta Mission set up schools in the region and the Mission Hospital at Narsapur. It was missionary activity that led to the setting up of the first Anglo-Telugu school in 1844, which was the first Anglo-vernacular school in Andhra Pradesh.
In 1853, Mrs Hay began a school where the girls were given education as well as training to become teachers. The missionaries also had a printing press at Visakhapatnam that printed religious books in the Telugu language. It is these activities that led to an interest in English education and, with it, social reform as well. The nineteenth century was a time of social reform in various parts of India, and the Telugu-speaking people were part of this intellectual and social ferment as well.
Like many other reformers of the time, Kandukuri Veerasalingam strongly believed in Western science and advancement and considered English education important in order to rejuvenate Telugu culture and literature. In 1875, he wrote:
It is admitted by one and all that western lore has worked wonders among the natives of India. We are quite aware that English education has rendered natives more refined in their manners, has dispelled the mist of superstition from the minds of several of them, if not many, and has considerably developed their moral calibre whenever it is properly imparted.
It was, therefore, imperative to find ways to make this “western lore” available to those who did not have access to English education. Kandukuri believed that translation into Telugu would be a way to make English texts available to Telugu people. Kandukuri Veerasalingam is also credited with the modernisation of the language of Telugu literature, in that the language of literature moved from the classical style to the use of a more colloquial form. This also meant an increase in the use of prose in the genres of the essay, biography, autobiography and the novel in Telugu.
Excerpted with permission from ‘Shakespeare in Telugu in the Nineteenth Century’ by Nishi Pulugurtha in Travelling Texts: Translating Nineteenth-Century European Classics into Indian Languages, edited by Shantanu Majee and K Subramanyam, Routledge.

title: Founder’s story: How Harsh Parikh cofounded DRiefcase, an online platform for saving health records
description: An excerpt from ‘Strivers: Balancing Success and Meaningfulness’, by Upasna A Agarwal, Arvind N Agrawal, and Usha Sunderarajan.
author: Upasna A Agarwal
content:
Harsh Parikh is a CA-turned-MBA from IIM-Bangalore. After working with Merrill Lynch as an investment banker for ten years, he co-founded DRiefcase Health Tech Pvt. Ltd. The mission of the organisation is to help citizens with safe and on-the-go access to their health records. Having online health records saves a lot of time for patients when they visit their doctors, resulting in an increase in productivity. DRiefcase has now partnered with Google Wallet to make ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) cards easily accessible to users.
Harsh was born into a business family and neither parent was a graduate. Because of this, his parents were very keen that he study well. Harsh was an academically bright student in school. While studying for a graduate degree, he also decided to become a CA (Chartered Accountant) because CA could be done alongside graduation. The fact that both his brothers-in-law were CAs also pushed him in that direction. Thus, Harsh completed his CA and internship along with his graduation.
However, Harsh was not too impressed with the CA degree – he believed that it “existed in the sixties” and had not evolved. Besides, he was not interested in audit or taxation. He knew that in 2002–03, there were not too many exciting jobs available to CAs. The next option was a management degree. Harsh appeared for the CAT and joined IIM Bangalore in 2004.
After IIM, Harsh was inclined towards a job in investment banking or consulting. His family wanted him to be in India, so unlike many of his classmates who were opting to go abroad, he looked for opportunities in India. Harsh got an offer from Merrill Lynch and joined them. He had a reason for choosing investment banking over consulting.
As a consultant rose in seniority, they would be required to get business for the company, and this would involve a lot of travel. Harsh wanted to make life easier for himself, not harder, as he grew older, and that tilted the decision in favour of investment banking.
A typical career path for an investment banker is to start as an analyst, and then become an associate, a vice president, a director and finally a managing director within a period of 11 to 12 years.
In 2006, Harsh, being an MBA, joined as a third-year analyst. He received a good rating every year and was in the top two or three in his batch. Between 2006 and 2008, several investment banking companies set up shop in India. Some of the vice presidents working with Merrill Lynch left to join these companies. Therefore, a lot of work that the seniors had handled was now available to juniors like Harsh.
He got an opportunity to perform high-level jobs and rose quickly in the organisation. He was doing well financially too and earning large bonuses and increments – not 10–15%, but 40–50%. Despite this, Harsh would tell himself every year that he was “done” and wanted to hang up his boots but continued working only for the money.
In Harsh’s words, though he was “not born with a silver spoon”, his father had started doing well and by the time he was 15, he realised the advantages of having money. So he stayed on for ten years, earned well and spent freely on himself and his family, like taking impromptu holidays. As he progressed in the organisation, he also had the freedom to choose his projects and that made work interesting for him.
By 2014, he had become a director in the bank. Harsh had enough savings and realised that money has diminishing marginal utility. He felt burnt out. He also knew that in a pyramidal organisational structure, he would have to “play games” and keep some people happy to rise further, and he did not like doing that. To him, it seemed like internal canvassing with people at the top. He states that he could have done that, but did not because, by his own admission, he was not ambitious and needed very little to be happy.
He had no vision of becoming the CEO of a Fortune 500 company at the age of 50. Given a task, he would do it well, but it was not to gain something for himself. He wanted to be with his family, keep himself fit and have his share of “me time”. In 2013, his father had a heart attack, and he had to look after him while delivering results at the office. All these experiences nudged him towards quitting his job. He had also reached a phase where he had stopped comparing himself with other batchmates and what they were doing.
When the time came to take a decision about his job and set up DRiefcase with Sohit, he jumped at the chance. Sohit was his senior from IIMB and a colleague at Merrill Lynch. Harsh admits that had Sohit not approached him, he might have joined another organisation. DRiefcase was established with the objective of maintaining online medical records for individuals, which were secure and easy to access. This ensured that a person’s full medical history was available when they went to visit a doctor.
Between December 2015 and May 2016, Harsh and Sohit spent time working out a strategy for DRiefcase. It was also the time his daughter was born, and he was happy spending time with the newborn. When Harsh started the business, he got a lot of support from family and friends, especially when times were bad. Co-founding DRiefcase was a humbling experience for him.
In his own words, he was a “CEO and chaprasi”. He had to get off his high horse and do everything with his own hands. Earlier, his colleagues were management graduates, IIT gold medallists and CA rankers. Harsh believes that the start-up experience has made him a better person. The Harsh of Merrill Lynch had a bad temper and believed in perfection. Today, he believes in Wabi-sabi and that one should not seek perfection at any cost. He is now patient and more willing to listen to others and interact with them. Besides, he has the advantage of being able to spend more time with his family.
Harsh and Sohit have now managed DRiefcase for more than nine years. He was never worried about the business not working out and having to go back to corporate life because he had enough savings and a good CV. He had invested his money wisely and the stock market had done well. He did not need to dip into his savings and spent only what he earned. Other classmates were doing better financially and professionally but that did not affect Harsh.
His experience at Merrill Lynch has stood Harsh in good stead. It has given him a sense of perspective in DRiefcase and how to deal with people and business. Harsh states that it is with good reason that Harvard Business School accepts people with work experience because that ensures that they have experienced organizational life before they study business management.
Today, DRiefcase is growing and many teething problems have been sorted out. Harsh and Sohit have done well for their employees and customers. Every day, one lakh tokens are generated. This means that they are saving 1–2 hours of time for one lakh people, especially hourly paid workers, resulting in better productivity for the country. The software is also very useful and has been deployed by the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. DRiefcase is now at a critical juncture, having been through three rounds of funding.
Harsh gives himself 4 on success and according to him, it can never be a 5. This is because he wants to “give back to society”, which he has not been able to do so far. His next venture is likely to be in the social sector – either starting an NGO or joining an NGO to do social work.
On meaningfulness, he gives himself a 5. They have employees in DRiefcase who joined them on day one, straight out of college, with not a care in the world. Today, they are married, have taken loans to buy vehicles and have settled down in life. Harsh states that he and the company played a role in making that happen, and that makes life meaningful for him.
Harsh would like to tell fresh graduates that perseverance is important and one should not look for instant gratification. One needs to be “at it” because results do not appear instantaneously. A lesson Harsh’s father had taught him early in life was that one should focus on one’s responsibilities before claiming one’s rights. The reward for doing one’s job will eventually come. You just need to be patient. This advice has remained with him till date.
Also, while it is good to rise quickly in an organisation and make money, because it allows you to have options, Harsh warns that eventually, life catches up and one needs to slow down. If you achieve everything by the time you are 40, then what would you do for the rest of your career?
Excerpted with permission from Strivers: Balancing Success and Meaningfulness, Upasna A Agarwal, Arvind N Agrawal, and Usha Sunderarajan, Penguin India.

title: India has been providing meals to students for 30 years. Did it change how families made choices?
description: Understanding what that meal means within family life may be just as important to making school meal programmes work as intended.
author: Swayamshree Mishra, The Conversation
content:
Debates about the provision of free school meals often focus on eligibility, nutrition and health, programme costs and reducing child poverty. These are important questions. But there is another critical question that receives much less attention: How do families themselves understand and respond to school food?
This question is at the heart of addressing the gap between eligibility and uptake that plagues school meal programmes around the world.
India offers a useful place to look for answers. Its midday meal scheme, now known as PM Poshan, marked its 30th year in 2025. It is the world’s largest – and one of the longest-running – school feeding programmes. It provides a free cooked meal on school days to 112 million children attending pre-primary and Classes I–VIII (aged from around six to 14) in more than a million government and government-aided schools on all school days across India.
Our new research offers important insights into how families perceive and experience school meals. We carried out interviews with members of 86 households in Uttar Pradesh and Goa, basing our analysis particularly on in-depth conversations with 134 adults and 112 children.
While the scheme aims to improve children’s nutrition and educational participation, our findings show that its significance extends beyond these outcomes. Children talked about the food’s taste and whether it filled them up. Parents, on the other hand, largely mentioned the meals’ nutrition only when prompted. Instead, they weighed the scheme against their aspirations, their sense of dignity and the pressures of precarious lives.
For low-income families, accepting a free school meal is rarely a simple yes or no. It is weighed against everything else the household needs: food at home, the cost of getting to school, children’s contributions to household work and family livelihoods, and their hopes for the future. How families make that calculation can decide whether a school meal programme reaches the children it is meant for.
Food carries social meaning
School meals were also shaped by what food signalled to others. Some children felt uncomfortable queuing for meals, adding their names to the monthly register, or asking for a second helping when portions were small. Each of these made a child’s need visible to classmates and teachers. For some, how others perceived their need for a meal mattered as much as the need for food itself.
Parents, too, attached meaning to how their children ate. Some fathers felt that relying on school food conflicted with their responsibility to provide, while mothers kept packing lunch boxes from home as an expression of maternal care.
Caste and class shaped eating as well. Reflecting purity norms, some families sent their own plates for their children. Some better-off parents kept their children away from the meal entirely, distancing themselves from those they saw as in need of help.
Because free school meals are only provided in government and government-aided schools, the choice of school is also a choice about food. Some families who could have benefited from the programme moved their children to low-cost private schools, giving up the free meal altogether. They associated these schools with English-medium teaching, greater accountability, more attentive teachers and better prospects.
This did not mean food was unimportant to them. Some households cut back on food at home to pay private school fees. For these families, going with less now was the price of hope for later. Choices that look puzzling from the perspective of a programme made sense from the perspective of a family investing in its children’s futures.
The scheme is designed around the individual child, but food insecurity is lived by whole households. For the poorest families, a single meal could not outweigh the hidden costs of free schooling, such as daily transport, or the income an older child could earn. Some children were kept at home or withdrawn from school altogether. Girls bore the heaviest share, more often leaving school early to care for younger siblings and run the home.
None of this diminishes the scheme’s importance. For families facing sudden hardship, school meals became a lifeline, sometimes the only place children still ate vegetables. A programme that was less of a priority for one family could be an essential safety net for another.
Lessons beyond India
The step between programme eligibility and take-up is where household trade-offs and social meanings do their work. A child who feels awkward about being seen to claim support, or a parent who feels judged for accepting it, may not show up in eligibility figures, but both shape whether a programme works. Programmes routinely count who is eligible and who eats. They rarely ask families why they do or do not take part.
India’s universal design offers an important, practical lesson. When every child eats the same meal, the meal itself reveals little about a family’s circumstances. As England and other countries debate means-testing and the design of school food, stigma and family meanings belong at the centre of those decisions.
Putting food on the plate is essential. But understanding what that meal means within family life may be just as important to making school meal programmes work as intended.
Swayamshree Mishra is Postdoctoral Research Associate in Social Science, Lancaster University.
Jasmine Fledderjohann is Professor in Sociology and Social Justice, Lancaster University.
Sukumar Vellakkal is Associate Professor of Economic Science, Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur.
This article was first published on The Conversation.

title: 20 जुलाई को दिल्ली प्रोटेस्ट में पुलिस बर्बरता पर शिकायतों की कमी से सुप्रीम कोर्ट सख्त, कमेटी को तुरंत जांच शुरू करने का निर्देश
description: 20 जुलाई की पुलिस बर्बरता पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट सख्त। HPEC को बिना देरी जांच शुरू कर एक महीने में रिपोर्ट सौंपने का निर्देश। जानिए कोर्ट में क्या-क्या हुआ।
author: Rajan Chaudhary
content:
नई दिल्ली: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने गुरुवार, 5 नवंबर को कहा कि 20 जुलाई को हुए हिंसक प्रदर्शनों के दौरान पुलिस की बर्बरता और महिलाओं के यौन उत्पीड़न के आरोपों की जांच कर रही हाई पावर्ड इंक्वायरी कमेटी (HPEC) के ऑनलाइन पोर्टल पर बहुत कम शिकायतें मिली हैं। यह हिंसा NEET-UG 2026 के प्रश्नपत्र लीक होने के खिलाफ हुए प्रदर्शनों के दौरान भड़की थी, जिसके बाद तत्कालीन शिक्षा मंत्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान को इस्तीफा देना पड़ा था।
मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) सूर्यकांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ ने 31 अक्टूबर को HPEC द्वारा सौंपी गई 'कार्रवाई रिपोर्ट' (ATR) का अवलोकन किया। अदालत ने पाया कि पोर्टल पर नाममात्र की प्रतिक्रिया मिली है। इसके अलावा, ईमेल, डाक या HPEC कार्यालयों में व्यक्तिगत रूप से जाकर भी कोई शिकायत दर्ज नहीं कराई गई है।
सुप्रीम कोर्ट द्वारा इस विशेष समिति का गठन अगस्त महीने में किया गया था। इसकी अध्यक्षता शीर्ष अदालत के पूर्व न्यायाधीश जस्टिस आर. सुभाष रेड्डी कर रहे हैं। इस समिति ने लगभग तीन सप्ताह पहले, अक्टूबर के मध्य में अपना ऑनलाइन पोर्टल लॉन्च किया था ताकि पीड़ित अपनी बात आसानी से रख सकें।
कार्रवाई रिपोर्ट में बताया गया है कि लगातार सार्वजनिक नोटिस जारी किए जाने के बावजूद प्रदर्शनकारियों की ओर से शिकायतें नहीं आ रही हैं। नोटिस में स्पष्ट किया गया था कि शिकायतों को पूरी तरह से गोपनीय रखा जाएगा और यह जानकारी केवल अध्यक्ष तथा HPEC सदस्यों तक ही सीमित रहेगी।
रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, पीड़ित बिना अपना नाम, फोन नंबर, पता या आधार विवरण दिए, गुमनाम रूप से भी शिकायत दर्ज करा सकते थे। इसके लिए पोर्टल पर प्रभावित प्रदर्शनकारियों और पुलिस कर्मियों के लिए अलग-अलग विंडो भी बनाई गई थीं।
इन परिस्थितियों और एटीआर को ध्यान में रखते हुए, पीठ ने शीर्ष अदालत में मौजूद याचिकाकर्ताओं से कहा कि वे हिंसा से जुड़ी जो भी सामग्री या वीडियो क्लिप उनके पास है, उसे विचार के लिए HPEC को सौंप दें। अदालत ने आदेश दिया कि याचिकाकर्ताओं द्वारा भेजी गई जानकारी और सबूतों की समिति द्वारा विस्तार से जांच की जाए।
अदालत ने HPEC को निर्देश दिया कि वह आरोपों की जांच का अपना काम शुरू करने के लिए सामग्री का 'अनिश्चित काल' तक इंतजार न करे। पीठ का कहना था कि समिति उपलब्ध शिकायतों के आधार पर जांच को आगे बढ़ा सकती है और जैसे-जैसे नई शिकायतें आती जाएं, उन्हें भी प्रक्रिया में शामिल किया जा सकता है।
अदालत का यह निर्देश अधिवक्ता वृंदा ग्रोवर की उस दलील के बाद आया, जिसमें उन्होंने कहा था कि पुलिस अधिकारियों ने अभी तक HPEC के साथ कोई जानकारी, सबूत या सामग्री साझा नहीं की है। ग्रोवर ने सवाल उठाया कि अगर पैलेट गन चलाई गई थी, तो इसे किसने अधिकृत किया, इसका आदेश कहां है और गोला-बारूद का रजिस्टर कहां है।
इस पर मुख्य न्यायाधीश ने कहा कि इस तरह की जानकारी मांगने वाली याचिकाओं पर HPEC को विचार करना चाहिए। पैनल को बिना किसी देरी के अधिकारियों से इन सवालों के जवाब दर्ज करने होंगे। सीजेआई ने अपने आदेश में स्पष्ट किया कि जो भी सामग्री सामने आए, अधिकारियों को उसका जवाब देना होगा और समिति को अब अपनी तथ्य-अन्वेषण (फैक्ट-फाइंडिंग) रिपोर्ट देनी शुरू करनी चाहिए।
सुनवाई के दौरान वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता एन. हरिहरन ने कुछ महत्वपूर्ण कानूनी सवाल भी उठाए। उन्होंने कहा कि प्रदर्शनकारियों की निगरानी या जासूसी करना उनके निजता और शांतिपूर्ण सभा के संवैधानिक अधिकारों का हनन है। उन्होंने तर्क दिया कि मौलिक अधिकारों को प्रभावित करने वाले इतने गंभीर मुद्दों की जांच केवल समिति पर नहीं छोड़ी जानी चाहिए, बल्कि अदालत को स्वयं इन सवालों पर विचार करना चाहिए।
सुनवाई के अंत में, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने HPEC को एक महीने के भीतर अपनी पहली तथ्य-अन्वेषण रिपोर्ट सौंपने को कहा है। अदालत ने कहा कि जब तक गोपनीयता की सख्त आवश्यकता न हो, समिति के प्रासंगिक निष्कर्षों को सभी पक्षों के साथ साझा किया जाना चाहिए। इस मामले की अगली सुनवाई अब दिसंबर में होगी।
गौरतलब है कि 20 जुलाई को दिल्ली में 'कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी' द्वारा बुलाए गए एक विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान पुलिस ने कड़ी कार्रवाई की थी। इस हिंसक पुलिस क्रैकडाउन में कई लोग गंभीर रूप से घायल हो गए थे।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।

title: अब 'हिरासत' के समय से ही शुरू होगी 24 घंटे की डेडलाइन, असंवैधानिक है पुलिस का 'बफर जोन'- सुप्रीम कोर्ट का फैसला
description: सुप्रीम कोर्ट का ऐतिहासिक फैसला। अब पुलिस को हिरासत में लेने के 24 घंटे के भीतर आरोपी को मजिस्ट्रेट के सामने पेश करना होगा। पढ़ें पूरा नियम।
author: Rajan Chaudhary
content:
नई दिल्ली: पुलिस या किसी भी जांच एजेंसी द्वारा किसी व्यक्ति को पूछताछ के लिए हिरासत में लिए जाने के क्षण से ही, उसे 24 घंटे के भीतर मजिस्ट्रेट के सामने पेश करने की संवैधानिक समय-सीमा शुरू हो जाएगी। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने गुरुवार को एक बेहद अहम फैसला सुनाते हुए स्पष्ट किया कि यह अवधि औपचारिक गिरफ्तारी दर्ज होने के समय से नहीं, बल्कि हिरासत में लिए जाने के समय से ही गिनी जाएगी।
शीर्ष अदालत का मानना है कि हिरासत में लिए जाने के साथ ही व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता बाधित हो जाती है।
जस्टिस उज्ज्वल भुइयां और जस्टिस अतुल एस. चंदुरकर की पीठ ने इस मामले में उच्च न्यायालयों के उन पुराने फैसलों को खारिज कर दिया, जिनमें कहा गया था कि 24 घंटे की यह अवधि औपचारिक गिरफ्तारी के बाद ही शुरू होती है।
पीठ ने सख्त टिप्पणी करते हुए कहा कि हिरासत और गिरफ्तारी के बीच कोई भी कृत्रिम अंतर पैदा नहीं किया जाना चाहिए। संविधान का अनुच्छेद 22(2) यह साफ तौर पर अनिवार्य करता है कि गिरफ्तार या हिरासत में लिए गए हर व्यक्ति को 24 घंटे के भीतर नजदीकी मजिस्ट्रेट के समक्ष पेश किया जाए।
शीर्ष अदालत ने अपने फैसले में स्पष्ट किया कि संविधान का अनुच्छेद 22(2) गिरफ्तारी से पहले पूछताछ और जांच में लगने वाले समय को इस 24 घंटे की सीमा से बाहर रखने की बिल्कुल इजाजत नहीं देता। अदालत ने कहा कि जांच के नाम पर किसी भी ऐसे 'बफर जोन' का निर्माण करना पूरी तरह से असंवैधानिक है, जहां किसी व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता तो छीन ली गई हो, लेकिन उसे कागजों पर औपचारिक रूप से गिरफ्तार न दिखाया गया हो।
यह फैसला जांच एजेंसियों के काम करने के तरीके में बड़ा बदलाव लाएगा। दरअसल, यह एक आम चलन बन गया है कि पुलिस पूछताछ के लिए किसी व्यक्ति को हिरासत में लेने के काफी समय बाद, या कभी-कभी पूरे एक दिन बाद उसकी औपचारिक गिरफ्तारी दर्ज करती है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट का यह कड़ा आदेश पुलिस और अन्य जांच एजेंसियों की इसी मनमानी पर एक मजबूत लगाम लगाने का काम करेगा।
अदालत ने इस आदेश के पीछे छिपे एक और बेहद गंभीर कारण का भी जिक्र किया। पीठ ने कहा कि इस फैसले का एक बड़ा उद्देश्य हिरासत में होने वाली हिंसा (कस्टोडियल वायलेंस) को रोकना है।
अदालत ने चिंता जताते हुए कहा कि दुर्भाग्य से हिरासत में हिंसा के ज्यादातर मामले उसी दौरान होते हैं जब व्यक्ति को हिरासत में तो रखा जाता है, लेकिन कागजों में उसकी गिरफ्तारी दर्ज नहीं होती। इसी वजह से उसे मजिस्ट्रेट के सामने पेश करने में भी जानबूझकर देरी की जाती है।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।

title: संसद और विधानसभाओं में SC/ST आरक्षित सीटों के रोटेशन की याचिका खारिज, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा- यह अधिकार संसद का है
description: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने संसद और विधानसभाओं में SC/ST आरक्षित सीटों के रोटेशन की मांग ठुकरा दी है। कोर्ट ने कहा- यह फैसला संसद का अधिकार क्षेत्र है। जानें पूरी खबर।
author: Rajan Chaudhary
content:
नई दिल्ली: संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं में अनुसूचित जाति (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) के लिए आरक्षित सीटों के रोटेशन (चक्रानुक्रम) को अनिवार्य बनाने की मांग वाली एक याचिका को सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने बुधवार (4 नवंबर 2026) को खारिज कर दिया है। सर्वोच्च अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि ऐसे फैसले लेना विधायिका के अधिकार क्षेत्र में आता है और न्यायालय इस संबंध में कोई आदेश पारित नहीं कर सकता।
भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्या बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की पीठ ने इस मामले की सुनवाई की। अदालत ने इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट के उस फैसले में दखल देने से इनकार कर दिया, जिसमें परिसीमन अधिनियम, 2002 की धारा 9(1)(c) को सही ठहराया गया था। यह धारा उन क्षेत्रों में आरक्षित निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों की पहचान करने का प्रावधान करती है, जहां SC/ST आबादी का अनुपात तुलनात्मक रूप से अधिक है।
यह याचिका उत्तर प्रदेश के सुल्तानपुर जिले की 191-कादीपुर विधानसभा सीट के मतदाता जगदीश सिंह ने दायर की थी। उन्होंने अपनी सीट के लगातार आरक्षित रहने को चुनौती देते हुए कहा था कि यह निर्वाचन क्षेत्र बनने के बाद से करीब सात दशकों से अनुसूचित जाति के लिए आरक्षित चला आ रहा है।
याचिकाकर्ता की दलील थी कि रोटेशन व्यवस्था का न होना संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14, 15 और 19 का सीधा उल्लंघन है। उनका कहना था कि इससे मतदाताओं के चुनावी विकल्प सीमित हो जाते हैं, क्योंकि वे केवल SC समुदाय के उम्मीदवारों को ही अपना प्रतिनिधि चुन सकते हैं। इसके साथ ही, उन्होंने यह भी दावा किया कि मौजूदा व्यवस्था से व्यापक समुदाय के बजाय केवल कुछ गिने-चुने राजनीतिक परिवारों को ही फायदा हो रहा है।
सिंह ने अपनी याचिका में मांग की थी कि संविधान के अनुच्छेद 243D और 243T के तहत पंचायतों और नगर पालिकाओं में जिस तरह से रोटेशनल रिजर्वेशन (चक्रानुक्रम आरक्षण) की व्यवस्था है, वैसा ही तंत्र यहां भी लागू किया जाए। उन्होंने पीठ से SC/ST आरक्षित सीटों को समय-समय पर रोटेट करने का निर्देश देने का आग्रह किया था।
सुनवाई के दौरान जस्टिस बागची ने एक बेहद अहम टिप्पणी की। उन्होंने कहा कि बहुदलीय लोकतंत्र में मतदाताओं से यह उम्मीद की जाती है कि वे जाति या धर्म के बजाय राजनीतिक विचारधाराओं के आधार पर अपना वोट दें।
जस्टिस बागची ने स्थिति स्पष्ट करते हुए कहा कि एक राजनीतिक लोकतंत्र में अलग-अलग विचारधाराओं वाली कई पार्टियां होती हैं। आप किसी विचारधारा को पसंद या नापसंद कर सकते हैं, लेकिन उस विचारधारा का प्रतिनिधित्व कौन कर रहा है, यह अप्रासंगिक हो जाता है। आप विचारधारा को वोट देते हैं, इसलिए आपका यह तर्क अपने आप खारिज हो जाता है।
पीठ ने वोट देने के अधिकार और किसी विशेष सीट से चुनाव लड़ने के अधिकार के बीच भी स्पष्ट अंतर बताया। अदालत ने कहा कि सामान्य वर्ग के उम्मीदवार उन निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों से चुनाव लड़ने के लिए पूरी तरह से योग्य हैं जो आरक्षित श्रेणी में नहीं आते हैं।
मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्यकांत ने कहा कि याचिकाकर्ता ने इस नीतिगत बदलाव की मांग के लिए गलत मंच का दरवाजा खटखटाया है। उन्होंने सुझाव दिया कि रोटेशन की इस मांग को सीधे संसद के समक्ष उठाया जाना चाहिए। हल्के-फुल्के अंदाज में सीजेआई ने यह भी टिप्पणी की कि याचिकाकर्ता इस मुद्दे को जन-विरोध और प्रदर्शनों के माध्यम से भी उठा सकते हैं।
अपने अंतिम आदेश में पीठ ने कहा कि हाईकोर्ट ने यह मानते हुए मामले को खारिज कर दिया था कि आदर्श रूप से रोटेशन का पालन होना चाहिए, लेकिन अदालत ऐसा निर्देश नहीं दे सकती क्योंकि यह पूरी तरह से संसद के दायरे में आता है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि उन्हें हाईकोर्ट के इस विचार से अलग राय रखने का कोई आधार नहीं दिखता।
हालांकि, अदालत ने याचिकाकर्ता को इस बात की पूरी छूट दी है कि वे अपनी मांग को लेकर जनप्रतिनिधियों से संपर्क कर सकते हैं और उन्हें रोटेशन के सिद्धांत को अपनाने के लिए राजी कर सकते हैं।
द मूकनायक की प्रीमियम और चुनिंदा खबरें अब द मूकनायक के न्यूज़ एप्प पर पढ़ें। Google Play Store से न्यूज़ एप्प इंस्टाल करने के लिए यहां क्लिक करें.
'द मूकनायक' जनवादी पत्रकारिता करता है. यह संविधान, लोकतंत्र और सामाजिक न्याय पर चलने वाला मीडिया समूह है। अगर आप भी चाहते हैं कि 'द मूकनायक' हमेशा हाशिए पर खड़े लोगों की आवाज बुलंद करता रहे, बेजुबानों की पीड़ा दिखाते रहें तो सब्सक्राइब करें।
