रहमान यांच्या मते, हसीना या कोणत्याही परिस्थितीत पक्षाचं नेतृत्व दुसऱ्या व्यक्तीकडे सोपवण्यास तयार नाहीत. हाच मुद्दा हसीना आणि अवामी लीग या दोघांसाठी अडचणीचा ठरू शकतो. पक्षाचं अस्तित्व टिकवायचं असेल, तर त्याला नवीन नेतृत्वाचा शोध घ्यावा लागू शकतो.
दुसरीकडे, बांगलादेश एंटरप्राइज इन्स्टिट्यूटचे वरिष्ठ संशोधन संचालक फैज सोभान यांनी अल जजिराला सांगितलं की, मायदेशी परतण्याच्या घोषणेमुळे हसीना राजकीयदृष्ट्या चर्चेत राहतात. त्याचबरोबर, देशातील आपल्या समर्थकांची मनःस्थिती, कल जाणून घेण्याची त्यांना संधीही मिळते.
सोभान यांच्या मते, हसीना प्रत्यक्षात मायदेशी परतण्याची शक्यता तशी कमीच आहे. कारण असं केल्यास त्यांना मृत्युदंडाला सामोरं जावं लागू शकतं किंवा उर्वरित आयुष्य तुरुंगात घालवावं लागू शकतं.
अल जजिराशी बोलताना अमेरिकेचे माजी मुत्सद्दी जॉन डॅनिलोविच यांनीही हसीना यांच्या मायदेशी परतण्याच्या घोषणेमागे आपल्या समर्थकांना एकत्र आणण्याचा प्रयत्न असल्याचं म्हटलं होतं.
त्यांच्या मते, डिसेंबरमध्ये मायदेशी परतण्याची घोषणा करून बांगलादेशातील कमी होत चाललेलं आपलं राजकीय महत्त्व पुन्हा चर्चेत आणण्याचा हसीना यांचा प्रयत्न आहे.
शेख हसीना यांनी मायदेशी परतण्यासाठी निवडलेली तारीखही राजकीयदृष्ट्या महत्त्वपूर्ण आहे. 16 डिसेंबर 1971 रोजी बांगलादेश मुक्तिसंग्राम संपला होता.
हा दिवस बांगलादेशच्या इतिहासात विशेष महत्त्वाचा आहे. हसीना यांचे वडील शेख मुजीबुर रहमान हे बांगलादेशच्या स्वातंत्र्यलढ्यातील प्रमुख नेत्यांपैकी एक होते.
अशा प्रकारे, विजय दिनी मायदेशी परतण्याची घोषणा करून हसीना आपल्या राजकीय वारशाची आणि बांगलादेशच्या स्वातंत्र्यलढ्यातील आपल्या कुटुंबाच्या योगदानाची आठवण करून देत आहेत.
2. अवामी लीगच्या हालचाली आणि हिंसाचार का वाढत आहेत?
बांगलादेशमध्ये अवामी लीगचे नेते आणि कार्यकर्ते पुन्हा सक्रिय होत असल्याने तणाव वाढत आहे. अशा वेळी हसीना यांनी मायदेशी परतण्याची घोषणा केली आहे.
बीबीसी बांगलाच्या वृत्तानुसार, गेल्या काही आठवड्यांपासून अवामी लीगचे नेते आणि कार्यकर्ते पुन्हा सक्रिय होऊन आपली उपस्थिती दाखवण्याचा प्रयत्न करत आहेत.
विशेषतः गोपालगंजसह अनेक जिल्ह्यांमध्ये आंदोलनं, तोडफोड आणि जाळपोळीच्या घटना घडल्या आहेत. या हिंसाचाराला आळा घालण्यासाठी सरकारनेही अनेक उपाययोजनाही केल्या आहेत.
इथे लक्षात घेण्यासारखी गोष्ट म्हणजे अवामी लीगच्या राजकीय हालचालींवर बंदी आहे. अशा परिस्थितीही पक्षाचे नेते आणि कार्यकर्ते सार्वजनिक ठिकाणी आंदोलन करत असल्याने सरकारसमोर कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्था राखण्याचं आव्हान उभं राहिलं आहे.
हसीना यांच्यासाठी नवीन पासपोर्ट आणि ओळखपत्राची मागणी केल्यानंतर बांगलादेशातील हिंसाचार वाढला आहे. गोपालगंजमध्ये त्यांच्या समर्थकांनी केलेली आंदोलनं हिंसक झाली. या घटनांमध्ये काही जणांचा मृत्यूही झाला आहे.
या घडामोडींमुळे सरकारची चिंता केवळ हसीना यांच्या मायदेशी परतण्यापुरती मर्यादित नाही. त्यांच्या परतण्याच्या घोषणेमुळे अवामी लीगचे नेते, कार्यकर्ते आणि समर्थक पुन्हा एकत्र येऊ शकतात, अशी सरकारला भीती आहे.
याच कारणामुळे सरकारने डिसेंबरच्या आसपास सीमेवरील सुरक्षा आणि देखरेख वाढवण्याबाबत भाष्य केलं आहे.
3. बांगलादेश सरकारने सीमेवर बीजीबीला सतर्क का केलं?
बीबीसी बांगलाच्या वृत्तानुसार, बांगलादेशच्या पंतप्रधानांचे माहिती आणि प्रसारण सल्लागार डॉ. जाहेद उर रहमान यांनी सांगितलं की, सीमेवरून होणारी घुसखोरी रोखण्यासाठी बॉर्डर गार्ड बांगलादेशला (बीजीबी) सतर्क राहण्याच्या सूचना देण्यात आल्या आहेत.
जाहेद उर रहमान यांच्या म्हणण्यानुसार, अवामी लीगचे हजारो नेते आणि कार्यकर्ते परदेशात आहेत. त्यांच्याविरोधात गुन्हेही दाखल करण्यात आले आहेत.
डिसेंबरच्या जवळपास गुन्हे दाखल असलेली एखादी व्यक्ती देशात येण्याचा प्रयत्न केल्यास तिला अटक करून कायदेशीर कारवाई करता यावी, यासाठी सीमेवरील सुरक्षा वाढवण्यात आल्याचं त्यांनी सांगितलं.
हे वक्तव्य फार महत्त्वाचं आहे. कारण सरकार हसीना यांच्या परतण्याकडे केवळ एका व्यक्तीच्या मायदेशी परतण्याच्या दृष्टीने पाहत नाही. देशाबाहेर असलेले अवामी लीगचे नेते आणि कार्यकर्तेही परतू शकतात, अशी सरकारला चिंता आहे.
परंतु, सरकारच्या या भीतीचा अर्थ मोठ्या प्रमाणावर घुसखोरी होण्याची शक्यता आहे, असा होत नाही. ही केवळ सरकारने केलेली सुरक्षा व्यवस्था आहे.
4. सरकार इतकी कडक भूमिका का घेत आहे?
शेख हसीना यांच्या परतण्याबाबत बांगलादेश सरकारमधील दोन वरिष्ठ अधिकाऱ्यांनी केलेल्या विधानांवरून सरकारची भूमिका समजून घेण्यास मदत होते.
परराष्ट्र व्यवहार राज्यमंत्री हुमायून कबीर यांनी 24 नोव्हेंबरला परदेशी राजनैतिक प्रतिनिधींना माहिती दिल्यानंतर पत्रकारांशी बोलताना सांगितलं, "शेख हसीना यांना कडक सुरक्षेत आणि बेड्या घालूनच बांगलादेशमध्ये आणलं जाऊ शकतं."
त्यांनी सांगितलं की, एखाद्या आरोपीला सामान्य प्रवाशाप्रमाणे देशात येण्याची परवानगी दिली जाऊ शकत नाही.
त्यांनी अवामी लीगवर दहशतवादाला प्रोत्साहन दिल्याचा आरोपही केला. त्यांच्या मते, बांगलादेशातील दहशतवादाचा संबंध अवामी लीगशी आहे.
दुसरीकडे, आंतरराष्ट्रीय गुन्हे न्यायाधिकरणाचे मुख्य सरकारी वकील मोहम्मद अमीनुल इस्लाम यांनी शेख हसीना यांना आणण्यासाठी विमान पाठवण्याच्या मागणीला 'अभूतपूर्व' मागणी म्हटलं आहे.
बीबीसी बांगलाच्या वृत्तानुसार, त्यांनी म्हटलं की, एखाद्या फरार दोषीला मायदेशी आणण्यासाठी दुसऱ्या देशाकडे विमान मागण्याची घटना जगात अत्यंत दुर्मीळ आहे.
अवामी लीगला दहशतवादी संघटना घोषित करावं की नाही, याची चौकशी सुरू असल्याचंही त्यांनी सांगितलं. या चौकशीत पक्ष दहशतवादी कारवायांमध्ये सहभागी असल्याचं सिद्ध झालं, तर सरकार किंवा न्यायाधिकरण त्याच्याविरोधात कायदेशीर कारवाई करू शकतं, असंही ते म्हणाले.
याचा अर्थ, शेख हसीना यांच्या परतण्यासोबतच अवामी लीगच्या संघटनेचं भवितव्य आणि तिच्या कायदेशीर स्थितीचाही प्रश्न समोर आला आहे.
5. भारताची भूमिका काय आहे?
शेख हसीना यांच्या परतण्याबाबत भारताची भूमिका सर्वात महत्त्वाची ठरणार आहे. ऑगस्ट 2024 पासून त्या भारतात राहत आहेत. बांगलादेश सरकारने यापूर्वीच त्यांच्या प्रत्यार्पणाची मागणी केली आहे.
भारत आणि बांगलादेश यांच्यात 2013 मध्ये प्रत्यार्पण करार झाला होता. याच करारानुसार शेख हसीना यांना बांगलादेशात परत पाठवण्याची मागणी सरकार करत आहे.
मात्र, दोन्ही देशांमध्ये असा करार असला, तरी भारताला शेख हसीना यांना बांगलादेशला सोपवावं लागेलच, असं नाही.
या करारात काही परिस्थितींमध्ये प्रत्यार्पणास नकार देण्याची तरतूद आहे. त्यामध्ये राजकीय स्वरूपाच्या गुन्ह्यांचाही समावेश आहे. परंतु, काही गंभीर गुन्ह्यांना या नियमातून सूट देण्यात आलेली नाही.
भारताच्या परराष्ट्र मंत्रालयाने एप्रिल 2026 मध्ये म्हटलं होतं की, बांगलादेशने केलेल्या प्रत्यार्पणाच्या मागणीची तपासणी सुरू आहे. तसेच, बांगलादेशच्या नवीन सरकारसोबत सकारात्मक चर्चा करण्याची भारताची इच्छा आहे.
परंतु, 'ढाका ट्रिब्यून'ने दिलेल्या वृत्तानुसार, बांगलादेश सरकारचे माहिती आणि प्रसारण सल्लागार जाहेद उर रहमान यांनी 24 नोव्हेंबरला एक महत्त्वाचं वक्तव्य केलं आहे.
त्यांनी सांगितलं की, शेख हसीना यांच्या परतण्याबाबत बांगलादेश सरकारची चर्चा शेख हसीना यांच्याशी नव्हे, तर भारताशी सुरू आहे. त्या बांगलादेशात कशा परततील, याबाबतही भारताशी चर्चा केली जाईल, असंही त्यांनी स्पष्ट केलं.
त्यांच्या मते, शेख हसीना यांना बांगलादेशात परतायचं असेल आणि बांगलादेश सरकारही त्यांना परत बोलावू इच्छित असेल, तर भारताने त्यांना बांगलादेशच्या सोपवण्याबाबत संकोच करू नये.
या वक्तव्यामुळे परराष्ट्र राज्यमंत्र्यांनी केलेल्या बेड्या घालून आणण्याच्या वक्तव्यापेक्षा सरकारची वेगळी भूमिका दिसून येते. शेख हसीना यांच्याशी थेट चर्चा करण्याऐवजी त्यांच्या प्रत्यार्पणाच्या प्रक्रियेबाबत भारताशी चर्चा करण्याची बांगलादेश सरकारची इच्छा असल्याचे दिसून येते.
6. पासपोर्ट रद्द झाल्यावर हसीना बांगलादेशात कशा परतणार?
शेख हसीना यांच्या परतण्याच्या मार्गात पासपोर्टची एक मोठी व्यावहारिक अडचण आहे.
ऑगस्ट 2024 मध्ये शेख हसीना भारतात आल्यानंतर काही महिन्यांनी बांगलादेश सरकारने त्यांचा राजनैतिक पासपोर्ट रद्द केला होता.
शेख हसीना यांनी आता नवीन पासपोर्टसाठी आणि राष्ट्रीय ओळखपत्रासाठी अर्ज केला आहे. ही कागदपत्रं देण्याची मागणी त्यांनी बांगलादेश सरकारकडे केली आहे.
त्यांच्या प्रवक्त्यांचं म्हणणं आहे की, ज्याप्रमाणे बांगलादेशच्या विमानातून शेख हसीना यांना भारतात आणलं होतं, त्याच पद्धतीने आता त्यांना परत नेण्याची व्यवस्थाही बांगलादेश सरकारने केली पाहिजे.
परंतु बांगलादेश सरकारने ही मागणी फेटाळली आहे.
7. बांगलादेशात परतल्यास हसीना यांना मृत्युदंड होईल का?
नोव्हेंबर 2025 मध्ये बांगलादेशच्या आंतरराष्ट्रीय गुन्हे न्यायाधिकरणाने शेख हसीना यांना मानवतेविरुद्धच्या गुन्ह्यांमध्ये दोषी ठरवलं होतं. त्यानंतर त्यांच्या अनुपस्थितीत त्यांना मृत्युदंडाची शिक्षा सुनावली होती.
हा खटला 2024 मधील विद्यार्थी आंदोलनादरम्यान झालेला हिंसाचार आणि त्यावर करण्यात आलेल्या कारवाईशी संबंधित होता. संयुक्त राष्ट्रांने दिलेल्या माहितीनुसार, या आंदोलनादरम्यान सुमारे 1400 लोक मारले गेले होते.
शेख हसीना यांनी त्यांच्यावर लावण्यात आलेले सर्व आरोप फेटाळले आहेत. त्यांच्या अनुपस्थितीत हा खटला चालवण्यात आला आणि आपली बाजू मांडण्याची योग्य संधी मिळाली नाही, असं त्यांचं म्हणणं आहे.
आता प्रश्न असा आहे की, जर त्या बांगलादेशात परतल्या तर त्यांना या निकालाविरोधात अपील करण्याची संधी मिळेल का?
असोसिएटेड प्रेसच्या 24 नोव्हेंबरच्या वृत्तानुसार, शेख हसीना यांना निकालाविरोधात अपील करण्यासाठी 30 दिवसांची मुदत देण्यात आली होती. मात्र, ही मुदत आता संपुष्टात आली आहे. त्यामुळे त्यांच्या फाशीला रोखण्यासाठी आता सर्वसाधारण कायदेशीर मार्ग उरलेला नाही, असं सरकारी वकिलांचं म्हणणं आहे. परंतु, राष्ट्रपतींना त्यांची शिक्षा माफ करण्याचा अधिकार आहे.
त्यामुळे शेख हसीना बांगलादेशमध्ये परतल्यास सर्वात आधी त्यांच्या अटकेची आणि शिक्षेची अंमलबजावणी करण्याची कायदेशीर प्रक्रिया सुरू होईल. परंतु, बांगलादेशात पोहोचताच त्यांना फाशी दिली जाईल, असं म्हणणं चुकीचं ठरेल.
(बीबीसीसाठी कलेक्टिव्ह न्यूजरूमचे प्रकाशन)

title: Delhi Police beats and detains a Caravan journalist during CEC protests
description: Caravan staffer Ryan Thomas was covering the protests against Gyanesh Kumar and SIR, which the government has tried to quash with an unprecedented police mobilisation in the capital.
author: The Caravan
content:
We’re glad this article found its way to you. If you’re not a subscriber, we’d love for you to consider subscribing—your support helps make this journalism possible. Either way, we hope you enjoy the read. Click to subscribe: subscribing
The Delhi Police detained and brutally beat up The Caravan’s assistant multimedia producer, Ryan Thomas, on 11 October. Ryan was covering the protests against Gyanesh Kumar and SIR, which the government has tried to quash with an unprecedented police mobilisation in the capital, with multiple trains and metros halted, and with internet shut down across central Delhi. Earlier in the day, the Supreme Court had directed that, among other things, journalists “shall not be hindered in discharge of their professional duties in any manner whatsoever.”
Around 6 pm, on Janpath Road, as the police were detaining protesters, Ryan started following and recording a video of a group of policemen taking an individual to a detention bus parked nearby. One of them, Assistant Sub-Inspector Kapil Kumar—who was, unlike the others, wearing a name tag—turned and asked Ryan, “Tum kya kar rahe ho yeh”—what are you doing? Suddenly, three cops rushed towards Ryan and began manhandling and hitting him, while dragging him to the detention bus. Ryan repeatedly told them he is a journalist, and his press card was hanging from his neck via a lanyard and visibly displayed.
Inside the bus, five police (two more had come into the bus by then) hit Ryan on the head multiple times and tried to snatch his phone. They tried to force him to delete the images he had recorded. When he refused, stating that he was willing to cooperate with them but would not give up his phone or camera, they intensified the beating. They tried to break his camera and goaded him. One of them said, “Camera se zyada deshbhakti aa raha hai logon main aajkal”—people are feeling a bit too much nationalism because of cameras these days.
A few minutes later, about two other policemen came into the bus. They began saying “Isko doosri gadi mein le chalte hain. Isko doosri jagah le ke jaenge, kyunki ye samajh nahin raha hai”—Let’s take him elsewhere, in a different vehicle, since he is not quite getting it. Kapil Kumar handed Ryan over to these policemen. As he was being taken out of the bus, Ryan asked the two officials not to hit him, since he was cooperating with them. At that point, one of them slapped him hard on the face.
Ryan was pushed into a police car where the detainee he had been trying to record was sitting, along with three other police officials. These officials asked Ryan his name. When they heard it, they slapped him. They asked him his father’s name, and again slapped him upon hearing his answer. Again, they asked him to delete footage from his phone and hand it over. When he refused, a policeman prodded him in the stomach with the butt of his gun. At one point, a policeman pointed to a scar on his own hand and tried to insist to Ryan, “You have done this.”
Finally, the vehicle arrived at the G Block of Connaught Place, where police and paramilitary personnel were shoving more protesters into detention buses. The police threatened to put Ryan in a bus but finally let him go.
Ryan reached the emergency room at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital at 7pm, with three colleagues from The Caravan. Upon reaching, he clearly told the RML staff that the police had beat him up while he was reporting on the protests and that he wanted a medico-legal certificate. He repeated the same to the police, as a part of the MLC proceedings. The doctors examined him and ordered some tests, including a CT scan. Once the tests were done, after more than three hours, Ryan was shown the MLC. Under the heading of “Gist of incident as stated by the injured/accompanying person,” there was a sub heading of “Alleged history.” The authorities had written “injury during protest on 11 oct 26 at 6.30pm cannaught place, c /o headache.” They did not mention that the police had caused the injury. When he, and our other staffers, insisted that this fact be mentioned in the MLC, the authorities refused and asked them to meet the medical superintendent the next day if they wished.
The Caravan reached out to Rajeev Ranjan, the Delhi Police public-relations officer, and Sachin Sharma, the deputy commissioner of police for the New Delhi district, but did not receive a response.

title: The ongoing fight for justice for Narendra Dabholkar
description: Hamid Dabholkar talks about the life and legacy of his father, the rationalist and activist Narendra Dabholkar, who was murdered thirteen years ago. Hamdi discusses developments of the ongoing legal battle and the larger struggle for rationalism that he and the Maharashtra Andhashraddha Nirmoolan Samiti, the organisation his father founded, continue to wage.
author: Shiv Inder Singh
content:
We’re glad this article found its way to you. If you’re not a subscriber, we’d love for you to consider subscribing—your support helps make this journalism possible. Either way, we hope you enjoy the read. Click to subscribe: subscribing
On 18 August 2026, the Bombay High Court stayed the life sentence given to Sachin Andure, who was convicted by a special court for the murder of Narendra Dabholkar, the rationalist, activist and founder of the Maharashtra Andhashraddha Nirmoolan Samiti. The bench granted him bail, citing “extremely weak” evidence and that Andure had a fair chance of acquittal in his pending appeal.
On the morning of 20 August 2013, 67-year-old Dabholkar was shot dead in Pune by two men. More than a decade later, on 10 May 2024, a special CBI court in Pune convicted Sharad Kalaskar and Andure of his murder and sentenced them to life imprisonment, while acquitting the alleged mastermind Virendrasinh Tawde, a lawyer named Sanjiv Punalekar, and his assistant, Vikram Bhave, of murder, criminal conspiracy, and other charges. The court also found the three accused not guilty under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. The Dabholkar family filed an appeal in the high court challenging the acquittal of the three accused.
Andure and Kalaskar filed separate appeals challenging their convictions. Kalaskar was granted bail by the Bombay High Court in April. Dabholkar’s family and the MANS opposed the bail application in April.
In the years following Dabholkar’s murder, the thinker and writer Govind Pansare, the intellectual and activist MM Kalburgi, and the journalist Gauri Lankesh were killed in a similar fashion. Their murders were shown to be part of a conspiracy to suppress rational and progressive voices. The perpetrators of these murders were associated with the Hindu right-wing organisation Sanatan Sanstha, which consistently opposed Dabholkar’s rational views and called his campaign—which included enacting a law against superstitions in Maharashtra—anti-Hindu. Following Dabholkar’s death, the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly passed the Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act in 2013, which remains in effect today.

title: India–China relations are now shaped entirely on Beijing’s terms
description: Beijing views Modi’s India as a state that projects aggressive rhetoric on domestic television channels but lacks the material and military strength to back up its words.
author: Sushant Singh
content:
We’re glad this article found its way to you. If you’re not a subscriber, we’d love for you to consider subscribing—your support helps make this journalism possible. Either way, we hope you enjoy the read. Click to subscribe: subscribing
Salman Khan set out to star in a film about the Galwan clash, in June 2020, in which twenty Indian soldiers died confronting Chinese troops. Since then, the filmmakers have had to change its title, Battle of Galwan, to Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace. They had to reshoot forty percent of the film to erase direct references to China and scrub out the explicit Galwan context. The narrative has shifted from a nationalistic military showdown into a broader human drama about the cost of war. These changes followed a new directive from the defence ministry, which judged that, even though it had earlier approved the script, portraying China as an adversary was not the right call at present. Narendra Modi, in seeking an accommodation with Beijing, is also attempting to control how Indians remember their soldiers’ deaths.
The producers of The Lion of Galwan, a biopic tracking the bravery of the sepoy Gurtej Singh, who died in the Galwan clash, shelved the film after the government’s decree. Without an authentic depiction of the actual combat and geopolitical context, they felt, the film had lost its purpose. Compare this to Haqeeqat, Chetan Anand’s seminal 1964 film about the 1962 Sino-India war, made with extensive support from the defence ministry. Under Modi, India has now arrived at a moment when even naming the adversary in a recent military clash threatens political sensitivities and diplomatic interests.
Khan’s film teaser had sparked online criticism in China, with the Global Times claiming that it “distorted facts” and fueled anti-China sentiment. On Chinese social-media platforms such as Weibo, users accused Bollywood of rewriting history and violating historical facts. Indian official sources initially defended the film as artistic expression, but the Modi government soon stepped in, to protect ties with Beijing. Asked about the issue, the ministry of external affairs spokesperson said film-production regulation in India was “looked after by the relevant authorities”—meaning the ministries of information and broadcasting, and defence, respectively. The I&B ministry has now given a no-objection certificate to Khan’s film after the new narrative reportedly casts India–China relations in a more positive light.
The Modi government's interventions in film projects on Galwan were driven by the shift initiated by the October 2024 India–China border understanding—a direct diplomatic concession to Beijing. What India received in return is much less clear. Since that understanding, followed by a meeting between Modi and Xi at Kazan, the official ecosystem in India has engineered a systematic attempt to project a sense of normalcy in bilateral relations. Meetings between senior officials and ministers have resumed, diplomatic exchanges have gathered pace and official language has grown more reassuring, particularly from the Indian side. This narrative relies on deliberate evasion concerning the actual ground situation across eastern Ladakh.

title: Saharanpur Showdown Before UP Polls 2027: Akhilesh’s Move Challenges Imran Masood’s Clout
description: The SP named Ashu Malik for Saharanpur and Umar Ali Khan for Behat. Both won their seats in 2022. This move has infuriate Masood who repornded with a blunt message: “Hum bhikhari nahi hain" (We are not beggers)
author: Aryan Dwivedi
content:
- The SP named sitting MLAs Ashu Malik and Umar Ali Khan for Saharanpur and Behat while seat-sharing talks with the Congress were still underway.
- Congress MP Imran Masood objected, saying the announcements showed a lack of seriousness and declaring, “Hum bhikhari nahi hain.”
- The row is sharpened by Masood’s political roots in Saharanpur and the SP’s record of winning both seats in 2022.
The Samajwadi Party’s first list of five candidates has put the allaince talks with Congress in danger ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. By naming candidates for Saharanpur and Behat, two Assembly seats in Congress MP Imran Masood’s home district, the SP has staked its claim while negotiations are still open. This move has infuriate Masood who repornded with a blunt message: “Hum bhikhari nahi hain" (We are not beggers).
The clash has put Masood’s standing in western Uttar Pradesh at the centre of the dispute. He represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and has a long political record in the district, while the SP has nominated its sitting MLAs in both constituencies.
Masood Says 'There's a Lack Of Seriousness'
The SP named Ashu Malik for Saharanpur and Umar Ali Khan for Behat. Both won their seats in 2022. The party also nominated Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mehboob Ali from Amroha and Jyoti Lodhi from Lalitpur. The Congress had sought Behat and Saharanpur, according to media reports.
Masood objected to the announcements coming before the alliance talks were settled. “There is a lack of seriousness in this matter because while you are holding talks on one side, you are making declarations on the other,” he said.
He also questioned whether the SP wanted to fight “me, the Congress, or the BJP?” Masood said the Congress leadership would decide whether to continue negotiations, adding: “I will fight for my party; I will fight for the existence of my party.”
Why Saharanpur And Behat Matter
Masood won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in 2024. His political roots in the district go back further: he was elected MLA from Muzaffarabad in 2007, a constituency renamed Behat after delimitation. His uncle, former MP Rasheed Masood, represented Saharanpur several times, including as a Samajwadi Party candidate in 2004.
That history gives Masood a strong local profile, but the SP also has an electoral case for retaining the two seats. Umar Ali Khan won Behat by 37,880 votes in 2022, while Ashu Malik won Saharanpur by 30,745. However it is important to understand that Masood was in SP during the 2022 elections and played an important role in those victories.
A 26-Seat offer, A Larger Congress Claim
The dispute over the two constituencies reflects a wider gap in the seat-sharing talks. SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said his party had offered the Congress 26 seats: two currently held by the Congress, four where it finished second in 2022, and 20 where the SP had received 60,000 to 70,000 votes while the Congress had polled around 2,000.
The Congress has submitted a list of around 130 constituencies, according to reports. Its Uttar Pradesh in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, said discussions covered all 403 Assembly seats. “26 seats? There is no such discussion about 26 seats,” he said, adding that the parties would announce an “amicable, respectable settlement” once talks were concluded. Gautam also said announcing candidates while negotiations continued “should have been avoided.”
Akhilesh Yadav has asked the Congress to suggest additional constituencies beyond the 26 in the SP’s priority list. He said the seat-sharing discussions were still underway and that alliances were formed to win: “The purpose of an alliance is victory.”
SP Defends Its Move; NDA Leaders Predicts Collapse
SP leaders have framed the early nominations as a decision based on winnability and preparation. MP Rajeev Rai said the party’s priority was victory, not a particular seat. He argued that constituencies held by sitting MLAs with significant winning margins should not be handed to another party.
SP MP SP Singh Patel defended the list, saying candidates needed time to reach voters and work on electoral rolls. On the Saharanpur seats, he said: “If two seats in Saharanpur have been declared, what is the problem? There are other seats there too; they will get whatever falls into their share.” He added: “Let them name their candidates—we have already declared ours.”
Masood hit back at Patel, saying the SP MP owed his parliamentary membership to Rahul Gandhi. “Many others like him contested elections in 2019 as well; it is a miracle of Rahul Gandhi post-2019 that he is an MP today,” he said.
NDA leaders also criticised the opposition alliance. Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brijesh Pathak called the SP-Congress partnership an “incompatible marriage”, alleging that bitterness between the parties would prevent their workers from campaigning together.
Uttar Pradesh minister OP Rajbhar accused the SP of betraying the Congress and said the candidate list was intended to pressure its ally. He also alleged that the move was aimed at stopping Muslim voters from shifting towards a possible alliance involving Chandrashekhar Azad and Asaduddin Owaisi.
A test For The Alliance
The parties’ electoral record gives them reason to cooperate—and makes the seat-sharing terms consequential. In 2022, when they contested separately, the SP won 111 Assembly seats and the Congress two. Their 2017 alliance won 54 seats—47 for the SP and seven for the Congress. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, they contested together and won 43 of Uttar Pradesh’s 80 seats.
Neither party has said negotiations are over. But the SP’s nominations have put Saharanpur and Behat at the heart of the bargaining, while Masood’s public rebuke has made clear that the Congress is contesting the terms of the deal.

title: Deepathoon Dispute In Tamil Nadu: Temple, Dargah & The Political Controversy Over Karthigai Deepam
UP Assembly Elections 2027: Can Congress Win Back Dalit, Muslim And OBC Voters?
description: With a renewed focus on Dalit outreach, Muslim voters, Brahmin support and non-Yadav OBC communities, Congress is attempting to rebuild its political base in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
author: Saher Hiba Khan
content:
- Congress is using caste-based outreach to rebuild its Dalit, Muslim, Brahmin and OBC support ahead of the 2027 UP Assembly elections.
- The party is seeking to attract non-Jatav Dalit and non-Yadav OBC voters amid the BSP's declining influence.
- Weak grassroots organisation and seat-sharing tensions with Akhilesh Yadav's Samajwadi Party remain major hurdles for Congress.
The Congress is attempting to rebuild its political base in Uttar Pradesh by bringing leaders from different caste and religious communities into key organisational positions. With the 2027 Assembly elections approaching, the party is looking to recover its traditional upper-caste, Muslim and Dalit support base while expanding its outreach to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), including extremely backward communities. But with its electoral footprint shrinking over three decades and its dependence on the Samajwadi Party (SP) continuing, the question is whether this recalibration can translate into votes and an independent political presence.
The latest appointments in the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) reflect an attempt to reconstruct the social coalition that once sustained Congress's dominance in the state. But representation alone will not be enough: the party must rebuild its organisation and regain the confidence of voters who have shifted towards regional parties.
Congress's attempt to recover its lost social coalition
The Congress's organisational reshuffle in October 2026 brought leaders from different communities into prominent positions in its Uttar Pradesh unit. Aradhana Mishra, a Brahmin leader and three-time MLA from Rampur Khas, replaced Ajay Rai as UPCC president. Saharanpur MP Imran Masood was appointed working president, while Devinder Nishad and Alok Prasad were named senior vice-presidents.
The appointments reflect an attempt to combine upper-caste and Muslim representation with outreach to OBC and Dalit communities. Mishra is a prominent Brahmin leader, while Masood has a support base among Muslim voters in western Uttar Pradesh. Nishad represents an OBC riverine community, while Prasad belongs to the Dalit Pasi community. The reshuffle gives the party leaders associated with different social groups, but their presence in the state leadership does not automatically translate into electoral support. That will depend on whether they can mobilise voters and strengthen the party's organisation in their respective areas.
The difficulty of rebuilding this coalition is evident in Congress's electoral decline. The party won 46 seats with a 17.32 per cent vote share in the 1991 Assembly elections, but secured only two seats with 2.33 per cent in 2022.
The shift was driven by several political developments. The Mandal movement and the rise of the Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party changed the state's caste-based political landscape, drawing sections of OBC and Dalit voters towards parties that claimed to represent their interests. The Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the BJP's expansion helped the latter consolidate upper-caste support. While Dalit voters increasingly moved towards the BSP and many Muslim voters rallied behind the SP, Congress failed to rebuild its organisation or retain its influence among these communities.
In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Congress won six of the 17 seats it contested in Uttar Pradesh as part of its alliance with the SP, securing a vote share of 9.53 per cent. The result marked a recovery from its performance in the 2019 general elections, when it won just one seat with 6.36 per cent of the vote. However, the gains came in an alliance with the SP and do not establish that Congress has rebuilt an independent electoral base in the state.
The Dalit question and the BSP's declining influence
One of the biggest opportunities Congress sees in its recalibration is the changing landscape of Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh. The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), led by Mayawati, once commanded a substantial Dalit support base and played a decisive role in the state's electoral politics. Its declining electoral fortunes have created an opportunity for other parties to seek support among communities that previously backed it.
In a July 2026 report, The Week examined whether Congress could emerge as an alternative political voice for Dalits as the BSP struggles to retain its influence. The report cited estimates suggesting that around 40 per cent of Dalit voters supported the INDIA bloc in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. However, the CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey points to significant differences within the community: The survey estimated that 56 per cent of non-Jatav Dalits supported the INDIA bloc, compared with 25 per cent of Jatav Dalits. The figures show why the Dalit vote cannot be treated as a single political bloc.
Congress is hoping to build on this shift, particularly by reaching non-Jatav Dalits, who account for around half of the state's Dalit population, according to political analyst Aditya Rathi, quoted by The Week. The appointment of Rajendra Pal Gautam as the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge is part of this effort. A former Aam Aadmi Party leader, Gautam previously headed the Congress's Scheduled Caste department and has been tasked with strengthening the party's engagement with Dalit communities in the state.
Speaking to The Week, Gautam said, "Dalits, Muslims and Other Backward Classes account for more than 60 per cent of the state's population and want a proportionate share, but right now only a few communities helm the affairs."
He also argued that Dalit concerns required national-level political attention. “There is a need to take up their issues; if we won’t, then who will?” he said.
The BSP's electoral decline does not automatically translate into support for Congress. The party will need sustained engagement with Dalit communities and an understanding of their differing political loyalties rather than assume that voters moving away from the BSP will automatically support it.
Can Congress expand beyond the SP's traditional support base?
Congress's caste recalibration also has implications for its relationship with the SP. The latter has traditionally drawn considerable support from Muslims and Yadavs, while Congress is attempting to expand the Opposition's social coalition by attracting Dalits, Brahmins and non-Yadav OBC communities.
The CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey found that 92 per cent of Muslim voters and 82 per cent of Yadav voters in Uttar Pradesh supported the INDIA bloc in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The alliance also received 56 per cent of the non-Jatav Dalit vote, but only 25 per cent of the Jatav vote. Among other OBC groups, 59 per cent voted for the NDA, compared with 34 per cent for INDIA. These figures underline the alliance's strength among Muslims and Yadavs, but also reveal the difficulty of expanding its support among other backward communities.
The party's strategy is to complement the SP's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) pitch, which refers to backward classes, Dalits and minorities, by reaching communities beyond the SP's traditional support base.
However, this also creates a political dilemma. Congress wants to strengthen its independent organisation and bargaining position, while the SP remains the larger Opposition force in the state. The tension between these two objectives was visible in the latest seat-sharing negotiations for the 2027 Assembly elections. On November 24, the SP offered Congress 26 seats after the latter submitted a list of around 130 constituencies it wanted to contest. Congress rejected the offer during the next round of talks on November 25, with the party reportedly submitting a revised list of 100–120 seats. The two parties held seat-by-seat discussions covering all 403 constituencies but failed to reach an agreement. Both sides indicated that negotiations would continue.
Representation is not the same as electoral revival
The Congress's caste recalibration comes against the backdrop of a prolonged organisational crisis. Its electoral performance in Uttar Pradesh has remained weak despite repeated attempts at revival. The party's 2017 alliance with the SP, for instance, ended in defeat. Congress contested 114 seats but won only seven, with a vote share of 6.25 per cent. The SP won 47 seats, while the BJP secured 312.
The Indian Express has identified the weakening of Congress's grassroots organisation, the departure of local leaders and workers, frequent leadership changes and dependence on electoral alliances as key reasons for its decline. Leadership appointments alone cannot reverse these weaknesses.
Political analyst and former MP Santosh Bhartiya told The Week that Congress lacked the organisational structure and grassroots presence to contest Uttar Pradesh independently. He argued that the party's real focus was not the 2027 Assembly elections but the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, as it sought to rebuild its social coalition over the longer term. His assessment points to the central difficulty facing Congress: it wants to expand its independent political base, but may not yet have the organisational strength to convert that ambition into electoral gains.
The 2027 Assembly elections will test whether Congress can turn its caste recalibration into electoral gains. The party must win back voters who have shifted towards the SP, BSP and BJP while rebuilding the organisation needed to mobilise them. Its new appointments signal an attempt to regain political ground, but whether that translates into an independent electoral base remains uncertain.

title: Justice Satish Chandra Sharma To Be Remembered For Humility, Cool Temper: CJI
description: CJI Surya Kant Praises Outgoing Supreme Court Judge At Farewell Function
author: Our Correspondent
content:
Justice Satish Chandra Sharma To Be Remembered For Humility, Cool Temper: CJI
CJI Surya Kant Praises Outgoing Supreme Court Judge At Farewell Function
Outgoing Supreme Court judge Justice Satish Chandra Sharma will always be remembered for his humble judicial approach and cool temper, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said on Wednesday.Justice Sharma had the art and capability to navigate and deliver actual justice even if a statute or a provision of law created an impediment, the CJI said, highlighting that deciding a case and delivering justice were not always the same.
He was speaking at a farewell function organised by the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) for Justice Sharma, who is scheduled to retire on November 29. The CJI said that in his zeal to decide all cases, Justice Sharma ensured that not a single lawyer went unheard.
"All talked about the very polite and humble approach of brother Satish, who never loses his temper and is always known to be one of the coolest judges of this court. I think he will always be remembered for that," Justice Kant said.
"As far as we judges are concerned, listening to the members of the bar with a lot of patience is a routine exercise for us. But listening to the members of the bar say kind words about a colleague, who is now demitting office on successful completion of his tenure, is unique and makes the occasion special," he said on a lighter note.
Thanking SCAORA for the farewell, Justice Sharma said a judge does not get every case right. "I believe no one who held this office can claim otherwise. But what a judge can do is read every file, hear every counsel and decide without fear or favour. I leave with one satisfaction from this institution -- that I do not carry a single file home that I did not read or decide without fear or favour. A judge is only as good as the assistance he receives," he said.
The outgoing judge also advised young lawyers to read the brief, be courteous to opponents, and always be truthful to the bench. Attorney General R Venkataramani, SCAORA president Devvrat and others spoke on the occasion. Born on November 30, 1961, in Bhopal, Justice Sharma initially practised in constitutional, service, civil and criminal matters before the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Jabalpur.
He was appointed additional central government counsel on May 28, 1993 and was appointed a senior panel counsel by the Government of India on June 28, 2004. In 2003, at the age of 42, he was designated as a senior advocate by the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
Justice Sharma was elevated as an additional judge of the Madhya Pradesh High Court on January 18, 2008 and was appointed as a permanent judge on January 15, 2010. He was transferred to Karnataka High Court as a judge on December 31, 2020.
Justice Sharma was later appointed as Acting Chief Justice of Karnataka High Court on August 31, 2021 and was elevated as Chief Justice of Telangana High Court on October 11 that year. He was later transferred to the Delhi High Court as Chief Justice and took the oath of office on June 28, 2022. He was elevated as a Supreme Court judge on November 9, 2023.

title: AIMIM Turns Azam Khan's Biryani Dig Into Campaign For 2027 UP Polls
description: Party Organises Hyderabadi Biryani Distribution Drives Across Muslim-Dominated Areas
author: Our Correspondent
content:
AIMIM Turns Azam Khan's Biryani Dig Into Campaign For 2027 UP Polls
Party Organises Hyderabadi Biryani Distribution Drives Across Muslim-Dominated Areas
Turning Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's "Hyderabadi biryani" dig at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi into a political opportunity, the Hyderabad-based party is serving the popular dish in the streets of Uttar Pradesh to drive home its message ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections."People here don't like Hyderabadi biryani. People here like pulao and mutton biryani," Azam Khan had told the media in Rampur when asked about Owaisi, who has entered into an alliance with the Chandrashekhar Azad-led Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) for the elections under the banner of the Samajik Parivartan Morcha.
From Etawah to Bareilly, AIMIM leaders have organised biryani gatherings and distribution programmes, drawing crowds in Muslim-dominated localities and turning a debate over food preferences into a political show of strength. In Bareilly, AIMIM's Uttar Pradesh general secretary Nadeem Qureshi hosted a Hyderabadi biryani gathering at his office on Tuesday night. Party office-bearers, workers and supporters attended the event.
"People have taken a liking to Hyderabadi biryani in the state and its popularity will only increase in coming days," Nadeem told PTI on Wednesday. The Hyderabadi biryani gatherings and distribution programmes began days after Khan's remarks, with AIMIM units organising events in different parts of the state.
Nadeem said such gatherings and distribution drives had been held in several districts, including Rampur, Hathras, Bahraich, Etawah and Sambhal, besides other places. He said such gatherings and the distribution of Hyderabadi biryani would continue across Uttar Pradesh until the 2027 Assembly elections.
In Etawah, the party's district unit organised a biryani distribution programme in the Muslim-dominated Nai Basti locality. A poster featuring Owaisi was also put up at the venue. District president Shamshad Hussain said the programme was organised in response to Khan's remarks. He claimed that "more than 85 per cent of Muslims now favoured Owaisi" and asserted that AIMIM would receive their support in the 2027 elections.
The biryani campaign has added an interesting dimension to the emerging political contest in Uttar Pradesh, where AIMIM is seeking to expand its presence beyond its traditional base in Hyderabad.
Owaisi has been pitching their alliance as an alternative to the BJP, while accusing the Samajwadi Party and Congress of failing to adequately represent Muslims. During a recent rally in Meerut, he said the alliance would first remove Yogi Adityanath from power in Uttar Pradesh and subsequently take on Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi.
The AIMIM chief has also repeatedly targeted the Samajwadi Party over the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, alleging that the then Akhilesh Yadav government failed to adequately assist those displaced by the violence.

title: Chennai's Kamarajar Port to Get 2nd Container Terminal
description: The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs 4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs 2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs 1,858.94 crore for Phase II
author: PTI
content:
Chennai's Kamarajar Port to Get 2nd Container Terminal
The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs 4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs 2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs 1,858.94 crore for Phase II
New Delhi: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the development of the second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu under a public-private partnership (PPP) model at an estimated cost of Rs 4,288.26 crore. According to an official statement, the project envisages a 900-metre-long container terminal with a design draft of 18 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), to be implemented in two phases. The project will be developed on a design, build, finance, operate and transfer (DBFOT) basis.
The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs 4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs 2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs 1,858.94 crore for Phase II.
"The investment is to be arranged by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model," the statement said, adding that the project proposal separately indicates an estimated dredging cost of Rs 450 crore to be borne by Kamarajar Port Ltd (KPL).
The terminal is designed to handle large container vessels, including vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length overall, with a design draft of 18 metres. This will strengthen KPL's ability to handle larger mainline vessels and improve connectivity with international shipping routes.
The project is intended to meet the growing demand for containerised export-import (EXIM) cargo from the Chennai–Ennore industrial and economic region and the wider southern hinterland. Key cargo-generating sectors include automobiles and auto components, engineering goods, electronics, chemicals and other manufactured products, the statement said.
KPL handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. The existing container terminal has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per annum and handled approximately 0.7 million TEUs in FY 2025–26, representing utilisation of about 88 per cent.
The project is aligned with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. It is expected to strengthen KPL's position as a container gateway on India's East Coast, improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics chain and support the growth of EXIM trade.
Kamarajar Port, formerly known as Ennore Port, is one of the 12 Major Ports of India and is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Located on the east coast of Tamil Nadu near the Chennai industrial and economic region, the port handles a range of cargo, including coal, petroleum, oil and lubricants, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo. 
( Source : PTI )

title: Mehbooba Questions Omar Over Roadwork at Fragile Sheshnag Lake
description: Environmentalists have raised concerns that the construction activity may damage Sheshnag, a glacial lake in Anantnag, and the alpine nature of its surroundings.
author: PTI
content:
Mehbooba Questions Omar Over Roadwork at Fragile Sheshnag Lake
Environmentalists have raised concerns that the construction activity may damage Sheshnag, a glacial lake in Anantnag, and the alpine nature of its surroundings.
Srinagar: Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti on Wednesday asked Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to explain the extension of the memorandum of understanding with the Border Roads Organisation for a road to the ecologically fragile Sheshnag area along the Amarnath yatra route.
The government, however, denied the charge and accused Mehbooba of misinformation.
Environmentalists have raised concerns that the construction activity may damage Sheshnag, a glacial lake in Anantnag, and the alpine nature of its surroundings.
"Shockingly, on 23 January 2026, the Omar Abdullah-led Cabinet cleared the road to Sheshnag by extending the MoU with BRO's Project Beacon," Mehbooba said on X.
The former chief minister tried to visit the construction site on Tuesday but was stopped by the police.
"In the name of development, it is an assault on our fragile ecology, putting both the Sheshnag ecosystem and the Amarnath Yatra at risk.
"Will the Chief Minister and Tourism Department explain this MoU and the clearance granted? Will they withdraw it before irreversible damage is done?" she asked.
The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) on Monday said that it was carrying out the post-Amarnath Yatra work in compliance with all safety norms and environmental safeguards.
The ruling National Conference hit back at Mehbooba, asserting that the Abdullah government sanctioned no road.
"Why this misinformation and mischief @MehboobaMufti? Where and when was a road approved? MOU in January 2026 was specifically aimed at COMPLETING the PENDING and CRITICAL works on SANJY Tracks. And also Slope Stabilisation and Snow Clearance," party spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said on X.
He dared the former chief minister to prove that the NC government approved the road, or apologise.
An online petition against the construction at the high-altitude lake is gaining momentum with more than 8,000 people signing on.
The petition on Change.org, named "Stop construction around Kashmir's alpine lakes", started by Zarqua Banday, garnered 8,663 signatures. The link briefly appeared broken but has since reappeared on the site.
The petition urged the authorities to engage with local environmental and community groups to develop a sustainable way forward.
It said that in the name of development and easy access, the government plans to construct roads that will cut through untouched havens in Kashmir.
The petitioners urged the government to "consider sustainable tourism initiatives that preserve our natural environment."
"Solutions like guided trekking, limited access permits and eco-friendly accommodations could bring economic benefits without sacrificing our wilderness. Other regions facing similar challenges, like the Swiss Alps, have successfully implemented such strategies. We need to learn from them and prioritise long-term ecological health over short-term gains," the petition read.
Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) chief Tariq Hameed Karra on Tuesday questioned the deployment of an excavator near the lake.
Kashmir's chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, who also signed the petition, said, "We all have to collectively raise our voice to stop the mindless destruction of our ecology at its most fragile places."
The Mirwaiz also challenged Abdullah to speak up on the matter as a public representative.
"Why is our Chief Minister @omarabdullah mute? As people's elected representative it is his duty to speak up and do the needful to ensure this plunder is stopped! I have signed this petition and urge all those who want to save Kashmir's fragile ecology do so," he said on X.
On the other hand, the Jammu and Kashmir BJP on Tuesday accused critics of selective environmental activism, asserting that it would firmly oppose any move to communalise development, undermine the annual pilgrimage or disturb peace in the valley.
"What is being projected as an environmental issue increasingly appears to be an attempt to manufacture controversy, disturb the peaceful atmosphere and exploit religious sentiments for narrow political gains," party spokesperson and former MLC, Girdhari Lal Raina, said in a statement.
Outrage was sparked when a video showed an excavator at work near the high-risk lake in the south Kashmir district.
( Source : PTI )

title: Sheshnag Row: J&K Govt Defends BRO Work, Rejects Eco Damage Claims
description: Opposition parties demand withdrawal of clearances over alleged environmental threat to fragile Himalayan ecosystem
author: Yusuf Jameel
content:
Sheshnag Row: J&K Govt Defends BRO Work, Rejects Eco Damage Claims
Opposition parties demand withdrawal of clearances over alleged environmental threat to fragile Himalayan ecosystem
The controversy surrounding ongoing work near the ecologically sensitive Sheshnag Lake on the Amarnath Yatra route intensified on Wednesday, with the Jammu and Kashmir government firmly defending the project while opposition parties renewed allegations of environmental damage and demanded the withdrawal of official clearances.
J&K's Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment, Altaf Ahmed Wani Kaloo, dismissed concerns that the fragile alpine lake or its surrounding ecosystem had been harmed, asserting that the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) was undertaking only limited work on an already existing pilgrimage track.
Speaking to reporters in Anantnag, Kaloo said the activity involved laying tiles and upgrading a designated walking route used by pilgrims during the annual Amarnath Yatra, and was being carried out strictly under the framework of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed in 2023.
Seeking to allay fears triggered by widely circulated videos of earth-moving machinery operating in the area, the minister maintained that there had been no damage to Sheshnag Lake. He said the government had directed officials to ensure that all work remained confined to the approved alignment and complied fully with the environmental safeguards incorporated into the agreement. According to Kaloo, the Forest Department is closely monitoring ongoing activities to prevent any violation of stipulated conditions.
Stressing that environmental conservation remained a priority, the minister said safeguarding the region's delicate ecology was a shared responsibility. He reiterated that the administration was committed to protecting the Himalayan environment while simultaneously facilitating infrastructure necessary for pilgrims undertaking one of the country's most significant religious journeys.
The minister also pushed back against criticism from opposition parties, accusing them of politicising the issue. He alleged that certain political forces, particularly the People's Democratic Party (PDP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), were exaggerating the controversy for electoral advantage ahead of upcoming political contests.
Responding to demands that the project be scrapped in view of environmental concerns, Kaloo said the matter could not be viewed in isolation from judicial directions governing pilgrimage infrastructure. He pointed out that the maintenance of the traditional route was linked to Supreme Court directives concerning facilities for Amarnath pilgrims. "No minister is above the Supreme Court," he said, adding that the 12-foot-wide track was essential for ensuring the safe movement and convenience of pilgrims visiting the holy cave shrine.
Kaloo reiterated that the government would not permit any activity beyond the approved scope of work and would ensure that all environmental safeguards envisioned under the 2023 MoU were implemented in both letter and spirit.
The government's defence of the project came hours after former chief minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti launched a fresh attack on the Omar Abdullah-led administration over the proposed road connectivity initiative in the Sheshnag region.
In a strongly worded statement, Mufti questioned the Cabinet's decision to extend the MoU with the BRO under Project Beacon, alleging that the clearance could inflict irreversible damage on one of the Himalayas' most fragile ecological zones. She claimed that the intervention threatened to destabilise the sensitive Sheshnag ecosystem and could ultimately undermine both the environmental integrity and long-term safety of the annual Amarnath Yatra.
Demanding greater transparency, the PDP leader asked Chief Minister Abdullah and the Tourism Department to publicly disclose the details of the MoU and the exact nature of the approval granted to the project. She also called for the clearance to be withdrawn before any ecological consequences became permanent.
Mufti's intervention comes amid growing debate over the use of heavy machinery in the high-altitude region, with environmental activists and experts expressing concern about possible impacts on glacial terrain, alpine biodiversity and water systems linked to the Lidder River basin.
Joining issue with the PDP, ruling National Conference chief spokesperson and MLA Tanvir Sadiq accused Mufti of selectively raising environmental concerns years after the project had already been approved. Sadiq noted that planning for the project began in 2022, the MoU was signed in 2023, and the relevant approval process was completed in 2024.
Questioning the timing of the PDP's objections, he asked why concerns had not been raised during earlier stages of the project when policy decisions were being finalised. The NC leader insisted that neither the government nor his party would permit any environmental violations. He said Chief Minister Abdullah had already directed the concerned departments, particularly the Forest and Environment departments, to submit reports immediately if any deviation from approved plans was found. Any violation, he said, would invite prompt action.
Emphasising communal harmony, Sadiq said Kashmir's tradition of coexistence required respect for all faiths and pilgrimages. At the same time, he maintained that environmental protection would remain non-negotiable and that the government would not allow political forces to turn the controversy into a divisive religious issue.
He further argued that those genuinely concerned about environmental violations should pursue legal and institutional remedies through bodies such as the National Green Tribunal or the courts rather than staging political protests.
The Sheshnag controversy erupted after videos surfaced showing excavation equipment operating along sections of the traditional Pahalgam-Amarnath route near the glacier-fed Sheshnag Lake, located at an altitude of nearly 3,600 metres in south Kashmir's Anantnag district.
Environmentalists have warned that the lake and surrounding alpine landscape are exceptionally sensitive, with concerns ranging from slope instability and erosion to potential impacts on water systems feeding the Lidder River. Several political leaders, climate activists and civil society groups have demanded an independent environmental assessment of the project.
The BRO, however, has consistently maintained that no new road is being constructed. According to the organisation, the work is limited to widening, stabilising and improving existing pilgrimage tracks to enhance safety, reduce congestion and improve accessibility for the hundreds of thousands of pilgrims who undertake the annual yatra.

title: संतोष कुमारी से पहले इन युवाओं ने भी दी सत्ता के धुरंधरों को पटखनी, मेयर-मुखिया और जिला प्रमुख बन रचा इतिहा...
description: देश की जमीनी राजनीति में युवा अपनी मेहनत, शिक्षा और नेतृत्व क्षमता से नई मिसाल कायम कर रहे हैं. केरल की रेशमा मरियम रॉय और आर्या राजेंद्रन से लेकर बिहार की अनुष्का कुमारी और राजस्थान की संतोष कुमारी तक, कम उम्र में बड़ी जिम्मेदारियां संभाल रही ये युवा नेता अपने-अपने क्षेत्रों में विकास, शिक्षा, महिला सशक्तिकरण और बुनियादी ढांचे को मजबूत कर रही हैं, जिससे राजनीति में नई पीढ़ी की भागीदारी को नई दिशा मिली है.
author: Sandeep Gupta
content:
संतोष कुमारी से पहले इन युवाओं ने भी दी सत्ता के धुरंधरों को पटखनी, मेयर-मुखिया और जिला प्रमुख बन रचा इतिहास
Written by:
Agency:News18Hindi
Last Updated:
देश की जमीनी राजनीति में युवा अपनी मेहनत, शिक्षा और नेतृत्व क्षमता से नई मिसाल कायम कर रहे हैं. केरल की रेशमा मरियम रॉय और आर्या राजेंद्रन से लेकर बिहार की अनुष्का कुमारी और राजस्थान की संतोष कुमारी तक, कम उम्र में बड़ी जिम्मेदारियां संभाल रही ये युवा नेता अपने-अपने क्षेत्रों में विकास, शिक्षा, महिला सशक्तिकरण और बुनियादी ढांचे को मजबूत कर रही हैं, जिससे राजनीति में नई पीढ़ी की भागीदारी को नई दिशा मिली है.
पूजा (मुखिया, गरारी पंचायत, गया, बिहार) बिहार के जहानाबाद की रहने वाली पूजा ने 2019 में शादी के बाद ससुराल के प्रोत्साहन पर मुखिया का चुनाव जीतकर अपने परिवार का 50 साल पुराना सपना पूरा किया. शुरुआती दौर में अनुभवहीन बताकर ताने सुनने के बावजूद, गांव की महिलाओं के समर्थन से उन्होंने अपनी नेतृत्व क्षमता साबित की. पूजा ने 'महिला आम सभा' की शुरुआत की, जिसे बाद में गया की 320 पंचायतों में लागू किया गया. उनके नेतृत्व में गरारी पंचायत को 'मॉडल महिला-हितैषी पंचायत' घोषित किया गया. महिला रोजगार, स्वच्छता, नली-गली और पीएम आवास योजना में बेहतरीन काम के लिए उन्हें स्वतंत्रता दिवस समारोह में दिल्ली आमंत्रित किया गया.
संतोष कुमारी (जिला प्रमुख, जैसलमेर, राजस्थान) पश्चिमी राजस्थान के जैसलमेर से मात्र 21 वर्ष, 1 महीने और 6 दिन की उम्र में संतोष कुमारी सबसे कम उम्र की जिला प्रमुख बनकर इतिहास रच चुकी हैं. एक सामान्य और गैर-राजनीतिक परिवार से आने वाली बीए शिक्षित संतोष के पिता ग्राम विकास अधिकारी हैं. पूर्व मंत्री शालेह मोहम्मद और फकीर परिवार के भरोसे पर उन्होंने अनारक्षित सामान्य वार्ड से चुनाव लड़कर 6202 वोटों से शानदार जीत दर्ज की और फिर निर्विरोध जिला प्रमुख चुनी गईं. Gen Z पीढ़ी का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाली संतोष का लक्ष्य वंचित गांवों-ढाणियों का कायाकल्प करना और पिछड़े इलाकों में बेहतर शिक्षा पहुंचाना है.
Advertisement
आर्या राजेंद्रन (तिरुवनंतपुरम, केरल) केरल की आर्या राजेंद्रन ने मात्र 21 वर्ष की आयु में तिरुवनंतपुरम नगर निगम की मेयर बनकर पूरे देश में इतिहास रच दिया था. कॉलेज में बीएससी की पढ़ाई करते हुए उन्होंने पार्षद का चुनाव जीता और फिर देश की सबसे युवा मेयर बनीं. एक साधारण मध्यमवर्गीय परिवार से आने वाली आर्या का कोई बड़ा राजनीतिक पारिवारिक बैकग्राउंड नहीं था. मेयर बनने के बाद उन्होंने शहर में कचरा प्रबंधन, स्वच्छता अभियान, सार्वजनिक परिवहन को बेहतर बनाने और युवाओं को रोजगार से जोड़ने के लिए कई प्रभावी योजनाएं लागू कीं, जिससे वे राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर युवा नेतृत्व की मिसाल बन गईं.

अनुष्का कुमारी (मुखिया, कुशहर पंचायत, शिवहर, बिहार) बिहार के शिवहर जिले की कुशहर पंचायत से महज 21 वर्ष की उम्र में अनुष्का कुमारी सबसे कम उम्र की मुखिया बनी हैं. उन्होंने रीता देवी को 287 वोटों से हराकर यह जीत दर्ज की. बेंगलुरु से हिस्ट्री ऑनर्स में स्नातक की पढ़ाई कर चुकीं अनुष्का पूर्व जिला परिषद सदस्य सुनील सिंह की बेटी हैं और अपने दादा को आदर्श मानती हैं. क्षेत्र की समस्याओं और भ्रष्टाचार को खत्म करने के उद्देश्य से चुनाव लड़ीं अनुष्का आगे भी पढ़ाई जारी रखना चाहती हैं. उनका मानना है कि कड़ी मेहनत और लगन से काम करने पर सफलता खुद पीछे आती है.
रेशमा मरियम रॉय (पत्तनमतिट्टा, केरल) केरल के पत्तनमतिट्टा जिले की रेशमा मरियम रॉय ने भी 21 साल की उम्र में पंचायत चुनाव जीतकर सबसे कम उम्र की पंचायत अध्यक्ष बनने का रिकॉर्ड बनाया था. चुनाव लड़ने के लिए न्यूनतम आयु सीमा 21 वर्ष पूरी करने के ठीक बाद उन्होंने नामांकन दाखिल किया और शानदार जीत हासिल की. अपने कार्यकाल में रेशमा ने ग्रामीण बुनियादी ढांचे, महिलाओं के लिए स्वरोजगार, स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं और डिजिटल साक्षरता को बढ़ावा देने के लिए जमीनी स्तर पर काम किया. बिना किसी राजनीतिक विरासत के अपने काम के दम पर उन्होंने स्थानीय राजनीति में नई ऊर्जा का संचार किया.
Advertisement
रविंद्र सिंह भाटी (शिव, राजस्थान) पश्चिमी राजस्थान के बाड़मेर जिले की शिव विधानसभा सीट से निर्दलीय विधायक बने रविंद्र सिंह भाटी युवाओं के बीच बेहद लोकप्रिय चेहरा हैं. एक साधारण परिवार से आने वाले रविंद्र ने छात्र राजनीति से शुरुआत की और जोधपुर के जयनारायण व्यास विश्वविद्यालय के छात्रसंघ अध्यक्ष बने. इसके बाद 2023 के राजस्थान विधानसभा चुनाव में बिना किसी बड़े दल के समर्थन के निर्दलीय चुनाव लड़कर दिग्गजों को मात दी. उन्होंने अपने क्षेत्र में पेयजल संकट, शिक्षा, रोजगार और सीमावर्ती गांवों के विकास के मुद्दों को विधानसभा में मजबूती से उठाकर अलग पहचान बनाई है.
अंशुमन सिंह राजपूत (कोलायत, राजस्थान) राजस्थान के बीकानेर जिले की कोलायत विधानसभा सीट से विधायक बने अंशुमन सिंह राजपूत राज्य के सबसे युवा विधायकों में से एक हैं. महज 27 साल की उम्र में उन्होंने विधानसभा चुनाव जीतकर युवाओं का प्रतिनिधित्व किया. चुनाव जीतने के बाद उन्होंने अपने क्षेत्र के दूरदराज के गांवों में बिजली, पानी और चिकित्सा सुविधाओं को बेहतर बनाने पर विशेष ध्यान दिया. युवाओं को खेल और शिक्षा के बेहतर अवसर उपलब्ध कराने के साथ-साथ वे ग्रामीण इलाकों में सड़क नेटवर्क को मजबूत करने और किसानों की समस्याओं को सरकार तक पहुंचाने के लिए लगातार सक्रिय रहते हैं.
अदिति सिंह (रायबरेली, उत्तर प्रदेश) उत्तर प्रदेश की रायबरेली सदर सीट से विधायक अदिति सिंह ने भी कम उम्र में सक्रिय राजनीति में कदम रखकर अपनी कार्यशैली से पहचान बनाई. विदेश से उच्च शिक्षा प्राप्त करने के बाद उन्होंने क्षेत्र की राजनीति संभाली और भारी मतों से जीत दर्ज कर विधायक बनीं. अपने विधानसभा क्षेत्र में उन्होंने सड़कों के निर्माण, बिजली आपूर्ति में सुधार, सरकारी स्कूलों के कायाकल्प और महिलाओं की सुरक्षा से जुड़े कई प्रोजेक्ट्स को प्राथमिकता दी. जमीनी स्तर पर लोगों की समस्याओं के त्वरित समाधान और विकास कार्यों के कारण उन्होंने अपने क्षेत्र में मजबूत पकड़ बनाई है.
लेटेस्ट कॉमर्स डील्स, खास डिस्काउंट और बेहतरीन शॉपिंग ऑफर देखने के लिए कंपेयर इंड‍िया✅देखें.

title: 'विनय कुलकर्णी की जमानत रद्द होना, हत्या कर सत्ता का सुख भोगने वालों के लिए एक सबक'
description: Yogesh Gowda Murder: 2016 के चर्चित भाजपा नेता योगेश गौड़ा हत्याकांड में कर्नाटक कांग्रेस नेता और पूर्व विधायक विनय कुलकर्णी को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से बड़ा झटका लगा है. शीर्ष अदालत ने कर्नाटक हाईकोर्ट से मिली उनकी जमानत को रद्द कर दिया है, जिससे कुलकर्णी की कानूनी और सियासी मुश्किलें फिर से बढ़ गई हैं.
author: राकेश रंजन कुमार
content:
'विनय कुलकर्णी की जमानत रद्द होना, हत्या कर सत्ता का सुख भोगने वालों के लिए एक सबक'
Edited by:
Agency:आईएएनएस
Last Updated:
Yogesh Gowda Murder: 2016 के चर्चित भाजपा नेता योगेश गौड़ा हत्याकांड में कर्नाटक कांग्रेस नेता और पूर्व विधायक विनय कुलकर्णी को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से बड़ा झटका लगा है. शीर्ष अदालत ने कर्नाटक हाईकोर्ट से मिली उनकी जमानत को रद्द कर दिया है, जिससे कुलकर्णी की कानूनी और सियासी मुश्किलें फिर से बढ़ गई हैं.
Yogesh Gowda Murder Case: कर्नाटक कांग्रेस नेता और पूर्व विधायक विनय कुलकर्णी को 2016 के भाजपा नेता योगेश गौड़ा हत्याकांड में मिली जमानत रद्द करने के सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसले का व्हिसलब्लोअर ने स्वागत किया है. उन्होंने इसे उन लोगों के लिए सबक बताया, जो मानते हैं कि हत्या जैसे अपराध करने के बाद भी राजनीतिक प्रभाव के दम पर सजा से बच सकते हैं.
धारवाड़ में फैसले पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हुए व्हिसलब्लोअर बसवराज कोरावर ने कहा कि अदालत ने ऐसे लोगों को सबक सिखाया है, जो हत्या करने, सब कुछ संभाल लेने और फिर विधायक बनकर सत्ता का आनंद लेने की सोच रखते हैं.
उन्होंने मीडिया से कहा, “यह अदालत की ओर से उन लोगों को दिया गया सबक है, जो सोचते हैं कि वे हत्या कर सकते हैं, सब कुछ मैनेज कर सकते हैं और फिर भी विधायक बनकर सत्ता का आनंद ले सकते हैं. सभी आरोपियों को सरेंडर करने के लिए कहा गया है. आज मैं खुश हूं और गर्व महसूस कर रहा हूं. धारवाड़ क्षेत्र ने ऐसा नेता नहीं देखा था.”
यह मामला भाजपा नेता और धारवाड़ जिला पंचायत सदस्य योगेश गौड़ा की हत्या से जुड़ा है. 15 जून 2016 को धारवाड़ स्थित उनके जिम में धारदार हथियारों से हमला कर उनकी हत्या कर दी गई थी. शुरुआत में धारवाड़ सब-अर्बन पुलिस ने मामला दर्ज किया और छह लोगों के खिलाफ आरोपपत्र दाखिल किया. बाद में कर्नाटक सरकार ने मामले की जांच केंद्रीय जांच ब्यूरो (सीबीआई) को सौंप दी.

सीबीआई की जांच के अनुसार, हत्या कथित तौर पर एक बड़ी साजिश का हिस्सा थी, जिसे विनय कुलकर्णी ने रचा था. उनके चाचा चंद्रशेखर इंदी उर्फ चंदू मामा और तत्कालीन धारवाड़ सब-अर्बन पुलिस स्टेशन के इंस्पेक्टर सी. टिंगेरिकर भी साजिश में शामिल होने, सबूत नष्ट करने और दूसरों को फंसाने के प्रयासों के आरोपियों में शामिल थे.

title: 4 देशों की सीमा के पास असम में बनेंगे एंटी-ड्रोन सिस्टम और बंकर, 14 एकड़ में लगेगी 50 करोड़ की यूनिट
description: असम में रक्षा उत्पादन की शुरुआत होने जा रही है. सीएम हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने रंगिया में यूनिट की नींव रखी. यहां ड्रोन और एंटी-ड्रोन सिस्टम बनाए जाएंगे. इस परियोजना को आत्मनिर्भर भारत की दिशा में अहम कदम बताया गया है.
author: SunilG
content:
4 देशों की सीमा के पास असम में बनेंगे एंटी-ड्रोन सिस्टम और बंकर, 14 एकड़ में लगेगी 50 करोड़ की यूनिट
Last Updated:
असम में रक्षा उत्पादन की शुरुआत होने जा रही है. सीएम हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने रंगिया में यूनिट की नींव रखी. यहां ड्रोन और एंटी-ड्रोन सिस्टम बनाए जाएंगे. इस परियोजना को आत्मनिर्भर भारत की दिशा में अहम कदम बताया गया है.
रंगिया: असम के मुख्यमंत्री हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने बुधवार को रंगिया में एक निजी कंपनी की रक्षा उत्पादन इकाई की आधारशिला रखी. जहां ड्रोन विमान, ड्रोन-रोधी प्रणालियों और अन्य उपकरणों का निर्माण किया जाएगा. इसी के साथ राज्य ने रक्षा विनिर्माण के क्षेत्र में दस्तक भी दे दी.
सीएम हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने 4 देशों की सीमाओं के पास इस इकाई के रणनीतिक महत्व पर प्रकाश डाला. उन्होंने कहा कि कामरूप जिले में स्थित ‘स्पीड4डिफेंस सिस्टम्स प्राइवेट लिमिटेड’ की विनिर्माण इकाई एक संपूर्ण रक्षा विनिर्माण पाइपलाइन तैयार करने और ‘आत्मनिर्भर भारत’ के दृष्टिकोण को आगे बढ़ाने की दिशा में पहला कदम है.
असम में बनेंगे ड्रोन और एंटी-ड्रोन सिस्टम
हिमंत ने एक सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट में कहा, “असम के रक्षा पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र में पहला बड़ा निवेश आया है. हमारी एयरोस्पेस और रक्षा विनिर्माण नीति के तहत मैंने ‘स्पीड4डिफेंस’ की रक्षा विनिर्माण इकाई की आधारशिला रखी है. यहां हमारे सशस्त्र बलों के लिए ड्रोन विमान, ड्रोन-रोधी प्रणालियां और अन्य उपकरण बनाए जाएंगे.” उन्होंने कहा, “यह सुविधा 4 देशों की सीमाओं के करीब है. यह एक पूरी रक्षा विनिर्माण पाइपलाइन बनाने की हमारी कोशिशों के तहत पहला कदम है. इससे माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के आत्मनिर्भरभारत के दृष्टिकोण को बढ़ावा मिलेगा और हमारे सशस्त्र बलों की क्षमताएं बढ़ेंगी, खासकर इस रणनीतिक क्षेत्र में.”
50 करोड़ की लागत से बनेगी रक्षा यूनिट
इससे पहले सीएम हिमंत ने एक अन्य पोस्ट में देश के दुश्मनों को चेतावनी देते हुए कहा था, “देश के दुश्मन, ध्यान दें! असम रक्षा विनिर्माण के क्षेत्र में कदम रख रहा है, जिससे मोदी के ‘लुक ईस्ट’ और ‘आत्मनिर्भर भारत’ दृष्टिकोण को बढ़ावा मिलेगा तथा राज्य का विकास तेज होगा.” हिमंत ने कहा, “आज, कल-पुर्जे. कल, कुछ और भी बड़ा. ‘मेड इन असम’. लेबल याद रखिएगा.” मुख्यमंत्री कार्यालय (सीएमओ) ने बताया कि रंगिया में ‘स्पीड4 डिफेंस सिस्टम्स प्राइवेट लिमिटेड’ की रक्षा उत्पादन इकाई 14 एकड़ जमीन में स्थापित की जाएगी, जिसमें 50 करोड़ रुपये का शुरुआती निवेश किया जाएगा. उन्होंने कहा कि जनवरी 2028 तक उत्पादन शुरू करने के लक्ष्य के साथ यह इकाई ‘प्रीफैब्रिकेटेड’ ढांचे, भूमिगत बंकर, ड्रोन-रोधी प्रणालियों और ड्रोन विमानों का निर्माण करेगी.
Advertisement
500 तक मिलेंगे नौकरियों के अवसर
सीएमओ ने कहा, “इस परियोजना से शुरुआत में 150 प्रत्यक्ष नौकरियां पैदा होने की उम्मीद है, जो आगे चलकर 500 तक पहुंच सकती हैं. साथ ही, इससे स्थानीय एमएसएमई (सूक्ष्म, लघु एवं मध्यम उद्यम), आपूर्तिकर्ताओं और सहायक उद्योगों के लिए भी अवसर पैदा होंगे. आईआईटी गुवाहाटी के साथ मिलकर काम करने से असम में अनुसंधान, नवाचार और रक्षा प्रौद्योगिकी के विकास को और बढ़ावा मिलेगा.”
